title: Weird rule from Saints-Lions wasn't mentioned during AFC Championship
summary: That strange rule no one seemed to know about had a major impact on the Week 1 game between the Saints and Lions.
full_text: That strange rule no one seemed to know about had a major impact on the Week 1 game between the Saints and Lions. And there's a reason no one knew about it, beyond the fact that it apparently had not been applied in years, if ever. A very similar play happened during the AFC Championship. But the rulebook's get-out-of-backward-pass-free card was never mentioned. It started with 2:59 to go in the first half. The Broncos, leading the Patriots 7-0, had the ball at their own 33, facing third down and four. Denver quarterback Jarrett Stidham ( not Drew Brees ) got the snap in shotgun formation. Stidham dropped back, apparently looking to set up a screen pass. Patriots linebacker Christian Ellis gave chase. Stidham started his throwing motion. Before he got rid of the ball, Ellis made contact with Stidham. The pass, which was initially deemed to have gone forward, ultimately was determined to have been a backward pass, recovered by the Patriots. The main source of the controversy — and the post-game pool report — was the decision to rule the play dead upon recovery, taking New England's touchdown off the board. Said referee Alex Kemp after the game: "I initially ruled it as a forward pass, which was incorrect. I proceeded to go through the administration of an intentional grounding foul. The down judge and the umpire came and talked to me and provided more information. The down judge explained that he extended his right arm to signal that he had a backward pass and at that point we determined that New England had picked up the then backward pass. We awarded possession to New England with no advance, because at that point we are not allowed to permit an advance." There was no mention during or after the game about the possibility that Ellis's contact with Stidham after he started his throwing motion meant that any pass thrown was necessarily a forward pass, even if it went backward. That's the provision that saved the Lions from a defensive scoop and score by the Saints in Week 1. Now, it's possible that a frame-by-frame review of the play would have resulted in a ruling that Stidham started his throwing motion, ended it, and got hit by Ellis before starting it again. But it was close enough that the rule no one knew about should have been mentioned, and arguably fully explained, at some point in the process. Because it would have been a forward pass, even if it went backward, if the final ruling was that Ellis had hit Stidham after he began his throwing motion. And so, instead of the Patriots getting screwed by the ruling on the field of a forward pass, it's possible the Broncos got screwed by the failure to apply the rule that worked against the Saints on Sunday. But no one knew about it, because no one knew about the bizarre rule that turns a backward pass into a forward pass. Bottom line? If that rule had been mentioned, discussed, and/or applied in the AFC Championship, 48.6 million football fans would have become aware of it. And it wouldn't have been nearly as stunning to first learn about this rulebook quirk in Week 1 of the 2026 season.
author: Mike Florio

title: Lane Kiffin returns to Ole Miss, and draws a very profane chant
summary: Football's equivalent of the Joker returns to Gotham City on Saturday, when coach Lane Kiffin's LSU team plays at Ole Miss, the program he ditched during a playoff season.
full_text: '' Football's equivalent of the Joker returns to Gotham City on Saturday, when coach Lane Kiffin's LSU team plays at Ole Miss, the program he ditched during a playoff season. College GameDay is on the scene. And the " fuck Lane Kiffin! " chant came early. (A preview of it happened during SportsCenter , when Stanford Steve did a quick segment from the scene in Oxford.) There's not much ESPN can do about that. And, in this day and age, it's no longer as jarring as it used to be to hear "F" bombs on live TV. But it's a snapshot of the vitriol Kiffin will be facing all day and all night when he faces a school that had its best chances ever to chase a championship — and that he abandoned before the job was finished. And so the man at the center of the effort to remove the so-called "chaos" in college football will be dealing with a different kind of chaos until the game ends and Kiffin exits the playing field. Meanwhile, here's hoping someone explains to Kirk Herbstreit why Kiffin is being booed . Because even Kirk's dog understands that one.
author: Mike Florio

title: Hollywood Brown: I don't know if chances will come, I just have to work
summary: Wide receiver Hollywood Brown was active for the Eagles' Week 1 game against the Commanders, but he never got on the field during the 24-22 win.
full_text: Wide receiver Hollywood Brown was active for the Eagles' Week 1 game against the Commanders, but he never got on the field during the 24-22 win. Brown said this week that there were "no conversations" with coaches leading up to the game about his role. Head coach Nick Sirianni said on Monday that they "obviously want to get him into the football game because his speed is real," but that the rotations "just didn't work out that way" last Sunday. Brown said he is unsure if anything will change against the Titans this week, but that he'll work to be ready for any opportunity that might come his way. “That I don’t know,” Brown said, via Ryan Novozinsky of the Philadelphia Inquirer . “I just got to come to work . If it do, it do. If it don’t, it don’t.” Brown was added to Friday's injury report as a full participant with a hamstring injury, but has no injury designation for Sunday. Whether that means he'll be on the field remains up in the air.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mike Sainristil says he'll stay positive after Dan Quinn called his play "not acceptable"
summary: Sainristil's coverage breakdown gave up a touchdown pass against the Eagles, and Quinn called him out afterward.
full_text: When discussing the Week 1 loss to the Eagles, Commanders head coach Dan Quinn made a specific point of saying that cornerback Mike Sainristil didn't play well enough. Sainristil says he's staying positive. Quinn doesn't often call out players by name, but during his Monday press conference after Sunday's loss, he named Sainristil, whose coverage breakdown gave up an Eagles touchdown pass, as one of the players who needed to correct the way he played. "We’ve definitely identified a few things that, ‘Hey, man, these are the things that we have to get corrected,’" Quinn said. "Mike’s a very good competitor. I’m certain that we will, but to have that type of play and just not have the right focus at the right time, completely not acceptable.” Sainristil told reporters in the Commanders' locker room this week that he won't let that get him down. "People sometimes focus on, What did I do bad? But you don't play a game and do all bad things. You have to focus on the good things, keep the good things good," Sainristil said. "I'm not somebody that sits there, whether I played good, whether I played bad, a few good plays or a few bad plays, I'm not going to sit there sulking." Sainristil said he'll always try to get better, whether his coach calls him out or not. "For me, it's just focusing on, What can I do better, every single day?" Sainristil said. "Whether I played good or whether I played bad."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Potential victims of 49ers imposter Daejon Love now exceed 60
summary: Daejon Love's scam worked incredibly well.
full_text: Daejon Love's scam worked incredibly well. Until it didn't. Via Kalyn Kahler of ESPN, the FBI has identified 35 more potential victims of the fraud allegedly perpetrated by Love and Taylor Chan. The total number of possible victims now exceeds 60. "We were surprised how many people were victimized in such a short period of time and then to have that many more come forward," FBI agent Doug Olson said at a news conference, per Kahler. "It's a large volume for just a couple of subjects. Our concern is that this fraud could be replicated by other individuals that are out there victimizing other people in similar schemes." The FBI believes even more potential victims could be identified. "We don't want anyone to be fearful of coming forward," Olson said, "certainly not for fear of embarrassment or anything like that, because we want to help them and we want to make sure that this doesn't happen to anybody else." Love, 35, and Chan, 18, allegedly stole more than $1.3 million, with Love posing as a 49ers player. Chan posed as Love's financial adviser. "The victims in this case were targeted precisely because they were trusting, responsible people who they believed were building genuine relationships and legitimate financial futures," Olson said. "They were deliberately manipulated through an extremely sophisticated scheme that blended fake personas, fabricated investment accounts, staged video calls and AI-reinforced false identities." A 49ers source told Kahler that the team was not aware of Love, and that it had not received any reports about him before learning about the situation from the FBI in August. And while most realize that anything that seems too good to be true probably is, our nature can make us susceptible to getting scammed. Hopefully, the potential victims won't fear ridicule for seeking justice — that alone could cause them and other victims of other scams to say nothing for fear of being embarrassed. They're the victims. They deserve no scrutiny for being on the wrong side of a criminal enterprise that was very successful. Until, again, it wasn't.
author: Mike Florio

title: DeForest Buckner: Colts didn't play up to our standards, whatsoever
summary: The Colts' defense gave up 304 passing yards and 202 rushing yards in their Week 1 loss to the Ravens, and Colts defensive tackle DeForest Buckner says it was unacceptable.
full_text: The Colts' defense gave up 304 passing yards and 202 rushing yards in their Week 1 loss to the Ravens, and Colts defensive tackle DeForest Buckner says it was unacceptable. "We didn't play to our standard at all whatsoever, and we know we're better than that and what we put on tape," Buckner said, via JJ Stankevitz of Colts.com. "But obviously, you're only as good as your last game and that's what we put on tape. So we got to continue to prove to ourselves and prove to everybody else that we're a better defense than that." The Colts are 6.5-point underdogs at Kansas City on Sunday night, and they know they need to play a lot better, or else Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker can put up the same kinds of numbers that Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry did. Colts head coach Shane Steichen said he's emphasizing not letting Walker break tackles. "The big thing is tackling, right? That's the biggest thing," Steichen said. "You got to get this guy on the ground. He runs low, he runs hard, and then our run fits have got to be great." If the Colts' defense again doesn't play up to its standards, it could be an ugly night against the Chiefs.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Jerry Jones: The Giants were better than we thought they were
summary: Jones seemingly tries to temper expectations for the 2026 Cowboys.
full_text: '' The latest Cowboys' season of high expectations started with a thud on Sunday night, when Dallas lost to the Giants in the regular-season opener. In a Friday appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, Cowboys owner and G.M. Jerry Jones acknowledged that the outcome had something to do with the opponent. "They just did a good job all over," Jones said regarding the Giants. "And I will tell you, they were better than we thought they were . I'm anxious to see how New York continues to play, but I really — combination of things. We didn't play as well as we should play and can play, but they played better than I thought they could." Was it also a product of the Cowboys not being as good as Jones had thought they would be? "Of course," Jones said. "Well, and to say it that way, I'd rather say it more positively. We're not at the level that we thought we would be. "I can give you a lot of reasons, logical reasons. We're dealing with a conceptually new coaching staff, dealing with a 'new' to a lot of people out there. The defensive scheme. And then you're dealing with people who are fresh into that scheme. Now, you got some really veteran players out there. But still, they're changing up some of the things that they're doing. Are they capable of doing what we're asking? Absolutely they are. "But the bottom line is that the last time, frankly, the last time that, from my perspective, that we had as many changes on defense, we had as many changes with the coaching staff, had as much change with the personnel, and had as much change with the team was the first year Jimmy Johnson was our coach, and we won one football game. "Now, things have changed, and you can come in with less experience than you could in those days. But having said that, it's a challenge now to put it together and get it ready to go. We didn't play well last week. I said — what I meant to say was, New York had really more to do with it than I thought they would. Than I thought they would. And so that's a factor. But Washington could have a lot to do with it here Sunday, too, so we've got to be ready to step up the level of play. There's no question." It's a sensible explanation. But it cuts against the vibe that had been created before the season, when season tickets were being renewed and hype was being generated and fans were being persuaded that things would be different this year. What should the real expectations be? With Jerry suggesting that the Cowboys undergone an overhaul they haven't experienced since the year Jones bought the team, they perhaps should be a lot lower than they were a week ago.
author: Mike Florio

title: Dolphins DE Chop Robinson in concussion protocol, out for Sunday
summary: Dolphins defensive end Chop Robinson will not play Sunday against the 49ers.
full_text: Dolphins defensive end Chop Robinson will not play Sunday against the 49ers. Robinson was diagnosed with a concussion during Wednesday's practice, and he remains in concussion protocol. The Dolphins remained out West, practicing in Napa, California, after last week's season opener against the Raiders. Robinson was limited on Wednesday's injury report and did not practice Thursday. The Dolphins will lean on Josh Uche, Clelin Ferrell, Rob Beal Jr. and Malik Herring to get after Brock Purdy, Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said, via Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN. " It’s all of the above . We might do some other things to help out," Hafley said. "But I have confidence in those guys. . . . They've done a good job at practice this week, and it'll be the next man up." Robinson, drafted 21st overall in 2024, has 10 sacks in his career and had three pressures in Week 1. Robinson had two concussions in 2025, which kept him sidelined for two games. Inside linebacker Ronnie Harrison Jr. (hamstring) also won't play. Long snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder) is questionable after three consecutive limited practices.
author: Charean Williams

title: Kirk Herbstreit offers flimsy defense for ESPN's decision to interview Ted Cruz on College GameDay
summary: ESPN committed a bizarre broadcasting faux pas last Saturday, by giving Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) an extended platform on College GameDay to push for the passage of the so-called Protect College Sports Act (which also could be called the Screw College Players Act or, as Simms suggested, Protect the ESPN and SEC Contract Act).
full_text: '' ESPN committed a bizarre broadcasting faux pas last Saturday, by giving Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) an extended platform on College GameDay to push for the passage of the so-called Protect College Sports Act (which also could be called the Screw College Players Act or, as Simms suggested, Protect the ESPN and SEC Contract Act ). The story has resonated throughout the week, and it looms over Saturday's episode of College GameDay in Oxford, Mississippi. Kirk Herbstreit, one of the College GameDay analysts, addressed the situation in comments with reporters on Friday. " I was first really impressed ," Herbstreit said, via Mississippi Today . "I've never seen a guy booed that long and be able to just power through that. You know, I don't know if he could hear what I could hear, but it was pretty — I think he was booed pretty much the entire time he spoke. "I don't really get into politics. It's just not — I'm kind of an independent guy, right down the middle of the fairway. I'm for America, so whoever helps us as a country, I'm for. Whether it's somebody on the left, somebody on the right, so I don't really follow it. I don't know anything about his political views. I don't know what he's for or against. I care about football, my family, and my faith, and my country. Those are things I love. "And so, I don't really pick sides, and I was surprised. I didn't know what his deal was, so him being booed, I asked people, 'Like, what's going on here?' And we had him on because they were gonna be voting this week, and maybe he could give us some insight to what's going on. That was really it. So we're not picking sides in any way at all. We just want to see the chaos that's surrounding this sport kind of be reeled in, and if this will help us get to that, then great. Now, the fact that the guy that sits right next to me, Nick Saban, was heavily involved in putting this act together, this guy loves college football more than anybody I've ever met. And so if he's happy about what this could do, then I follow his lead. But yeah, that was surprising. But, again, I don't really follow it, so I didn't really understand it." There's a lot to unpack there. I'll keep it simple. Herbstreit is either flat-out lying or he's ridiculously naive. How can anyone say "I love my country" while being completely detached from the issues that shape its present and future? How can any American adult not know what it means to be a Republican or to be a Democrat, and how those labels have become so inherently polarizing and conducive to negative reactions? Beyond Herbstreit's claim that he's clueless as to why someone like Ted Cruz would be booed, Herbstreit's position that he's "right down the middle of the fairway" and that ESPN isn't "picking sides" on the issue at hand can't be reconciled with his viewpoint that the "chaos" needs to "kind of be reeled in" and that he supports anything Nick Saban recommends on the matter because Saban "loves college football more than anybody I've met." It's entirely possible to love college football and to want to limit player pay and mobility. Which is precisely what the Screw College Players Act will do. The word "chaos" is a matter of perspective. From the players' perspective, it's not chaotic; they have real rights and power. From the perspective of those who don't like the fact that the rabbit has the gun, it's definitely chaotic. Because the rabbit has the gun . The best news is that folks seem to be figuring out what's going on here. The powers-that-be don't like the fact that they've lost some of their power, given the implosion of a system that was fueled by antitrust violations that collectively prevented players from getting paid. In the aftermath of the reckoning, those who don't like the new reality are shedding crocodile tears and screaming "the sky is falling" to anyone who may be able to help them implement a system that limits the new rights the players enjoy. It's a grift. It's a scam. Herbstreit has made himself part of that scam while pretending to be neutral — and not even his dog will shield him from the criticism he now deserves.
author: Mike Florio

title: Azeez Al-Shaair on publicizing Hind Rajab's story: Most of you might not even know who she was
summary: The NFL fined Texans linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair $11,941 for writing the name "Hind Rajab" on his eye-black strips during a Week 1 game against the Bills.
full_text: The NFL fined Texans linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair $11,941 for writing the name "Hind Rajab" on his eye-black strips during a Week 1 game against the Bills. On Friday, Al-Shaair explained his decision to publicize the name of the five-year-old Palestinian girl who was killed, along with six family members, by Israeli forces in 2024. "I think everybody knows what it's about," Al-Shaair said, via D.J. Bien-Aime of ESPN. "I think that was the point. Because before that, probably most of you guys might not even know who she was . That's kind of the point. "There a lot that goes on in the world, not just overseas, right here in our own country. . . . This past Tuesday, a friend of mine, literally just sitting there crying in front of me on the phone, come to find out her cousin, who's been here since he was five years old, got detained on the way to a concert and is being deported. Mind you, he has no family, no nothing over there. And that was my first interaction, my first experience, with somebody that I personally know. . . . "There's a lot of issues that I speak on, that's really just to shed a light, because a lot of people don't care nothing about it. . . . We're blessed to be able to have the comforts of, you know, living in the United States and not having to worry about certain things, but there's issues here and all over the world that, you know, when you talk about even what happened with Hind Rajab and her family, those are taxpaying dollars that we're — as Americans — are paying, that are being used to bomb innocent men, women, and children. So that's really what that was about." Dallas Mavericks star Kyrie Irving offered to pay the fine. Al-Shaair said that he and Irving "align on the cause, which is humanity; we both care about humanity ." "Regardless of skin color, race, anything like that," Al-Shaair said. "That's what I think, more than anything, when it comes to me and him, that we align on, and just not being afraid to do that. . . . We don't have to have all the answers to everything to know that an innocent man, an innocent woman, an innocent child losing their life is not right. Like, I don't need anybody to gaslight me into saying that, 'Well, you gotta ask. . . .' I just know that's not right, whether they're here in America or somewhere halfway across the world." It remains to be seen whether Al-Shaair will have a similar message during Sunday's game against the Bengals, and whether the league will threaten to keep him from playing if he does.
author: Mike Florio

title: Rams WR Puka Nacua misses practice with a hip injury
summary: The Rams added wide receiver Puka Nacua to the injury report on Friday.
full_text: The Rams added wide receiver Puka Nacua to the injury report on Friday. Nacua missed practice with a hip injury. It is unclear whether it is related to the psoas soreness that forced him to leave the joint practice with the Cowboys early on Aug. 13. The psoas is a deep core muscle and a primary hip flexor. Nacua was not listed on the injury report for Week 1. Nacua’s backup, Jordan Whittington, also missed Friday's practice. Whittington has a quad injury. Safety Kamren Kinchens (hamstring) was the other player who didn't practice. Safety Kam Curl (ankle), inside linebacker Omar Speights (hip) and inside linebacker Nate Landman (shoulder) were limited. Wide receiver Davante Adams returned to practice Friday after a rest day on Thursday.
author: Charean Williams

title: 49ers K Eddy Piñeiro is questionable with an illness
summary: 49ers kicker Eddy Piñeiro is questionable to play against the Dolphins because of an illness. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said the team will sign a kicker to the practice squad on Saturday as insurance in case Piñeiro can't play.
full_text: 49ers kicker Eddy Piñeiro is questionable to play against the Dolphins because of an illness. 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said the team will sign a kicker to the practice squad on Saturday as insurance in case Piñeiro can't play. "There's two guys we're deciding on," Shanahan said, "but not sure which one." Running back Kaelon Black (groin) is also questionable. When asked what level of optimism Shanahan has about Black's availability, he said, "a questionable amount of optimism." The 49ers ruled out wide receiver De'Shaun Stribling (ankle).
author: Charean Williams

title: Aaron Donald plans to play on Monday night
summary: The return of the three-time Defensive Player of the Year will come against the Giants.
full_text: ''' Aaron Donald is ready to return. Donald, the Rams defensive tackle who hasn't played since announcing his retirement after the 2023 season, said today that he expects to play against the Giants on Monday Night Football. "That's the plan," Donald said when asked if he is playing. Donald, who did not make the trip to Australia for the Rams' Week 1 loss to the 49ers, said he has been feeling like his old self while practicing this week. "Have another practice tomorrow, and then we'll see, but feeling good," Donald said. The 35-year-old Donald was the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year in 2017, 2018 and 2020. He retired after 10 seasons with the Rams but started considering a comeback after the Rams traded for the NFL's reigning Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett. Donald and Garrett on the same defensive line would be a ferocious combination, but we'll have to wait at least four more weeks to see that, as Garrett went on injured reserve after Week 1. Instead, the focus on Monday night will be on Donald, and seeing whether he still looks like the Aaron Donald of old.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Deshaun Watson could lose seventh straight start on Sunday
summary: It's been a long week for Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson.
full_text: It's been a long week for Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson. And it's still not over. Against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Watson could post his seventh straight loss as a starter. That would be the longest streak for any Browns quarterback since DeShone Kizer in 2017, when a 15-game losing streak cemented an 0-16 season. Which opened the door to drafting Baker Mayfield the following April. Watson drew fresh criticism after the Week 1 34-10 loss to the Jaguars by claiming that the "media has this expectation that I’m supposed to throw [for] 400 yards and five touchdowns every week ," even though he hasn't done that once since Week 5 of the 2019 season. There are even more depressing statistics than that. As Anthony Lima of 92.3 The Fan observed on Friday morning, Bills quarterback Josh Allen has nine total touchdowns in five days. Watson has eight total touchdowns in 1,041 days . And, yes, the Browns could have drafted Allen instead of Mayfield. But don't feel too bad about that, Browns fans; the organization likely would have ruined and/or moved on from Allen by now, too. After Sunday — barring a win and, perhaps, 400 yards and five touchdowns — the Browns will have to move on from Watson or risk a full-blown riot for the Week 3 home opener against Carolina.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Steelers have received no serious trade inquiries about Joey Porter Jr.
summary: As the contract impasse lingers between the Steelers and cornerback Joey Porter Jr., none of the other 31 teams has made a move to try to get him.
full_text: As the contract impasse lingers between the Steelers and cornerback Joey Porter Jr., none of the other 31 teams has made a move to try to get him. A lengthy article from ESPN exploring the dynamics of the situation contains this key line: "[T]he team has neither made nor received any serious inquiries about the cornerback." Given that it's been obvious for weeks that Porter and the Steelers aren't seeing eye-to-eye on a potential extension, interested teams have had every reason to spark a dialogue. The absence of any such effort suggests that no one is willing to pay Porter what he wants and to give the Steelers what they'd need. ESPN also points to two primary issues with the negotiations. One, the two sides have a "significant difference" about Porter's value. Two, Porter wants the team to break from its habit of fully guaranteeing compensation beyond the first year of the contract. The Steelers historically had done that only for high-end quarterbacks, like Ben Roethlisberger. As noted by ESPN, they broke from that precedent with linebacker T.J. Watt, twice. As not noted by ESPN, they also deviated from this habit when trading for, and signing, receiver DK Metcalf in 2025; he got $60 million fully guaranteed over the first two years. While cash-flow concerns possibly will keep the Steelers from expanding the practice to a player who won't be paid at the top of the market, the bigger issue seems to be the value of the contract. Either way, the team's other internal rule regarding not doing new deals after the season begins has put everyone in an awkward spot. As noted by Steelers Depot , the team made an exception in 1995 for safety Darren Perry. At the time, the explanation from Ed Bouchette of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette was that "if they were close to a deal that would carry it over to the early part of the season." In this case, they could try something like "we'll do a deal before the first game of the season in which the player plays." Semantics don't matter, since no deal is close. And it's possible Porter will continue to not play until the Steelers trade him for whatever they can get. As an unnamed "source with knowledge of the situation" told ESPN, "I don't know if he ever puts on a Steelers uniform again." For now, he won't put on a uniform for the second game of the 2026 season. With no end to the standoff in sight, it could continue on a weekly basis until he's traded or the Steelers decide to play hardball by fining him for refusing to play.
author: Mike Florio

title: Giants place Paulson Adebo on IR, sign Nikko Reed from Chargers
summary: One of the Giants’ defensive backs will be sidelined for at least the next four weeks.
full_text: '' One of the Giants’ defensive backs will be sidelined for at least the next four weeks. New York placed cornerback Paulson Adebo on injured reserve on Friday, the team announced. Adebo played 10 defensive snaps and eight special teams snaps in Sunday’s victory over the Cowboys. He did not practice on Thursday, listed with a knee injury. As a corresponding move, the Giants signed Nikko Reed to the 53-man roster off of the Chargers’ practice squad. Reed appeared in five games for Los Angeles last season as an undrafted rookie, mainly playing special teams. The Giants will play the Rams on Monday night to wrap up Week 2.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Mike Macdonald: Not sure when Sam Darnold will be back, but I'm optimistic
summary: The Seahawks ruled quarterback Sam Darnold out for Week 2 a couple of days ago, but his health was still a topic for head coach Mike Macdonald during Friday's press conference.
full_text: '' The Seahawks ruled quarterback Sam Darnold out for Week 2 a couple of days ago, but his health was still a topic for head coach Mike Macdonald during Friday's press conference. Darnold has not practiced since injuring his glute in the team's season-opening win over the Patriots and Macdonald didn't provide much sense about when that would change. “He’s on his way back," Macdonald said. "Is it next week? Is it the week after, the week after that? I’m not sure. I’m optimistic, put it that way.” Drew Lock will start against the Cardinals with Jalen Milroe serving as their backup. Safety Ty Okada (hamstring) will also mean the game. Safety Nick Emmanwori (hip, ankle) and guard Anthony Bradford (knee, hip) are both listed as questionable.
author: Josh Alper

title: Chargers list Ladd McConkey as questionable
summary: The Chargers had wide receiver Ladd McConkey on the practice field Friday for the first time this week, but his status for Sunday's game against the Raiders remains up in the air.
full_text: '' The Chargers had wide receiver Ladd McConkey on the practice field Friday for the first time this week, but his status for Sunday's game against the Raiders remains up in the air. McConkey left Week 1 with a rib injury that kept him out of practice on Wednesday and Thursday. The Chargers listed him as questionable to play as they try to rebound from their season-opening loss to the Cardinals. Defensive back Deane Leonard (abdomen) was a limited participant in practice all week and he joins McConkey in the questionable category. Defensive back Elijah Molden (hamstring) and offensive lineman Trey Pipkins (knee) were ruled out after missing practice all week.
author: Josh Alper

title: Chris Jones, Mansoor Delane listed as questionable to face Colts
summary: The Chiefs have a couple of question marks on the defensive side of the ball heading into Sunday's game against the Colts.
full_text: The Chiefs have a couple of question marks on the defensive side of the ball heading into Sunday's game against the Colts. Defensive tackle Chris Jones and cornerback Mansoor Delane are both tagged as questionable for the home matchup. Jones was limited in practice all week with a calf injury. Delane hurt his shoulder in Monday night's win over the Broncos and moved up to full practice participation on Thursday, but he dropped back down to limited work to close out the week. Left tackle Josh Simmons (back) and defensive back Chamarri Conner (knee) were both ruled out for the second straight week. Rookie Kahlil Benson is set to start in place of Simmons again this weekend.
author: Josh Alper

title: Nico Collins one of four Texans players ruled out for Week 2
summary: If the Texans are going to beat the Bengals on Sunday, they'll have to do it without a few key players.
full_text: If the Texans are going to beat the Bengals on Sunday, they'll have to do it without a few key players. Houston has ruled out receiver Nico Collins, starting guard Ed Ingram, edge rusher Jadeveon Clowney, and linebacker Jake Hummel for Week 2. Collins suffered a hamstring injury during practice on Wednesday and did not participate on Thursday or Friday. Collins — Houston’s top receiver — caught seven passes for 75 yards with a touchdown in last week’s loss to the Bills. Ingram was limited with a groin injury on Thursday before he did not participate on Friday. Clowney (knee) and Hummel (groin) also did not practice on Friday. Offensive tackle Trent Brown (hand/wrist) and linebacker Wade Woodaz (thumb) were both full participants on Friday. Neither Brown nor Woodaz has a game status, with both expected to play. Houston will be at home on Sunday to face Cincinnati at Reliant Stadium at 1 p.m. ET.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Bengals officially list Joe Burrow as questionable
summary: Burrow said earlier this week that he will be playing against the Texans on Sunday.
full_text: '' Joe Burrow said it was " ridiculous " to think he'd miss Sunday's game against the Texans after dealing with back tightness this week, but the team has left some wiggle room with their final injury report of the week. The quarterback is listed as questionable for the game in Houston. Burrow moved up to full practice participation on Friday and head coach Zac Taylor said he " feels good ," but official word on his status is going to have to wait until closer to Sunday afternoon's kickoff. Defensive tackle B.J. Hill is also listed as questionable. He's dealing with an Achilles injury. Defensive end Shemar Stewart is off the injury report after missing Week 1 with a knee injury and is set for his 2026 debut.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jonathan Greenard ruled out for Eagles-Titans
summary: The Eagles will once again be without edge rusher Jonathan Greenard for Sunday’s matchup against the Titans.
full_text: The Eagles will once again be without edge rusher Jonathan Greenard for Sunday’s matchup against the Titans. Philadelphia has ruled Greenard out with his pectoral injury. He was a limited participant in practice all week, but is not yet ready to play. Additionally, safety Andrew Mukuba (knee) is questionable. He was limited on Friday after he did not participate on Thursday. While Marquise Brown (hamstring) and Elijah Moore (neck) were both added to the injury report on Friday, they were both full participants and are expected to play. Defensive tackle Jalen Carter (wrist) and defensive back Cooper DeJean (calf/abdomen) are also expected to play with no game status.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Steeler rule Joey Porter Jr. out again this week
summary: Any hopes that cornerback Joey Porter Jr. would be in the Steelers' lineup for Sunday's game against the Patriots came to an end on Friday afternoon.
full_text: Any hopes that cornerback Joey Porter Jr. would be in the Steelers' lineup for Sunday's game against the Patriots came to an end on Friday afternoon. Porter has been ruled out for the second straight week. Head coach Mike McCarthy said on Thursday that the team expected Porter to do more work in practice, but he wound up leaving the session early and was limited again on Friday. Porter is listed with both a back injury and conditioning as reasons why he won't play. He did not practice at all during training camp because he was on the physically unable to perform list and his ongoing contract impasse with the team has led to reports that he could be traded at some point during the season. Wide receiver Michael Pittman (foot) missed his second straight practice, but the door is open for him to play after getting a questionable tag on the final report. Left tackle Troy Fautanu (ankle) was a limited participant and joins Pittman in the questionable category.
author: Josh Alper

title: Will McDonald questionable for Jets, Minkah Fitzpatrick ruled out
summary: The Jets will be missing a handful of players as they try to open a season with a 2-0 record for the first time since 2015, but they hope linebacker Will McDonald won't be one of them.
full_text: The Jets will be missing a handful of players as they try to open a season with a 2-0 record for the first time since 2015, but they hope linebacker Will McDonald won't be one of them. McDonald is listed as questionable to face the Packers due to an ankle injury. McDonald was added to the injury report on Thursday and he was listed as a limited practice participant for the second straight day on Friday. The Jets called safety Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin) week-to-week after his Week 1 injury, which foreshadowed Friday's news that he's been officially ruled out. They'll also be without wide receiver Omar Cooper (ankle), linebacker Joseph Ossai (foot), and running back Kene Nwangwu (back). Second-round pick D'Angelo Ponds is set to make his NFL debut. The cornerback has no injury designation after missing Week 1 with a calf injury.
author: Josh Alper

title: Joe Brady: If DJ Moore can be out there for Week 3, he’ll be out there
summary: After defeating the Lions on Thursday night, the Bills will have a long weekend to rest up and heal before hosting the Chargers in Week 3.
full_text: After defeating the Lions on Thursday night, the Bills will have a long weekend to rest up and heal before hosting the Chargers in Week 3. That's good news for a club that has a pair of key players banged up. Head coach Joe Brady did not have much of an update on receiver DJ Moore — who exited the game with a shoulder injury — or Ed Oliver, who was inactive after injuring his hip during pregame warm-ups. "We’re still obviously going through [it]," Brady said. "One of the perks of the Thursday night game, not a lot of perks, but one of the perks of it is you do get that long weekend, and guys will recover. So we don’t practice again until next Wednesday. No different than any other — we’ll see how these guys are going to recover and how their body will take it. As you guys who have been around DJ or know DJ’s past, he’s as tough as they come. So, if he can be out there, he’ll be out there . "[Oliver is] another guy, we’ll just see how he’s progressing," Brady added. "The guys that are getting tests and MRIs and all that, they’re getting that now." Additionally, Brady noted that running back Ty Johnson and defensive lineman T.J. Sanders were close to playing against the Lions. With the extended break before Week 3, both may be able to be back for Buffalo’s next game. The Bills will host the Chargers on Sunday, Sept. 27.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Ravens list Zay Flowers as doubtful; Trey Hendrickson and Ronnie Stanley are questionable
summary: Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers was back on the practice field Friday, but he's unlikely to be back in their lineup for Sunday's game against the Saints.
full_text: '' Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers was back on the practice field Friday, but he's unlikely to be back in their lineup for Sunday's game against the Saints. Flowers, who is dealing with a hamstring injury, was listed as a limited participant in practice and reports from the open portion of the workout said he was on the very limited end of the spectrum. He's listed as doubtful to play this weekend, but the outlook is better for three other players who returned to action to close out the week. Defensive end Trey Hendrickson (finger), left tackle Ronnie Stanley (toe), and left guard John Simpson (groin) were all listed as questionable after getting in limited practice work. Linebacker Teddye Buchanan (knee), defensive lineman Nnamdi Madubuike (neck), and cornerback T.J. Tampa (knee) have all been ruled out.
author: Josh Alper

title: D'Andre Swift, Kyle Monangai good to go for Bears
summary: The Bears had their top two running backs on the injury report this week, but neither one of them is at risk of missing Sunday's game against the Vikings.
full_text: '' The Bears had their top two running backs on the injury report this week, but neither one of them is at risk of missing Sunday's game against the Vikings. Neither D'Andre Swift nor Kyle Monangai has an injury designation for Week 2. Swift was limited with ankle and knee issues the last two days while Monangai has a hamstring injury, but they were both full participants in practice on Friday. The full participation and lack of injury designations gives them two things in common with the rest of the team's active roster. Everyone on the team fully practiced and no one will be carrying a designation into Sunday. That should mean safety Xavier Woods makes his 2026 debut, but it remains to be seen when offensive tackle Ozzy Trapilo will make his return from a torn patellar tendon.
author: Josh Alper

title: Raiders call Brock Bowers doubtful to play in Week 2
summary: Tight end Brock Bowers was back at practice for the Raiders on Friday, but it looks like he is going to miss another game.
full_text: '' Tight end Brock Bowers was back at practice for the Raiders on Friday, but it looks like he is going to miss another game. Head coach Klint Kubiak said at his Friday press conference that Bowers will be listed as doubtful to play against the Chargers this Sunday. Kubiak said that the plan is for Bowers to work out ahead of the game before a final decision is made, but the listing makes it unlikely that will result in a green light to play. Assuming he is ruled out, Michael Mayer will be the team's top tight end for the second straight week. Cornerback Darien Porter (foot) has been ruled out for the Raiders this weekend.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bills are third team ever to start 2-0 while giving up more than 30 points in both games
summary: The Bills have started the season with two wins over two teams that entered the season as favorites to win their divisions.
full_text: ' The Bills have started the season with two wins over two teams that entered the season as favorites to win their divisions. They have to be pleased with their 36-31 win over the Texans and their 41-31 win over the Lions. At least, they have to be pleased with scoring 36 and 41 points in their first two games. Giving up 31 points in each game is not so pleasing. In fact, the Bills are just the third team ever to start the season 2-0 despite giving up more than 30 points in both games. Previously, the 2000 Rams won their first two games by scores of 41-36 and 37-34, and the 1991 Bills won their first two games 35-31 and 52-34. Via Josh Dubow of the Associated Press, only four teams in NFL history have given up 62 or more points while starting 2-0: This year's Bills, those 2000 Rams and 1991 Bills, and the 2018 Chiefs. The good news for the Bills is, the three previous teams to give up 62 or more points while starting 2-0 made the playoffs. The bad news is, all three of them lost in the postseason — and all three of them gave up more than 30 points in those losses. The Bills' offense looks great through two weeks of the season. It remains to be seen whether they can win a championship with this defense.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Rams sign S Tanner Ingle to 53-man roster
summary: The Rams have made a couple of roster moves on Friday.
full_text: '' The Rams have made a couple of roster moves on Friday. Los Angeles announced the club has signed Tanner Ingle to the 53-man roster off of the club’s practice squad. Ingle played eight special teams snaps in Los Angeles’ season-opening loss to San Francisco. The Rams could use some depth at safety with Kam Kinchens dealing with a hamstring injury and Kam Curl dealing with an ankle issue. As a corresponding move, the club has signed defensive tackle Jaxson Moi to the practice squad. The Rams had an open roster spot after placing edge rusher Myles Garrett on injured reserve on Thursday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: No, Pack, no: Missing Micah Parsons, Green Bay ties grim NFL record -- and may currently be NFC's worst team
summary: Parsons' absence can't be the only excuse, which is why Matt LaFleur should be on a warming seat
full_text:
Apparently nobody ever told the Packers the famous sales mantra and acronym 'ABC' from the 1992 film Glengarry Glen Ross. 'ABC' stands for 'Always be closing."
Green Bay hasn't been able to do anything of the sort since Micah Parsons' tore his ACL in Week 15 in Denver last season. The Packers have lost six straight games since their superstar edge rusher went down, their longest losing streak since the pre-Brett Favre era in the early 1990s.
The collapses without Parsons have reached historic levels of futility, including the 17-point loss in Week 1 in Minnesota after leading by 12 points in the second half. Here's a summary of those four collapses:
Their four straight losses in games when leading by at least two scores in the second half is tied with the 2000 Chargers for the longest such losing streak in NFL history. By the way, those Chargers went 1-15 and Ryan Leaf was their quarterback for three of those four blown leads. It was his last season with San Diego.
The Packers have their sights set on Super Bowls, yet they find themselves in the company of one of the worst teams (and draft busts) in NFL history.
Green Bay had been 63-4 in their previous 67 games when up multiple scores in the second half under Matt LaFleur. Now, they've dropped four in a row, including two straight (both to Chicago) with a double-digit lead in the last five minutes!
Oh, but it gets worse. The Packers have been outscored 90-15 in the fourth quarter and OT during this six-game losing streak since Parsons' injury. That is one of the five worst score differentials (-75) in a six-game span in the fourth quarter and overtime in NFL history.
Packers in fourth quarter/OT during six-game losing streak
They haven't outscored a single team in the fourth quarter since Parsons went down and they were outscored 22-0 in the fourth quarter this past Sunday, their worst final period in 45 years.
The Packers haven't been able to stop anyone without their closer. They've allowed 11 touchdowns and four field goals on 18 drives in the fourth quarter and OT during this streak. That's five points per drive! Look away Packers fans!
This is downright embarrassing and an argument could be made right now, today, the Packers have the worst team in the NFC. I'm not talking about projections, but right now. It's not the Cardinals, who just upset the Chargers. The Giants don't look like a punching bag anymore. It could be an NFC South team, but there's also a case it's the Packers. Thanks to those embarrassing defeats, they have the longest active losing streak in the conference right now.
So what does it all really mean?
LaFleur was extended last offseason following the shocking collapse in the playoffs in Chicago. Well, Green Bay might want to reconsider. It would be foolish to chalk up all the blown leads to Parsons' absence. After all, they also blew a big lead to the Browns of all teams last year. It was their first loss since 1967 when up 10+ points in the final four minutes of regulation. That wasn't just a blip in the radar, it was the start of a startling trend that ultimately the head coach is responsible for.
LaFleur gets lauded as an offensive genius, so explain how the Packers are 0-for-8 converting potential game-tying and go-ahead drive chances in the fourth quarter and overtime during their losing streak. That has nothing to do with Micah Parsons. They've had eight chances to drive the ball down the field to tie or take the lead and they've failed every time.
If Green Bay somehow falls apart on Sunday vs. the Jets, LaFleur's seat will be as hot as it's ever been.
Love can't escape responsibility here, either. The Packers have one touchdown in the fourth quarter and overtime of this losing streak. Love has been off target on nearly one quarter of his passes in those situations, a figure that would easily be dead last in the NFL over an entire year.
Sometimes the best way to close games is to have someone you can go to in the crunch. The Packers haven't had a No. 1 WR since Davante Adams was traded in 2022 and clearly the lack of a top option hurts in these spots. Christian Watson looks like a breakout candidate after his Week 1 performance but he was nowhere to be found in the fourth quarter on Sunday. Jayden Reed and first-round pick Matthew Golden are also candidates.
Love gets a little bit of a pass because the Vikings rained blitz after blitz down on him in Week 1 (and let's not forget he had over 300 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions in the playoff loss in Chicago), but if he wants to keep the title of a top 10 quarterback he needs to be the closer. Or perhaps, the stopper, like an ace in baseball who can be counted on to win crucial games and stop losing streaks.
We already knew Micah Parsons was one of the best defensive players in the game, but this shows he might be the most valuable. The Packers have seven sacks during their six-game losing streak. Their sack rate (4.2%) with Parsons off the field since the start of last year amounts to the second-worst in the league. Only the 49ers (whose pass rush was historically bad last year) are worse.
The Cowboys have had the worst defense in the NFL since trading Parsons and now the Packers have had one of the worst defensive units since he got injured. They have the second-worst defensive rating (as measured by EPA) since his injury. Only the Cowboys, of course, are worse in that time. In other words, Micah Parsons' stock has never been higher.
They will have to navigate at least another few weeks without Parsons as he's on the PUP list, meaning he's out for the first four games. Who knows what chaos will ensue before he comes back.
Another blown lead and some heads are going to start rolling in Green Bay.
author: Douglas Clawson

title: NFL Week 2 injury report: Joe Burrow questionable, Brock Bowers doubtful, Kyler Murray out
summary: Joe Burrow appears to be trending toward playing, but Brock Bowers and Zay Flowers face uncertain outlooks while several starting quarterbacks have been ruled out
full_text:
After a wild, high-scoring Week 1, the NFL is moving into Week 2, full steam ahead. Unfortunately for some teams, the league takes no breaks for bad breaks, literally and figuratively. Several teams already face significant injuries.
The Falcons are still dealing with major issues at quarterback, and the Vikings are already down their Week 1 starter, too. Top targets for several AFC teams are in doubt as we head into the weekend, too. Below are the final injury reports of the week for every team playing on Sunday -- plus the latest updates from the "Monday Night Football" teams (the Rams host the Giants) -- and analysis for every report.
On Wednesday, Burrow said, "That's ridiculous," when asked about not facing the Texans, and Friday, coach Zac Taylor indicated his franchise quarterback would be good to go. Nonetheless, he is officially questionable against a talented Houston defense looking to bounce back from a poor Week 1.
The Texans, meanwhile, will be without their top target in Collins, who hurt his hamstring in practice this week. He's had hamstring issues previously, too. Remember, Jayden Higgins (ACL) is out for the year, so Houston is hurting at pass catcher. They'll also be down Ingram, a starter on the offensive line.
The Panthers being without Bobby Brown III leaves them thin along the interior defensive line behind standout Derrick Brown. Second-round rookie Lee Hunter impressed in Week 1 and should be in line for more time as Carolina's defense looks to bounce back after allowing 59 points last week. In good news for the offense, WR Jalen Coker (ankle) practiced fully on Friday and is not on the final injury report.
It's a much longer list for the Falcons, who will again start Cooper Rush, with Penix Jr. still returning from last season's ACL surgery and Tagovailoa doubtful with an oblique injury sustained ahead of last week's game. Lindstrom and Terrell both practiced fully Friday, a good sign for their availability.
The Browns are without Jenkins for the second straight week. Campbell popped up on the injury report Thursday, when he did not practice, but he was back out there Friday. Todd Monken thought Campbell "moved around well."
The Buccaneers have listed three players as questionable after they all practiced fully on Friday: safety Miles Killebrew (concussion), wide receiver Jalen McMillan (knee) and cornerback Jacob Parrish (back). Otherwise, Tampa Bay enters Week 2 relatively healthy.
The Packers have several issues, mostly in the trenches. An already-struggling offensive line is being tested by knee ailments to Bako-Bewele and Banks. Both practiced in a limited fashion all week, just like they did in Week 1. Bako-Bewele started in Week 1 despite this status, while Banks was inactive. On the other hand, Hargrave's doubt hurts the interior defensive line. Van Ness' status will be crucial for the Packers to generate pressure.
New York is also dealing with several injuries, including to Fitzpatrick -- a significant blow to the secondary. Ossai will miss his second straight game. McDonald is expected to play, per Aaron Glenn. Also, second-round pick D'Angelo Ponds is expected to make his NFL debut.
Minnesota will turn to Carson Wentz with Murray out. Murray suffered his concussion just a few plays into his Vikings debut, though Wentz entered and threw three touchdown passes to rally the Vikings to a win over the Packers. O'Neill's status is worth monitoring. He went from a limited participant on Wednesday to a non-participant on Thursday.
Chicago had a clean injury report.
New Orleans will carry some injury concerns into Week 2 as it looks to avoid an 0-2 start. Olave and Young were limited participants on Friday.
Still, their issues pale in comparison to Baltimore's. Flowers had 150 yards and a touchdown in less than one half last week before exiting; the hamstring has bothered him for a bit, going back to training camp. Stanley and Simpson constitute two starting offensive linemen, while Hendrickson is the top pass rusher. All three were limited on Friday, their first practice of the week. Buchanan and Madubuike still aren't quite back from season-ending injuries from last year.
Greenard will miss his second straight game, a tough blow to the Eagles' pass rush. Elsewhere on Philadelphia's defensive line, Jalen Carter (wrist) was limited Friday but does not carry an injury designation. The Titans, meanwhile, saw Flott not practice on Friday after practicing on Wednesday and Thursday. Gray has been a full practice participant all week.
Porter's situation continues to be a sticky one , as the nature of his "injury" suggests, and now he'll officially miss his second game in a row. Fautanu logged a full practice Friday, whereas Pittman did not practice Thursday or Friday.
The biggest injury concern for New England is Davis, who has not practiced this week. New England is pretty thin at cornerback behind Davis, Christian Gonzalez and nickel back Marcus Jones. A.J. Brown (ankle) is also out, though he's not listed because he's on IR.
Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Bowers will test out his knee ahead of Sunday's game before a decision is made, but for now, the 2024 All-Pro is considered doubtful. Michael Mayer would again be in line for a busy day if Bowers can't play. Backup quarterback Aidan O'Connell is questionable after not practicing on Thursday and Friday because of a personal reason.
Chargers No. 1 wide receiver Ladd McConkey is questionable after practicing in a limited fashion for the first time this week on Friday. Cornerback Deane Leonard (abdomen) is questionable after practicing as a limited participant all week.
Jacksonville had a clean injury report.
Denver ruled out wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr. (foot) after he didn't practice all week. Running back RJ Harvery (hamstring) is questionable after not practicing on Wednesday and then practicing on a limited basis on both Thursday and Friday.
Amid a tough start to the season, the Dolphins got some more bad news in the form of Robinson suffering a concussion in Wednesday's practice. The promising young pass rusher will not play Sunday. Inside linebacker Ronnie Harrison (hamstring) is also out after not practicing all week. Long snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder) is the only player questionable after being limited in practice all week.
San Francisco rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) underwent surgery and will be out for at least a couple months. Meanwhile, kicker Eddie Pineiro (illness) and running back Kaelon Black (groin) are questionable. Pineiro hasn't practiced all week, while Black was limited on Thursday and Friday.
Seattle ruled out starting quarterback Sam Darnold (glute) for Week 2 after he didn't practice all week, which means backup Drew Lock will start against the Cardinals. Guard Anthony Bradford is questionable after being limited on Wednesday and Thursday before not practicing on Friday. Safety Nick Emmanwori (ankle, hip) is getting closer to potentially making his 2026 season debut. He was a limited practice participant all week.
Much of the Cardinals defense is questionable this week after their Week 1 win at the Los Angeles Chargers. Arizona ruled out cornerback Garrett Williams (Achilles) despite him practicing as a limited participant all week. Guard Isaac Seumalo (shoulder) is questionable after not practicing on Wednesday but then practicing on both Thursday and Friday.
Washington will be without two key pieces in this NFC East matchup. Both Okonkwo and Luvu got hurt in Week 1 against the Eagles. The Commanders don't have a tight end who can match Okonkwo's speed and YAC abilities, but they could use more three-wide receiver looks.
The Cowboys hope both Hooker and Overshown can return from their respective injuries after missing just one or two games. Hooker underwent surgery for his forearm this week while Overshown remains on the mend. Overshown was the green dot, middle linebacker for Dallas in Week 1, but it will be third-round…
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Bengals star Joe Burrow listed as questionable: Here's what Zac Taylor said about Week 2 status
summary: Why the Bengals' QB was listed as questionable for Week 2
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- After being limited in two practices, Joe Burrow is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Houston Texans . A back injury limited him in practice on both Wednesday and Thursday, but the good news for the Bengals is that he was back on the field as a full participant for Friday's session.
During a Friday interview with a small group of reporters on Friday, including CBS Sports, Bengals coach Zac Taylor was asked what Burrow's status would be for Sunday.
"He practiced in full today," Taylor said. "He feels good."
The fact that Burrow is now feeling good is definitely a positive sign for his availability for the game in Houston, so why the injury designation if the signs are pointing up for him? The nature of Burrow's injury is likely why he was listed as questionable. The veteran QB was dealing with back tightness this week, which can be somewhat unpredictable. Burrow might feel "good" on Friday, but if he were to wake up with an ailing back on Sunday, the Bengals might have to consider keeping him on the bench (That doesn't mean that's going to happen; it just means the Bengals are essentially covering their bases by listing him as questionable).
Taylor was asked whether the Bengals might elevate Josh Johnson from the practice squad to serve as the emergency third quarterback this week, and the eighth-year coach admitted it's a move his team might consider.
"It's a possibility," Taylor said.
The fact that the Bengals are considering that move likely means they want to see how Burrow's back feels over the next 48 hours before committing to anything.
During Friday's session, Burrow threw more than a dozen passes and didn't appear to show any discomfort during the portion of practice that was open to the media.
Burrow suffered his injury during a Week 1 win over the Buccaneers , where he took a couple of big hits, including one that came from Alex Anzalone . On a third-and-6 play in the first quarter, Burrow crashed into Anazlone while fighting for a first down on what ended up being a six-yard run.
Although Taylor doesn't ever want to see his QB take a big hit, he said he won't ask Burrow to stop being Burrow.
"He has to go play football," Taylor said. "This is the NFL . Of course, we want him to be safe and healthy. I'm not comfortable saying don't get the first down on third-and-8, and then be two yards short, and [then] let's go for it. That's why he's here, he's a competitor. If you take that from him, now what do you have? You got a guy, you're taking the stinger out of him a little bit. I'm not about that."
If it's up to Burrow, he's definitely going to play Sunday. During a press conference on Wednesday , the QB was asked if he might consider sitting out the Texans game as a precaution and he gave a three-word answer.
"No, that's ridiculous," Burrow said.
If Burrow can't play Sunday, then the Bengals would turn the offense over to Joe Flacco , but he sounds 100% confident that he'll be out there.
"If I'm not getting surgery, I'll be out there," Burrow said.
The Bengals and Texans will kick off in Houston at 1 p.m. ET on CBS, with Kevin Harlan and Trent Green on the call and Melanie Collins on the sideline.
author: John Breech

title: Texans rule out two-time Pro Bowl WR Nico Collins for Week 2 vs. Bengals
summary: Collins had seven catches and a touchdown in Week 1, but he suffered a hamstring injury during Wednesday's practice
full_text:
The Houston Texans may have escaped a major injury scare, but they are without their star wide receiver this Sunday. Nico Collins will not play in the Texans' Week 2 game against the Cincinnati Bengals . The team ruled him out on Friday after Collins didn't practice on Thursday or Friday. It's thought his hamstring injury isn't considered serious, but it's enough to keep him out at least a week.
Collins got off to a strong start this season, posting seven catches for 75 yards and a touchdown in Houston's season-opening loss to the Buffalo Bills . He's coming off back-to-back Pro Bowl campaigns and three consecutive 1,000-plus-yard, six-plus-touchdown seasons. He is widely considered one of the best X receivers in the league.
With Collins missing Sunday's game, the Texans could be in trouble. Houston already lost presumptive No. 2 wideout Jayden Higgins for the year to a torn ACL suffered during a preseason practice, while the explosive Tank Dell remains on injured reserve. He was not yet ready to return from the devastating knee injury he suffered during the 2024 season.
The Texans will likely roll with Kayshon Boutte , Xavier Hutchinson , Jaylin Noel and Jared Wayne as their top four wide receivers. They also have Lewis Bond , Josh Kelly , Daniel Sobkowicz and Mitchell Tinsley on the practice squad. Houston also has five tight ends — Dalton Schultz , Foster Moreau , Marlin Klein , Cade Stover and Brevin Jordan — on the roster and would likely lean into more 12 and 13 personnel looks in Collins' absence.
The Bengals looked somewhat improved defensively in Week 1, forcing four turnovers against the Buccaneers . But they still allowed 5.4 yards per play, which would have been an above-average offensive mark last season. Houston managed 5.2 yards per play in Week 1 against Buffalo with an inconsistent run game ( David Montgomery scored three total touchdowns but averaged just three yards per carry), and things could get even more difficult in Week 2 since the Texans are without Collins to open up the field.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Here's what Tom Cruise and Taylor Swift talked about at the Chiefs' NFL opener
summary: Cruise attended his first NFL game in many years, and described the experience and discussions with Taylor Swift
full_text:
The biggest celebrity hotspot in the NFL in Week 1 was definitely in Kansas City. Taylor Swift and Tom Cruise both showed up to watch the Chiefs' cruise (Sorry, I couldn't resist the pun) to a 31-10 over the Broncos on Monday night.
It's not often that you get the most famous movie star in the world sitting next to arguably the most famous singer on the planet, but that's exactly what we got at Arrowhead Stadium. Swift, who married Travis Kelce back in July, is regularly in attendance at Chiefs' games, but for Cruise, it was the first NFL game he's attended since at least 2020.
Taylor Swift and Tom Cruise in the house for MNF DENvsKC on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/59S027XB8M
Apparently, Cruise loved everything about his experience on Monday night.
"That was the most fun I've ever had at a football game," Cruise told Travis and Jason Kelce on the latest episode of the New Heights podcast .
"I'm not coming to Kansas to see you lose" @tomcruise had one message for Travis before coming to watch a game at Arrowhead NEW EPISODE OUT NOW!!! pic.twitter.com/5wnAZ0pn3d
Cruise was partly there to watch Travis, so he was probably thrilled to see the Chiefs' tight end catch three passes for a team-high 71 yards in the win.
During an interview on "The Tonight Show starring Jimmy Fallon ,", Cruise revealed what he talked about with Swift during the game, and apparently, our main takeaway here should be that Taylor knows ball.
"She was schooling me on football, for real," Cruise said. "First of all, she's a genius. I've been following her since she was a kid. Everybody's there [at the game], all their friends, they're a beautiful couple and magical in their own right, and everybody there in that booth -- I hadn't been to a football game since pre-COVID, where I was working and everything -- to get to hang out there and have that moment, it was a lot."
During his conversation with Swift, Cruise apparently found out that she didn't know much about football before meeting Kelce, but after she started dating the Chiefs' star tight end, she did her homework.
"She knew nothing about football when she met Travis," Cruise said. "It was like, 'What was it like playing against your brother, like, tackling each other.' I told Travis, he was very patient. She said, 'You know, he's so patient.' And I said, 'I'm sure he was.'"
Taylor might not have known the basics of football back in 2023, but now, she's an expert on the sport.
"She knows, she's just bringing it," Cruise said.
As you can imagine, Cruise and Swift didn't just talk about football; they also conversed about several other topics.
"We talked about music and movies," Cruise said. "And she's funny. She's got such a great sense of humor. She's a brilliant writer, also, by the way. A brilliant musician. Very skilled."
Based on how much fun he had, don't be surprised if you see Cruise at a Chiefs' game at some point down the road.
"Mahomes is back, the team is just fantastic," Cruise told the Kelce brothers. "I gotta say, the whole crowd, the vibe, you hear about it, but to be here and experience it, it was so cool."
Cruise has been making the rounds this week to promote his new movie, "Digger," which comes out on Oct. 2.
author: John Breech

title: Joey Porter Jr. best trade fits: Why Cowboys make sense, two NFC North teams could be in line to make offer
summary: Five possible mock trade fits for Porter, who is still at odds with the Steelers and is out for Week 2
full_text:
The Joey Porter Jr . situation in Pittsburgh is seemingly growing and evolving every day. The talented fourth-year cornerback has been waiting months for a contract extension, and the Steelers aren't willing to comply — at least not to Porter's liking. According to ESPN's Brooke Pryor and Jeremy Fowler , the biggest issue is the Steelers' reluctance to guarantee money long-term, an organizational precedent they have broken only for stars. Porter, 26, believes he's a star of that caliber; Pittsburgh isn't quite there.
Porter's absence has also had its twists and turns. He was officially on the physically unable to perform list throughout training camp with a back injury, though Mike McCarthy later pointed to his absence as contract-related. Even this week, Porter was listed as a limited participant Wednesday with "Not Injury Related -- conditioning" as the reason. On Thursday, though, he was listed as limited due to the back injury.
Porter missed Week 1 and is out once again for Week 2. One source told ESPN, "I don't know if he ever puts on a Steelers uniform again."
It should be noted that ESPN reports the Steelers have "neither made nor received any serious inquiries" regarding Porter, though Porter did request a trade. One source, per ESPN, believes Porter plus a quality Day 3 pick could fetch a second-round selection.
Joey Porter Jr. has been very good for the Steelers since going 32nd overall in 2023. At 6-foot-2, he has impressive size and physicality, especially at the catch point. The Penn State product allowed just a 42% completion percentage as the primary defender last year, according to Pro Football Focus, the second-lowest number in the league behind Quinyon Mitchell (min. 50 targets).
He was even better in man coverage, allowing an NFL-low 35.3% completion percentage in those scenarios (min. 30 man coverage targets). That was just a tick better than the player currently topping the cornerback market: the Patriots ' Christian Gonzalez .
Furthermore, Porter has improved in several statistical areas throughout his career.
Porter can get a little too physical — his 14 defensive pass interference penalties are the most since he entered the NFL in 2023, and his five defensive holds are tied for eighth-most — but he is generally a very good corner who can take on the toughest assignments.
Because Porter was a second-round pick, he has no fifth-year option attached to his rookie deal. Other top corners drafted in 2023, such as Christian Gonzalez and Devon Witherspoon , received record-breaking deals, but they were also first-round picks. The Patriots and Seahawks , therefore, were more eager to extend them in order to limit their cap hits in their respective fifth years. They've also, simply, been better players than Porter.
That's not to say Porter hasn't been good — and at times excellent — but he is not quite regarded as being in their class. Gonzalez was a second-team All-Pro in 2024 and a Pro Bowler in 2025. Witherspoon is a three-time Pro Bowler and was a second-team All-Pro last year. Both were in the Super Bowl a season ago, and both shined in that game. Porter, who is also older than both, has not made a Pro Bowl or All-Pro team, and his team has not won a playoff game.
You had to know this one was coming, right? Jerry Jones has hinted at another big move all offseason and into the preseason, and he certainly didn't like what he saw from the Cowboys ' defense in Week 1 against the Giants . Porter would immediately be the top cornerback on the team. Jones has also shown an ability to open up his checkbook. (In fact, he usually pays more than he needs to because he drives a hard bargain and waits too long to extend guys, but the deals usually eventually get done.)
One only needs to turn on the Bears ' Week 1 win over the Panthers to see why cornerback is such a need. There were issues all over the place. Top slot cornerback Kyler Gordon is still battling injury issues that limited him to just five games (including playoffs) last year.
Furthermore, the Bears played the second-highest rate of man coverage in Week 1, only behind the Colts . Ben Johnson has said he wants the highest-scoring offense in NFL history, and he might have to, given how porous his defense is. Porter would be an immediate, massive upgrade. Chicago would have to do a lot of restructuring for 2027 (which it'd do regardless), but the fit and need are clearly there.
Buffalo is off to a flying 2-0 start this year with Josh Allen already the frontrunner for MVP . The Bills have scored 77 points in two games.
The only problem? They've conceded 62 points. Jared Goff threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns in Week 2, four days after C.J. Stroud threw for 274 yards and two scores in Week 1. When the Bills don't get pressure, they're allowing 8.2 yards per attempt this season, which is among the bottom dozen teams.
Moreover, big picture, the Bills should be all-in. The offense looks awesome. The defensive front is getting early breakouts from Greg Rousseau and Deone Walker . Adding a game-changing cornerback would be an excellent "cherry-on-top" move, and pairing Christian Benford with Porter would turn a question mark into a strength.
Here's the team the Bills just beat. The Lions have problems all over their defense, so much so that All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell was fighting back tears after Thursday night's loss.
Cornerback, especially, is a glaring need. The Lions swung and missed in a big way in 2024 with first-rounder Terrion Arnold (no longer with the team) and second-rounder Ennis Rakestraw Jr . (last played in 2024). Those misses are really hurting right now. Perhaps there will be shakeups with the mini bye ahead. The Lions have been aggressive moving draft capital in trade-ups; maybe this time they will be aggressive in acquiring a player. Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard would love a big, physical man corner.
The Chargers had a ton of cap room this year and didn't really do much with it. That's been the modus operandi for the Bolts and GM Joe Hortiz, who came over from Baltimore, another team that leans heavily on drafting and developing.
Los Angeles got excellent play out of its defense in recent years, with Jesse Minter's outstanding defensive playbook and coverage concepts helping many defensive backs play at their highest level. But it's not an overly talented group — more one where the sum has been better than its parts — and Porter could immediately bring the talent level up a notch. Premier young talent doesn't come available often. If it does with Porter, the Chargers shouldn't hesitate to throw themselves into the mix.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Vikings rule out Kyler Murray for Week 2 vs. Bears, Carson Wentz to start
summary: Murray remains in concussion protocol after his anticipated Vikings debut lasted less than one quarter
full_text:
Kyler Murray (concussion) is out for the Vikings ' Week 2 game against the Bears , the team announced. Carson Wentz will get the start, his sixth for Minnesota since the beginning of last season.
Murray's much-anticipated Vikings debut ended after less than a quarter , when he got hit by two Packers defenders -- Lukas Van Ness and Javon Bullard -- during a scramble. Bullard was flagged for unnecessary roughness while Murray lay on the ground and got medical attention, and Murray went back to the locker room shortly thereafter.
Scary scene as Kyler Murray takes a massive hit and stays down after the play. pic.twitter.com/sVqZ7M24e4
Wentz entered and played well, going 12 for 19 for 133 yards and three touchdowns, including a 39-yarder to Justin Jefferson . He did not commit a single turnover (a Packers penalty wiped out an interception), but he had three sacks (a Packers penalty also wiped out another sack).
The Vikings were hoping Murray would stop the quarterback carousel Minnesota unhappily rode last season. The Vikings opened the season with 2024 first-round pick J.J. McCarthy as the starter, but he got hurt, leading to Wentz taking over. All told, McCarthy started 10 games, Wentz started five games, and undrafted rookie Max Brosmer started two games.
Murray, on a one-year deal, battled McCarthy for the starting job for a few weeks in training camp before winning the job. McCarthy then fell to third on the depth chart, behind Wentz, as he struggled with his accuracy. Now, it'll be Wentz called upon again in an important early-division matchup; McCarthy will back him up.
The Vikings and Bears are both 1-0 this season.
Counting Sunday, Murray will have missed 13 of the last 14 games going back to last season. He suffered a foot injury in the Cardinals ' Week 5 collapse against the Titans and did not play thereafter.
Murray was supposed to be a convenient answer for the Vikings after last year's roller coaster. Though he has never reached the heights expected of a No. 1 overall pick, he has generally been a solid option behind center, delivering average or above-average play. Considering the Vikings went 9-8 last year with major quarterback issues, Murray's cheap signing (he's still getting paid by Arizona) was looked at as a major boost to Minnesota's playoff hopes.
Instead, one week in, he is dealing with injuries, an all-too-familiar issue.
The good thing for the Vikings is Wentz has experience -- both in general and in the system -- and is just a few days removed from leading an unlikely comeback. Since the start of last season, Wentz is (out of 45 quarterbacks with at least 100 attempts)
Those first two numbers are fine. The next two numbers are not great, and the last two numbers are pretty bad. Wentz's proclivity to take sacks can derail drives in a hurry, and he no longer avoids pressure like he once did when he was younger and more mobile. Avoiding negative plays will be absolutely crucial for Wentz and for Minnesota as a whole.
While the Bears don't possess the most fearsome pass rush and have a leaky defense overall, they did sack Bryce Young twice and pick him off once. Chicago also led the NFL in takeaways last year.
Still, Wentz has a big arm and one of the NFL's best wide receivers in Jefferson. In fact, Jefferson averaged 95.4 receiving yards per game in Wentz's five starts last year, and the two showed a strong connection in Week 1 as well.
