title: Chicago Bears Big Play Breakdowns from Week 1
summary: There’s a lot to love about Ben Johnson but his focus on hunting explosive plays may be my favorite part of his football philosophy. The Bears logged nine explosive plays (a run of 10 or more yards or a pass of 20 or more yards) in Sunday’s monster victory against the Carolina Panthers. Four of […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - SEPTEMBER 13: Cole Kmet #85 of the Chicago Bears scores a touchdown during the second quarter of the game against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s a lot to love about Ben Johnson but his focus on hunting explosive plays may be my favorite part of his football philosophy. The Bears logged nine explosive plays (a run of 10 or more yards or a pass of 20 or more yards) in Sunday’s monster victory against the Carolina Panthers. Four of those explosive plays were on touchdowns and the other five led to scores. That’s the most in the Ben Johnson era and a preview of the big things to come this season. We’ll track all of them weekly in this column. Explosive Play 1.1 – Q1 8:19, 1st and 10 at the Carolina 45. D’Andre Swift carries the ball off right tackle for 32 yards. The possession would end in a TD. After the Bears turned the ball over on the opening possession, they got things rolling on a scoring drive highlighted by this Swift explosive play. Last year, many of the big runs put up by the Bears were to the right side of the offensive line, so it was fitting to have the first explosive play of the season feed off Darnell Wright. The Bears huddle here with 11 personnel (1 running back, 1 tight end, 3 wide receivers) and line up in an I-Formation with Cole Kmet as the fullback. Luther Burden starts on the right side of the formation next to Rome Odunze, motioning to the left side before the snap. Darnell Wright kicks his defender off to the right. Jonah Jackson and Garrett Bradbury try to work a double team with Kmet leading into the four hole (between the right guard and right tackle). Bradbury leaves the double team early when Jackson powers his defender off to the right, leaving the center to pick up a linebacker at the second level. It’s well-blocked and Swift encounters first contact about 6 yards from scrimmage. After that, it’s an incredible display of running from Swift, breaking out of two tackles at the point of contact and quickly juking a third defender, maneuvering back to the middle of the field before getting chased down. Swift gets a ton of the credit here. D'Andre Swift showing why he got that extension ‼️ CHIvsCAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/AiqMSBsMEJ — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 Explosive Play 1.2 – Q1 3:01, 2nd and 8 at the Chicago 47. Caleb Williams pass complete deep right to Rome Odunze for 47 yards. The possession would end in a TD. This is one of those plays I’ve been dreaming about since early last season when it was clear Caleb Williams had a special talent in avoiding pressure. This is a scramble drill success play and one of those aspects of the Bears offense that could take this thing to the stratosphere. The Bears break the huddle in 11 personnel but split Loveland out to the left side of the formation with Luther Burden. Caleb drops back, looks right, looks left, and flushes to his right. Odunze senses the scramble drill starting and flies down the field with his hand in the air. Caleb throws the ball a little late or short, but it’s either going to be a defensive pass interference or an Odunze catch given the position of the defender scrambling to make back the space. Odunze reaches over the head and pulls in a highlight throw. While this isn’t the play that is scripted, the scramble drill is something that desperately needed work from last season and something Ben Johnson has mentioned as an area of focus. Early returns are good. 🗣️ ROOOOOOME ODUUUUUNZE 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/upRsL6ndv8 — Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) September 13, 2026 Explosive Play 1.3 – Q2 14:05, 1st and 10 from the Carolina 22. Caleb Williams pass complete deep left to Cole Kmet for 22 yard TD. This play-action pass elicited an audible gasp-turned-maniacal-laugh from me when it happened. The Bears come out in 13 personnel (3 tight ends!) with the rookie Sam Roush lined up next to Kmet and Loveland on the right side, Jahdae Walker the lone wide receiver to the left. Walker runs a route to the post pulling the boundary defender with him long enough for Caleb to fit a perfect (and I mean perfect) ball into Kmet for the score. Cole’s route starts as if he’s down blocking to the left and quickly heads up field on a TE leak play. The defender does a nice job sticking with him but no defending a perfect pass. CALEB TO KMET FOR 6 CHIvsCAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/KedXXw4da5 — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 Explosive Play 1.4 – Q2 1:14, 3rd and 11 from the Chicago 19. Caleb Williams pass complete deep left to Kalif Raymond for 28 yards. This was the first of three explosive plays on the drive that ended the half with a TD. Jump man back at it! This amazing end of the half sequence started with this beauty to Kalif Raymond. The Bears come out in 11 personnel with Loveland lined up tight next to Braxton Jones and three receivers to the right. Luther Burden motions to the left and Caleb takes the snap from shotgun. Caleb pump fakes short to Rome and starts to scramble to his left before firing a jump man pass into Raymond near midfield. Raymond makes a sliding catch and the Bears are in business. The Caleb Williams jump pass makes an appearance 👀 CHIvsCAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/2VrYZolfV7 — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 Explosive Play 1.5 – Q2 0:38, 2nd and 10 from the Chicago 47. Caleb Williams pass complete deep left to Luther Burden for 24 yards. This was the second of three explosive plays on the drive that ended the half with a TD. Two plays later, Williams and Burden connect for a nice little gainer. Sticking with 11 personnel, Loveland is flexed out to the left side with Burden. Loveland runs an underneath route with Burden working intermediate. Burden does a nice job at the top of his stem with a juke before breaking inside with separation. Caleb finds him in rhythm with Burden adding a few additional yards after the catch. Solid pitch and catch. Explosive Play 1.6 – Q2 0:32, 1st and 10 from the Carolina 29. Caleb Williams scrambles around left end for 29 yard touchdown. This was the third of three explosive plays on the drive that ended the half with a TD. This was great recognition on the part of Caleb to evade pressure and know that he could get a good gain with man coverage. The Panthers bring only four here but fail to leave anyone to spy on Williams. As the onset of pressure, Caleb tucks the ball to flee the pocket and takes off with his world class speed. Seeing that the coverage was blanketing his receivers in man coverage, the speed of Williams made this an easy touchdown – but don’t discount that there are very few quarterbacks that can reach the sprint speed that Williams has put on film in his young career. The longest run of Caleb Williams' career 💨 CHIvsCAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NCOfwIBcDx — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 Explosive Play 1.7 – Q3 0:50, 1st and 10 from the Chicago 39. Kyle Monangai runs up the middle for 61 yard TD. Now we’re just showing off. The Bears take over on downs up 38-31 and score a monster touchdown with Monangai. The Bears use basic 11 personnel with Kmet attached to the right side of the formation. Burden comes in short motion left to right and acts of a lead blocker for Monangai. Raymond scores an excellent block at the point of attack about five yards from scrimmage, allowing Monangai to cut off that block to the right. From there it’s a race to the end zone with Walker providing a…hands up block to slow down one Panthers defender and Monangai using just enough jet fuel to pull off a 61-yarder. This really broke the game. 61-yard Kyle Monangai TD! title: 4 key matchups to watch for Bengals vs. Texans
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals will travel to Houston this Sunday to take on CJ Stroud and a very talented defense on the other side of the ball. That defense is coming off a performance in which they allowed 36 points against the Buffalo Bills. Will the Bengals do the same, or will the Texans bounce back? […]
full_text: Sep 13, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Cincinnati Bengals defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II (97) runs on the field before the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cincinnati Bengals will travel to Houston this Sunday to take on CJ Stroud and a very talented defense on the other side of the ball. That defense is coming off a performance in which they allowed 36 points against the Buffalo Bills. Will the Bengals do the same, or will the Texans bounce back? Let’s take a look at some of the key matchups in this one. Ja’Marr Chase vs. Derek Stingley This is a matchup of two of the best players at their respective positions. These guys are familiar with one another dating back to their LSU days. Chase is coming off a game in which he had just 2 catches for 12 yards. Stingley was credited with allowing 4 catches on 6 targets that came his way. That 66.7% completion rate is much higher than his career mark of 53.4%. With both players looking for a better performance than in Week 1, we could be in for some fireworks. Amarius Mims vs. Will Anderson Jr. Anderson was able to record .5 of a sack against Buffalo during week one. He is a player who has 30 sacks through his first 3 seasons in the league. He is one of the most explosive pass rushers in all of football. Meanwhile, Amarius Mims didn’t allow a single pressure against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Mims was tasked with going up against a talented rookie in Rueben Bain. While that was a fantastic performance, Anderson presents an even bigger challenge due to that aforementioned explosiveness. This titanic battle could go a long way in deciding which team comes out on top this weekend. It is important to note that the Texans will move their defensive ends around. Even when Mims is not facing Anderson, he will be going up against talented pass rushers like Danielle Hunter and Jadeveon Clowney for the Texans. Amarius Mims vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers pic.twitter.com/ehyW38iwIP — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 14, 2026 Texans running backs vs. Bengals linebackers Not a one-to-one direct matchup, but the running game of the Texans against the run defense of the young Bengals linebacker is a key matchup in this one for me. Barrett Carter looked like an improved player from his rookie season. However, he did still record 3 missed tackles. Demetrius Knight Jr. also recorded 3 missed tackles against Tampa Bay. They did combine for 15 tackles, with Carter adding half a sack on a play that Knight scooped and scored on. Carter would then go on to force a fumble at the goal line on Baker Mayfield, which was recovered in the end zone by Bryan Cook. The young Bengals linebackers will need to make sure they do not allow David Montgomery and Woody Marks to run wild this week. Montgomery finished Week 1 with 3 total touchdowns. He rushed for 60 yards and added another 19 receiving yards to go with it. Woody Marks was also able to rush for 42 yards against the Bills. Dexter Lawrence vs. Texans interior 0-line Lawrence didn’t stuff the stat sheet in Week 1, but he was all over the revamped Bengals defense. He was second on the team with 3 pressures during the game, and should have drawn several holding penalties against the Buccaneers offensive line. One of those non-penalties was when he almost had a sack on Mayfield, before Mayfield ultimately had the ball knocked loose by Barrett Carter. The Texans interior offensive line consists of Keylan Rutledge, Evan Brown, and Ed Ingram. Those three players will all take turns having their hands full with trying to slow down Dexter Lawrence. Lawrence’s impact will continue to free up his teammates, but I imagine Lawrence is hoping that this is the week he gets to unleash the Sexy Dexy dance for a sack celebration after coming so close during the first week. Dexter Lawrence vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers Lawrence’s impact will not always show on the box score, but this is absolutely a difference maker on defense. pic.twitter.com/5ccswD2BDK — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 15, 2026

title: Bengals vs. Texans: 5 questions with Battle Red Blog
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are getting set for a big test in Week 2 against the Houston Texans. There are concerns on the injury front for the Bengals, and the Texans are hungry to get their first win in front of a home crowd. To help us get a lay of the land, we tapped the […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow runs the ball in the first quarter during the home opener against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Paycor Stadium on September 13, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Cincinnati Bengals are getting set for a big test in Week 2 against the Houston Texans. There are concerns on the injury front for the Bengals, and the Texans are hungry to get their first win in front of a home crowd. To help us get a lay of the land, we tapped the knowledge of Scott Barzilla over at Battle Red Blog. Here are five questions we asked him ahead of the clash. 1.) What did you see from C.J. Stroud, in terms of improvement this summer and last week? I know there has been a contract impasse between him and the Texans—does he still feel like the long-term answer? SB: It’s always a mixed bag with Stroud. Overall, it was a really good performance, and it makes you feel good about him as a quarterback. He had a 106.5 rating and is on pace to have a 30-TD season. However, that was sandwiched by two fumbles that played a key role in the game. I don’t really blame him for the second fumble, but ball security is a huge issue. The question for the Texans long-term is how much they want to invest in a near-franchise quarterback, considering that they have committed so many resources to their defense. $60-million quarterbacks mean you have to save elsewhere, and there is still an open question as to whether he is good enough to elevate a flawed roster the same way the other elite quarterbacks do. As I sit here, I don’t know what the long-term answer is. He is certainly as good as many of the quarterbacks that have gotten paid, but he is not as good as others (say Joe Burrow), so it makes it an impossibly complicated question. 2.) Talk about the loss of Henry To’oTo’o this week, and its potential impact on this game. SB: I’m really worried that this team is already losing key starters to injury when the defense was very healthy last year. It is not as acute as when facing more mobile quarterbacks, but it still presents coverage issues because the Texans already have difficulties covering tight ends, and that is one more option taken away from them. I would bet pretty heavily on the over for Mike Gesecki receiving yards, as the Texans really don’t have a good answer for him with injuries they have already suffered to their linebacking core (they lost E.J. Speed in training camp). 3.) Much like the Bengals, questions about the Texans’ offensive line have been prevalent. They have made moves to remedy that—did it show up last week? SB: Keelan Rutledge may have been the steal of the draft. He was the only lineman to have a 70+ PFF rating last week at left guard. They are marginally better at center with Evan Brown than they were last season. The rest of the line is the same. In particular, the right side of their line struggled against Buffalo as Trent Brown and Ed Ingram got beat on some key plays. Ingram was solid last season, so we can hope that was a one-off. Brown was solid down the stretch, but there is very little chance he makes it through 17 games healthy. They signed Braden Smith in the offseason, and he is out with a plantar fasciitis injury. Hopefully, he will be able to return by week five, but that is the state of the line. So, overall they are improved, but there are still some holes that opponents can exploit. 4.) Who are a couple of X-Factors (maybe under-the-radar guys who could surprise) on Houston’s offense and defense for you this week? SB: On offense, the big key on Sunday will be the receiving core with Nico Collins out. Keyshon Boutte was acquired right before the end of the preseason, so he is probably still learning the playbook, but he is capable of making a big play or two. The rest will likely rest on their tight ends and Xavier Hutchinson. I like Jaylin Noel in the open field if they give him a screen or two, but the overall production from the receivers will be an issue. A deep cut could be Marlin Klein, their second-round pick. He has a ton of athleticism for a tight end, but is still raw. If he is guarded one-on-one by a linebacker or safety, it could be a mismatch. 5.) The line has hovered between 2.5-3-points in favor of the Texans, per FanDuel this week. What are your thoughts on that and how do you see this playing out? SB: I’m not comfortable going either way on this line. I just don’t have a good feel for the game. Like you, I think the over is as good a bet as could be had in this game. Both offenses can put points on the board, so someone is going off in this game. If you held a gun to my head, I would pick the Bengals and take the points. I am not touching this money line with a forty-foot pole on either side. I just don’t have a good feel for it, to tell you the truth. Our thanks to Scott Barzilla for the chat. Check out the other side of the conversation at Battle Red Blog .
author: Anthony Cosenza

title: 3 keys to a Cincinnati Bengals victory vs. the Houston Texans
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are set to play their first road game of the season, as they’ll head to the Lone Star State for a battle with a Houston Texans team coming off three straight playoff berths. Here is a look at the Bengals’ three keys to getting a victory. Exposing the Texans’ linebackers in coverage […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are set to play their first road game of the season, as they’ll head to the Lone Star State for a battle with a Houston Texans team coming off three straight playoff berths. Here is a look at the Bengals’ three keys to getting a victory. Exposing the Texans’ linebackers in coverage The Houston Texans have one of the best defenses in the NFL. One area of weakness on it is at the linebacker position, specifically taking advantage of the linebackers in coverage. With Henry To’o To’o going on short-term IR, there will be an even bigger opportunity for the Bengals to take advantage of some of these matchups. Buffalo Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid was able to go for 130 receiving yards against the Texans this past week. Meanwhile, Mike Gesicki was the Bengals’ leading receiver, with 78 yards against the Buccaneers. I would expect the Bengals to be looking Gesicki’s way once again this week. Cincinnati should also be looking to get Chase Brown and Samaje Perine the football in the passing game. The two players combined for 8 receptions for 52 yards in the Bengals ‘ Week 1 victory. Taking advantage of Jake Hansen, who is filling in for the injured To’o To’o, is one key to the Bengals starting the season 2-0 this year. Win the turnover battle While this is key to victory any week, it is even more crucial this coming Sunday. The Bengals forced and recovered four fumbles in their Week 1 victory. Meanwhile, the Texans had to sack fumbles of their own. If the Bengals can force a couple more turnovers than the Texans in this one, they will have a great chance to come out with the victory on the road. While quarterback CJ Stroud did not throw an interception against Buffalo, he threw 4 interceptions last year in the playoff loss to the New England Patriots. Meanwhile, Joe Burrow had a pick-six this past week against Tampa Bay that cut a two-possession lead down to just 7 points in the second half. Whichever team can limit the mistakes should be able to walk out with the win between two really talented football teams. Interior pressure from the defensive line Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen were force multipliers during the Bengals ‘ Week 1 victory, with Allen recording a key third-down sack that led to a Buccaneers field goal. Kris Jenkins added a sack on the day, and TJ Slaton had a tackle for loss, along with a fumble recovery later on. Meanwhile, center Evan Brown had his hands full with a massive defensive tackle in Deone Walker during the Texans’ Week 1 loss to Buffalo. Rookie Keylan Rutledge played well at one guard spot for the Texans, but Ed Ingram had an inconsistent game on the other side. There will be opportunities for the Bengals’ interior defensive line to create havoc and get plenty of pressure on CJ Stroud. If they can do that, they will be what helps the Bengals to win the aforementioned turnover battle.

title: 9 questions with Bengals WR Ja’Marr Chase
summary: We recently had a unique opportunity to chat virtually with Bengals star receiver Ja’Marr Chase. Fabletics and Chase’s new partnership with the activewear brand made this opportunity possible. In conjunction with The Orange and Black Insider podcast, its hosts Anthony Cosenza and John Sheeran, as well as with Cincy Jungle and A to Z Sports, […]
full_text: We recently had a unique opportunity to chat virtually with Bengals star receiver Ja’Marr Chase. Fabletics and Chase’s new partnership with the activewear brand made this opportunity possible. In conjunction with The Orange and Black Insider podcast, its hosts Anthony Cosenza and John Sheeran, as well as with Cincy Jungle and A to Z Sports, Fabletics gave us an opportunity to have a back-and-forth with the team’s star receiver. We fired off questions to “Uno” as the season kicked off, and he gave us his thoughts on a number of topics pertaining to the team. The Bengals are 1-0 and are seemingly heading in a great direction for the season. Chase is and will continue to be a major component of the team’s success. You’ve been very open about the expectations surrounding the Bengals this year. With the additions Cincinnati made on defense, particularly Dexter Lawrence, what feels different about this team heading into 2026 compared with the teams you’ve been part of in the past? JC: It just feels like we’re more complete. We know what we can do on offense, and adding guys like Dex on defense helps take us to that next level. He makes his presence known every day in practice. The foundation is there, now we’ve just got to go win. You’ve accomplished virtually everything individually that a receiver can accomplish, but the Super Bowl remains the obvious team goal. Has your mindset changed at all as you’ve gotten further into your career in terms of balancing individual success with that bigger goal? JC: At this point, winning is what matters. I want a Super Bowl. That’s always the goal. Everything else comes with that. You and Joe Burrow have been together since 2021, and your connection has obviously become one of the defining QB-receiver relationships in the NFL. Is there still a part of that relationship or your on-field chemistry that you feel you can take to another level in 2026? JC: For sure. There’s always more. Me and Joe have been doing this a long time, so we know what the other one is thinking. But we’re never satisfied. We can always get better, make more plays and keep pushing each other. That’s the fun part of the game. Joe Burrow said he’s getting 2019 LSU vibes from this team. What do you remember about the leadup to that season, and do you also feel something similar now with the Bengals? JC: Back then, we knew we had something special before everybody else did. It was just about going out and proving it. I feel some of that now. We know what we’ve got in this locker room. Now we’ve got to show it on the field. After a full training camp going up against DJ Turner II, how does he challenge you in practice and how do you feel you’ve helped each other get better? JC: DJ competes. He’s fast, he’s physical, and he’s going to make you work every rep. That’s what you want in practice. I make him better, he makes me better. We’re going at it every day. With Dohnte Meyers officially making the team, what has impressed you the most about him this offseason? JC: He comes in ready to work, competes and isn’t scared of the moment. I like that about him. He earned his spot. At this point in your career, defenses obviously know exactly what you’re capable of. What part of being Ja’Marr Chase on a football field has become more of a mental game for you — recognizing coverages, manipulating defenders, understanding what Joe is seeing — rather than simply relying on athletic ability? JC: It’s a lot more mental now. They know what I’m trying to do, I know what they’re trying to do. So it’s like, alright, who’s gonna win? I’m watching where the safety is, how the DB is playing me, where the help is coming from. Me and Joe usually see the same thing, so I already know where I need to be. Then it’s just setting the DB up. Make him think he’s got me figured out, then give him something different. That’s the fun part for me now. You think you know what’s coming? Cool. Stop it. Your Fabletics partnership is pretty different from a traditional athlete endorsement because you’ve had a significant hand in the actual creative process. What was something in the collection where you said, “That’s got to be changed,” and what did you ultimately get them to do? JC: I care about what I wear. On the field, in the gym, wherever. It’s got to look right and feel right. That’s what I like about working with Fabletics. I actually get to be in it. I’m not just putting my name on something. I’m wearing it, testing it, telling them what I think. For me, it’s always about fit, and I’m picky about that. Something can look good, but if I put it on and it doesn’t move right or sit the way I want, I’m gonna say something. But it’s also about having the right pieces, all the way down to the stuff people forget. Accessories are where a lot of brands stop paying attention. That’s where I pushed hardest. I wanted a skull cap. I wanted a balaclava. Things I’m actually reaching for in December in Cincinnati, not just things that look good in a photo. Fabletics ran with all of it, and now that’s some of the gear I’m most excited about. The phrase “Chasing No One” has been associated with your Fabletics collection. What does that phrase mean to you personally at this stage of your career? JC: I’m really just focused on being better than I was yesterday. That’s it. I’m not watching what everybody else is doing. I know what I can do, and I know I can still get better. So, I’m chasing the best version of me. Numéro uno. Our thanks to Ja’Marr Chase and Fabletics for this exclusive opportunity. title: 3 X-Factors for the Browns clash with the Buccaneers in Week 2
summary: The Cleveland Browns will try to finish their two-game Florida road trip on a positive note as the team will travel to Tampa Bay to play the Buccaneers this Sunday. For the Browns, it’s all about trying to bounce back after a rough season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars. As a collective, the Browns didn’t […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - NOVEMBER 27: Tristan Wirfs #78 and Shaq Mason #69 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers block Taven Bryan #99 of the Cleveland Browns during the second half at FirstEnergy Stadium on November 27, 2022 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Cleveland Browns will try to finish their two-game Florida road trip on a positive note as the team will travel to Tampa Bay to play the Buccaneers this Sunday . For the Browns, it’s all about trying to bounce back after a rough season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars. As a collective, the Browns didn’t play well at all, and it doesn’t get much easier as they will play a Buccaneers team that will have a highly motivated quarterback in Baker Mayfield . Here are three X-Factors for Browns vs Bucs in Week 2: Zac Robinson vs Mike Rutenberg In terms of debuts for coordinators in new situations, both Zac Robinson and Mike Rutenberg would’ve like to have done things differently. However, if people don’t know by now, Rutenberg and Robinson have history. Both Robinson and Rutenberg were with the Atlanta Falcons last year under former Falcons head coach Raheem Morris (who is now the San Francisco 49ers defensive coordinator). Robinson was the offensive coordinator and Rutenberg was the defensive passing game coordinator. Robinson had his issues against the Cincinnati Bengals, mainly in terms of communication when it came to relaying the plays, but he called a somewhat competent game. Rutenberg, on the other hand, struggled. The Browns defense spent more time playing zone coverage rather than man coverage, which led to frequent coverage busts. The players have to execute, but the defensive coordinator has to put the players in better situations. Familiarity is well known between the two, but Rutenberg has to call a better game defensively and make life difficult for Tampa Bay’s offense. Browns DBs vs Bucs WRs In terms of matchups, this one will be one to monitor. Browns cornerback Denzel Ward was the only cornerback that played well last week against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Cornerback Myles Harden struggled mightily, while Tyson Campbell’s performance wasn’t nearly as poor as Harden’s; it wasn’t great. This week doesn’t get any easier. Ward will likely be matched up with Buccaneers wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, Campbell will likely be tasked against Jalen McMillan or rookie Ted Hurst, Myles Harden will be tasked against Chris Godwin. It’s hard to imagine the secondary playing any worse than they did last week but the Bucs have versatility in the wide receiver room. Campbell’s questionable status for the game could create other issues. It’s possible that the cornerbacks will have to play more zone due to the lack of a consistent pass rush. It’s not necessarily ideal, but due to the pass rush not being there, they might not have a choice. Cleveland Defensive Line vs Tampa’s Offensive Line By the Browns standards, their defensive line didn’t perform to the level that they are capable of in Week 1. The pass rush was nonexistent, and the run defense was questionable at best. Tampa’s offensive line had an uneven performance, as the pass blocking wasn’t up to standard, but the run blocking was solid in their opening contest. As for the Browns, the pass rush needs to be better. It’s simple as that. Pressure was going to fall off after the team traded away Myles Garrett; it’s the reality of the situation. However, Jared Verse, who they traded for in the Garrett deal, wasn’t the best defensive lineman for the Browns that day. That was Mason Graham. Aside from quarterback play, the game will be determined in the trenches, and both units (who had lackluster debuts) will look for redemption this week. The Browns are 8.5-point underdogs against the Bengals, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Here are my favorite player prop bets from the Browns’ perspective in Week 2. Browns vs. Buccaneers Best NFL player prop bets Harold Fannin Over 35.5 Receiving Yards (-114) The Bengals’ tight ends combined for 8 catches for 97 yards and 1 touchdown against the Buccaneers’ defense. Last year, Harold Fannin led the Browns in receiving, and had 36+ receiving yards in 10 of his 16 games, while averaging 6.7 targets per game. In the opener, he was targeted just 3 times. Late in the second half, he finally caught 2 passes for 21 yards, and continued to show that ability to break tackles. If the coaching staff is trying to target things that got away from them, then not getting Fannin involved should be near the top of the list. I expect Fannin to be leveraged early this week, and with the Buccaneers’ defense, he’ll get over 35.5 receiving yards. RB Raheim Sanders Over 8.5 Rushing Yards (-114) The rushing distribution last week saw Quinshon Judkins get 12 carries, and other running backs ( Raheim Sanders ) get just 1. Then, non-quarterbacks had 9 carries, between Deshaun Watson and KC Concepcion . With Dylan Sampson out for awhile, Sanders becomes the backup running back and should get a boost in stock. He also had a nice kickoff return last week and caught several passes, but I’d look for him to get 3+ carries this week too. You’d *hope* that he’d be able to gain 9+ yards with those reps. Deshaun Watson over 175.5 yards passing (-114) I know we don’t like to hear things like, “ Deshaun Watson looked less tentative in the first game,” because we’re sick of coddling him. However, I was saying that throughout training camp. That doesn’t mean he’s also a good decision-maker, as evidenced by him throwing the same interception on the first drive last week that he threw all of camp, but he does seem a bit more sure about pulling the trigger. Good or bad, that should lead to some decent statistical days, like last week, even if the play itself is utter crap. In other words, you can be right about him sucking, but also take advantage of the eventual stat padding via the air (over 175.5 passing yards). title: Browns vs. Buccaneers Predictions: Baker Mayfield faces a Cleveland team that is down, but are they out?
summary: This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Below, we analyze a few advantages, disadvantages, or general thoughts about the two teams before getting to our predictions for the game. Rose-Colored Glasses If I was trying to be completely optimistic despite the horrible performance in Week 1, what would I say? Maybe […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 22: A Cleveland Browns fan holds up a Baker Mayfield giant head cutout during the game against the Baltimore Ravens at FirstEnergy Stadium on December 22, 2019 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Below, we analyze a few advantages, disadvantages, or general thoughts about the two teams before getting to our predictions for the game. Rose-Colored Glasses If I was trying to be completely optimistic despite the horrible performance in Week 1, what would I say? Maybe Deshaun Watson did just need to knock off more rust after being out of action for almost two years, coming off two Achilles injuries. Maybe with how bad the defense played, the defensive coordinator won’t be stubborn about sticking with what sucked and is more likely to make radical adjustments. It was an ass-whipping so bad that even a stubborn coaching staff can’t say, “it wasn’t our day.” It has to be something you address immediately to try to recognize your mistakes, own them, and think of ways to fix them. Like, for example, when Travis Switzer (see the quick hitters section) talks about how they adjusted things in practice to quicken things up and hopefully prevent delay of game penalties. Cleveland actually got some really solid efforts from the whole offensive line and their rookie receivers last week. Special teams also showed some promise. Shake off the bad, and maybe you find yourself in a competitive game this week. The Reality There’s actually some truth embedded in portions of the first section above, but in summary, the execution of Deshaun Watson and the defense in general last week were both abysmal. As I said earlier in the week, for Watson, the fans could overlook some of his mistakes, if it weren’t for the fact that we’ve been dealing with the same story for years now. Nothing has changed. Baker Mayfield squares off against the Browns for the second time, the first being when he was with the Panthers a few years ago. I root for Mayfield any time he plays; I feel like he’s still a Brown, which goes to show you just how much this organization f’ed up with their quarterback handling a few years ago. You had your quarterback of the future, and you dumped him for absolute dogs*#t. The Jaguars have grown into an efficient, well-oiled machine on offense, coupled with Trevor Lawrence making some outstanding individual plays. The Buccaneers are different. I view them as a scrappy offense that relies consistently on the heroics of Mayfield to get them somewhere. Sometimes, it’s awesome and pays off. Other times, it leads to turnovers as he tried to do too much. The Browns’ defense is probably what concerns me most heading into this game. What we saw last week was horrible, and nothing like the defense that I expected to still dominate oppositions this year. It’s certainly possible that they quickly get back to what we thought they would be, but if we see another game of them being lost, it’s going to be a long season. I think Cleveland’s offense has a chance to be better this week, because we saw the ingredients of other pieces of the offense playing well. Despite how much we hate Watson, there are some days where he can play up to an average level. Quinshon Judkins needs to be a lot better this week. He gets somewhat of a pass for the first game, due to the Jaguars’ statistical run defense ranking from a year ago. On offense, I hope we see Isaiah Bond get some more reps than Tylan Wallace . On defense, I’m looking to see if Maliek Collins’ reps go up, while Adin Huntington’s reps go down. I also want to see more of Emmanuel McNeil-Warren . According to FanDuel , the Browns are 8.5 point underdogs against the Buccaneers. The over/under is 41.5. Quick Hitters Defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg gave some vague answers about the defense playing more zone than man in the first game: “You know, again, it’s all about getting the players in the best position. Sometimes zone turns out to be man. Sometimes man can have zone feels. And the truth is, collectively, we’re going to do everything we can to put our best effort forward on Sunday. And again, starting with yesterday’s practice today and focusing then on tomorrow’s practice.” Offensive coordinator Travis Switzer talked about some of the procedural things they adjusted in practice this week, to help prevent things like delay of games: “…like this week, we cut the play clock down a little bit in practice. We’re going to do all the subs from the sideline. So, those are things that we’re doing now to try to address those things. But yeah, I would agree, and I didn’t see it coming either. It wasn’t like it was a daily issue, certainly. But those are kind of the things we’re doing moving forward to address that.” Special teams coordinator Byron Storer was asked about the success with RB Raheim Sanders getting a 74-yard kick return last week, and he praised several blockers for helping make it possible: “Yeah, it was really a combination of Mike (Michael) Burton, Tylan Wallace, Blake Whiteheart, and then Malachi getting the block right there at the end to seal it. It was a fun play, and now I feel like I’m so far removed from it, I’m on to the next one. But it’s a testament to the guys blocking up front, and then Rocket going out there, trusting his eyes and hitting it, and showing the speed that he has out there.” Here are predictions from multiple staff members at DBN: Predictions Chris Pokorny: “I didn’t have faith the Browns would actually win last week, but I picked them to try to have some positive mojo to begin the season. Being down 24-0 early in the second quarter set the tone that there is no optimism to be had right now. Cleveland may improve upon some things, but being beaten like that can take an immediate toll on confidence. We’ve also seen headlines about the players not being in on Watson. So for whatever marginal improvements there might be, no one in their right mind can legitimately point to a reason why Cleveland should win this week.” Buccaneers 24, Browns 14 Curtiss Brown: “I understand people want to dunk on the Browns and get their jokes off but let’s be real. Yes, the Browns played atrocious last week. That’s not an opinion it’s a fact. However, they aren’t the only team that played poorly in their season opener. It’s only magnified because it’s Cleveland. I know they played poorly but the Miami Dolphins looked bad, same can be said for the Tennessee Titans. As far as the game goes, this is Baker Mayfield’s second revenge game against his former team (he lost the first one when he was in Carolina with the Carolina Panthers). If Baker can’t outplay Deshaun Watson (which isn’t hard to do) then that’s on him. Offensively, asking Watson to look competent seems too big of a task for him. Offensive line blocked well enough in pass protection but the run blocking is a work in progress. Defensively, I am giving the defense some form of grace for last week because its a lot of moving parts but their performance still needs to be better by their standards. The players know it and they held themselves accountable for it. Overall, this team can’t look worse than did they did last week. I’m not saying they are going to win this game (because they wont) but I expect the execution to be better. The effort wasn’t lacking. Whether Baker Mayfield gets his revenge or not, doesn’t matter because he had an opportunity in 2022 to get it and he failed. Pressure is on him to not be as reckless as he was last week. Don’t know what to expect from this game to be honest but most fans are expecting Tampa Bay to blow Cleveland out. I don’t see it. Maybe I’m wrong.” Buccaneers 26, Browns 16 Barry Shuck: “It looks like it will be another rough afternoon for the Browns and their “rusty” offense. Recently retired , Chubb’s on-field resume may not match up with Hall of Famer Joe Thomas or DE Myles Garrett , especially with his single-season sack record , but the way he played, the hard work he put in, and the character ( including “Batman” ) have a special place in our hearts. title: Important Cowboys vs Commanders storylines on Sunday
summary: I don’t think anyone expected things to go the way they did in the Dallas Cowboys vs. New York Giants game. Without dwelling too much on a game in the rearview mirror, the Dallas defense caught many by surprise considering the overhaul over the offseason. Guys like Jalen Thompson, Rashan Gary, and Caleb Downs were […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - OCTOBER 19: Ceedee Lamb #88 of the Dallas Cowboys is brought down by Quan Martin #20 of the Washington Commanders during a game at AT&T Stadium on October 19, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images I don’t think anyone expected things to go the way they did in the Dallas Cowboys vs. New York Giants game. Without dwelling too much on a game in the rearview mirror, the Dallas defense caught many by surprise considering the overhaul over the offseason. Guys like Jalen Thompson, Rashan Gary, and Caleb Downs were supposed to usher in something different. Unfortunately, it was more of the same. Here’s the good news. It was Week 1. The Cowboys still have 16 regular-season games left, and they have plenty of time to turn things around. They have to do it in a must-win way this week against the Washington Commanders. Here are five points to watch for as the game kicks off on Sunday. First point: More of the same? Heading into their matchup with the Giants, one of last week’s five points was limiting Jaxson Dart in the running game. The Cowboys had 54 yards on the ground to Dart, averaging almost five yards per carry. Dart’s ability to scramble kept Dallas’ defense on the field, which we all know how that went. The Cowboys have another quarterback coming up on Sunday who can hurt them with his legs: Jayden Daniels. Last week against the Philadelphia Eagles, Daniels didn’t run for as many yards as Dart did in Dallas, but he was an effective runner when he had the opportunity or needed to make a play. He had five carries for 31 yards, averaging over six yards every time he would run. Dallas needs to make sure last week’s mistake doesn’t happen again, because it’ll lead to more of the same, with the Commanders extending drives and keeping the Cowboys offense on the sidelines. Second point: The terror twins or the DeVille twins Somehow, someway, the Cowboys need to get CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens the ball early and often against the Commanders. Brian Schottenheimer has talked about wanting to run the ball and set the tone, but the team’s real playmakers are on the outside. On a great day, both wideouts can have over 100 yards each and be a terror to opposing defenses. Against the Giants, it just seemed like Pickens and Prescott weren’t always on the same page, and we’ve seen how Lamb can take time to get going if things don’t go his way early in a game. The best version of Lamb and Pickens earned them the nickname “the terror twins.” That version of the duo needs to be on display vs. the Commanders’ smaller cornerbacks. Last year against the Commanders at AT&T Stadium, Lamb went for 110 receiving yards and Pickens had 85. Both players averaged over 20 yards per catch. What we don’t need to see are the DeVille twins, which, if anyone has seen the show Rugrats , you know what I’m talking about. Third point: A rookie DC in DC The Commanders have the same question at defensive coordinator as the Cowboys do: Is this moment too big for them? Head coach Dan Quinn went out and hired two first-time coordinators on both sides of the ball this offseason, which could make him look like a genius or get him fired. Washington’s DC should be a familiar name to Cowboys fans since he was in the running for the same position with Dallas: Daronte Jones. He spent most of his coaching career with the Minnesota Vikings and learned under Brian Flores over the last three seasons. Unlike Christian Parker, Jones was actually a defensive coordinator in college in 2021 for LSU. That was his only season holding the position. Against the Eagles, the Commanders defense looked good and got the Philly offense out of rhythm on multiple drives. However, a few explosive plays happened where it looked like the secondary didn’t know what was going on (sound familiar). It’ll be interesting to see the storylines coming out of the game because one of these teams will be 0-2, with a ton of questions surrounding their first-time defensive coordinators and whether they were the right guys for the job. Fourth point: Reading between the linebackers Before offseason training and the NFL draft, the Cowboys’ linebacking corps was seen as a glaring need, even with Jaishawn Barham and Dee Winters coming aboard. DeMarvion Overshown’s health was a question, and Dallas needed to keep developing second-year pro Shemar James. As time went on, the questions around linebacker seemed to shift towards the pass rush and secondary. We should have stuck with our first instincts. With Overshown leaving Week 1 with a hamstring injury that could cost him one to two weeks, the Cowboys linebacker room looks even thinner heading into Week 2. Barham could be called upon as the next man up with green-dot responsibilities , but with growing concerns about the defense’s ability to communicate calls properly, should a rookie be trusted to make the right calls? Dallas has Curtis Robinson and Justin Barron on the practice squad and could elevate one of them to the active roster for Sunday, but they aren’t on the same level as Overshown to fill the void. The Cowboys were impressed by what they saw from Barham all offseason and in the first preseason game. If that player is still there, which he should be, the Dallas defense will need him in a big way this weekend. Fifth point: Kicking and screaming No need to panic; this is an under-the-radar point my colleague RJ Ochoa brought up on Twitter . Dating back to last season, Dallas Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey has now missed a kick of some kind (field goal or extra point) in 3 straight games. This is the first time in his career he has a 3-game streak of such kind. Aubrey is one of, if not the best, kickers in the NFL. However, if the defense struggles to start the season and the offense needs to score as many points as possible in their opportunities, missing kicks can’t happen. Questions lingered about the special teams unit’s performance last year under Nick Sorensen, and doubt remains about his return this offseason. Sorensen stuck around, and so far, after one game, the special teams unit has not looked any better in year two. Aubrey signed a historic deal this offseason, and deservedly so. But if he starts missing critical kicks in games that could come down to three points, it could raise alarm bells about what’s happened to one of the league’s most clutch kickers.

title: Cowboys news: Jaishawn Barham to start at middle linebacker, wear green dot
summary: Despite a frustrating rookie debut, the Dallas Cowboys will give the green dot to linebacker Jaishawn Barham as he starts in place of the injured DeMarvion Overshown. full_text: Despite a frustrating rookie debut, the Dallas Cowboys will give the green dot to linebacker Jaishawn Barham as he starts in place of the injured DeMarvion Overshown. Another rookie, safety Caleb Downs, performed very well against the Giants, but he’s looking to take his play to an even higher plateau. All-Pro wide receiver CeeDee Lamb didn’t have the performance in Week 1 he wanted, but he’s chomping at the bit to play inside AT&T Stadium this Sunday. Starting the season 0-2 in the NFL is all but a guarantee that a team won’t make the playoffs, and Dallas desperately wants to avoid that as well as getting a second loss in NFC East play. Why Brian Schottenheimer, Cowboys trust rookie Jaishawn Barham in first start at MLB – Calvin Watkins, Dallas Morning News Jaishawn Barham didn’t have the best game in his first taste of NFL action. However, with DeMarvion Overshown on the shelf, he’ll get the start on Sunday against the Commanders. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer made it official Friday when he named Jaishawn Barham the starting middle linebacker for the home opener against the Washington Commanders . Starter DeMarvion Overshown is out for the game with a hamstring strain, suffered in the season opener against the New York Giants. “He’s got great command of what we’re doing,” Schottenheimer said of Barham. “Again, had to get into a little teaching moment this morning on the radio. Again, the green dot, I think gets overblown at times, basically what you’re doing, you’re repeating the call and then you’re setting the fronts and all that. And then the entire defense needs to communicate.” Caleb Downs looking to build off NFL debut vs. Commanders – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Caleb Downs was among the best defensive players on the Cowboys in their loss to the Giants in Week 1. Now, as the Commanders come to Dallas, he wants to be even better. Cowboys first-round pick Caleb Downs rarely came off the field in his NFL debut last Sunday against the Giants, playing 60 defensive snaps and tallying seven tackles, three quarterback pressures and a sack. On Sunday, Downs will take the field for his first game at AT&T Stadium as a Cowboy, where he’s aiming to build off his start to the year. “Excitement, honestly,” Downs said about Sunday’s game. “It’s the best feeling to be able to play this game. There’s no really other way to feel about it then just straight joy. I’m excited to do that, and we’re excited to do what we need to do to get a win.” Cowboys looking to avoid the wrong side of history in Sunday’s home opener – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram The Cowboys will try to avoid an 0-2 start on Sunday. If not, history shows that they’ll likely be in for a long and disappointing season. Since 1990, only 35 of 287 NFL teams that have started 0-2 have made the playoffs. Of those 35 teams, only four have lost both games to divisional opponents. The Dallas Cowboys will look to avoid having to make that same kind of history this season, as they look to get in the win column for the first time against the Washington Commanders in the home opener on Sunday afternoon in Arlington. Dallas Cowboys’ Friday Injury Report Includes Two Sidelined Starters – Randy Gurzi, SI.com Dallas will be without a couple of key defenders this weekend. A few others dealing with ailments were full participants on Friday. Malik Hooker went down with a forearm injury, which was later deemed to be a fracture that would force him out for a few weeks. Also injured in the loss was linebacker DeMarvion Overshown , who suffered a hamstring injury. Neither will play this weekend against the Washington Commanders , but the good news is that Friday’s injury report from practice is thin beyond Hooker and Overshown. CeeDee Lamb ‘can’t wait’ for chance to bounce back in home opener vs. Commanders – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com Lamb only had 44 yards on five receptions against the Giants. With the Cowboys staring at an 0-2 hole, he’s ready to have his first big performance of 2026. “Can’t wait. Can’t wait,” the three-time All-Pro receiver said. “ I know the city gonna be rocking. The game iss gonna be fire. I can’t wait to just go out there and have everybody excited, score a couple of touchdowns and blow the roof off the place.” The urgency to dictate terms against the incoming Commanders must also fuel the Cowboys toward getting a fast start, something they failed to do by going three-and-out on their first offensive series from scrimmage at MetLife Stadium. 3 Keys: Big-play shots must return for Cowboys to beat Commanders – Reid D Hanson, Cowboys Wire There’s a lot that the Cowboys have to fix from their performance in their season opener. Here are three things that need to happen. Key No. 1: Stop the run Filed under, “easier said than done,” stopping the run has to be the first priority for the Cowboys this week. Washington ranked right around league average in rushing EPA last week, but they faced off against a talented Philadelphia defense and largely kept their biggest threat, Jayden Daniels, holstered and underutilized. The Commanders pose a much bigger threat on the ground than the numbers indicate, and the Cowboys have to be ready. Daily discussion question: What is the best way that tomorrow can go?

title: Commanders have been ‘get right’ opponent for Cowboys before
summary: The 2026 Dallas Cowboys were supposed to find themselves in better positions to compete in all phases compared to the 7-9-1 campaign of a year ago. Instead, after one game, they find themselves in eerily similar position ahead of a week two divisional game at home. Last season began with a primetime road loss by […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - OCTOBER 19: Donovan Ezeiruaku #41 of the Dallas Cowboys lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the Washington Commanders at AT&T Field on October 19, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 Dallas Cowboys were supposed to find themselves in better positions to compete in all phases compared to the 7-9-1 campaign of a year ago. Instead, after one game, they find themselves in eerily similar position ahead of a week two divisional game at home. Last season began with a primetime road loss by one score to a NFC East rival, putting the Cowboys in a bit of a “prove it or lose it” spot back in their home stadium against another division opponent, the Giants, in week two. The Cowboys won that game ugly in overtime, and it felt ominous for how this team would play against better competition. If things were at least slightly optimistic following last year’s close week one loss to the reigning Super Bowl champions, this week has been a category five hurricane that has fans ready to jump ship if the Cowboys do anything less than beat the Commanders handily. Yes, a Commanders team that was just within a few plays of beating the Eagles on the road in their first outing. Luckily, the Cowboys have used recent games against the Commanders in this way before, as Sunday will be the fifth time they go up against their former defensive coordinator Dan Quinn since he became the Commanders’ head coach in 2024. Dallas is 3-1 in these games scoring at least 30 points in each win, and the one loss was Week 18 of 2024 when Trey Lance started for Dak Prescott. That game was also the Commanders’ first win in Arlington since Thanksgiving of 2020. Last season, the Cowboys came into the home game against the Commanders off a deflating, one-score road loss to the Panthers. The defense was bad, wasn’t even put in position to succeed if they wanted to in critical moments of the game, and the offense made costly mistakes. Sound familiar? The Cowboys responded with a 44-22 win against the Commanders, a season high for points. Dak Prescott had his second highest yards per attempt of the season, completed 70% of his passes, and threw two touchdowns to Jake Ferguson plus another to CeeDee Lamb. The approach on offense was balanced with 31 rushing attempts, 19 from Javonte Williams for 116 yards and a touchdown, and 30 pass attempts for Prescott. The Cowboys got points on drives that started at their own 34 yard line to start the game, own 40, 46, 45, and 33 to win the battle of field position. As a season long trend the Cowboys were very poor in this area, and that was among the long list of concerns after last week’s Giants game for the current Cowboys too, but taking the ball away from the Commanders twice while also making two stops on fourth downs went a long way. The Cowboys will know what they’re seeing in the Dan Quinn defense, one that remained aggressive but had it’s struggles in week one against the Eagles. After failing to establish Ferguson as a threat against the Giants defense, the Cowboys should be encouraged by Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert leading Philly in catches and yards with two touchdowns last Sunday. Both touchdowns came from distance too, one of 17 yards and the other 43. In the Commanders secondary that will look to be the second straight to keep George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb in check, Nick Cross, Amik Robertson, and Mike Sainristill were all at the top of the Commanders box score for tackles against the Eagles. This is normally not a good sign of how well a defense won at the point of attack, and also points to something else that will be familiar for Cowboys fans and coaches alike for this matchup against Quinn, which is defensive backs on an island. In an eight point loss in week one, the Cowboys lost an expected 8.3 points to three costly drops. All of the ingredients are in place for the Cowboys to get all of their skill players involved in the game plan this week, calm down the fan base by getting push in the run game, spreading it around through the air, and flipping the script the Giants used on them by having their own offense control a home game. How many expected points did each team lose on drops in week 1? 1. PIT 11.7 (2 drops) 2. DAL 8.3 (3) 3. DET 6.8 (2) 4. ARI 5.1 (3) 5. IND 4.0 (3) Drops charted by @FTNFantasy pic.twitter.com/XRX9D5l1PH — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) September 16, 2026 The other win for the Cowboys against the Commanders last year came on Christmas Day. This time around they were coming in off a season-worst three-game losing streak. A Week 14 Thursday night loss at the Lions felt like the official end to vague playoff hopes, but another primetime loss the following week at home to the Vikings followed by a no-show type performance and loss to the Chargers had the feeling around Christmas anything but jolly. Dallas had already played on Thanksgiving and beaten the Chiefs, but there was little reason to expect more holiday cheer in this game. The Cowboys caught a break with the Commanders having an injury at quarterback, something that’s been a theme of this rivalry as of late, starting veteran journeyman Josh Johnson. Washington went 1-6 on third down and 1-3 scoring touchdowns in the red zone, seeing Dallas come in and win 30-23. KaVontae Turpin scored an 86-yard touchdown down the middle of the field in the second quarter to push the Cowboys lead to 21-3. This upcoming game should be an opportunity for Christian Parker’s defense and the Cowboys to keep the ball in front of them, play downhill at linebacker, and win their matchups on the outside. Anything short of this with the Commanders offense picking up where the Giants left off in confusing and physically outperforming the Cowboys defense would be a serious letdown. If there’s a very general, overall takeaway from week one in the books around the NFL, it’s that coaching is at an all-time importance in games being decided by a razor’s margin. We already said that this week has been toxic around the Cowboys fanbase, but it hasn’t quite reached outcries for the likes of Schottenheimer, Parker, or other coaches to lose their jobs. The same can’t be said for Quinn in Washington who has had the feel of outstaying his welcome for a little bit now within that fanbase, and this also needs to be an area the Cowboys win the Xs and Os battle this week to preserve the optimism of this season. Speaking of, the last time the Cowboys started 0-2 was 2010, which was also the last time they made an in-season coaching change from Wade Phillips to Jason Garrett. Even that year’s Cowboys team beat Washington at home for win number five of six that season. The Cowboys have not started a season 0-2 with both losses coming against division opponents since 2000, the second to last year of the Cardinals being in the East. Dallas lost at home to Philadelphia in week one and in Arizona week two. That Dave Campo led Cowboys team finished with even fewer wins than 2010 with five, and even they had two against Washington. The Cowboys need this game in the worst way in their first appearance on America’s Game of the Week on FOX.

title: Cowboys vs Commanders: 3 causes for concern in Week 2
summary: While it’s only Week 2, Sunday’s contest between the Washington Commanders and Dallas Cowboys is virtually a must-win for both sides. Since the 2015 season, just 14.7% of teams that started 0-2 (14 of 95) ended up making the playoffs. After the poor display they put on the field in New York, the Cowboys have […]
full_text: While it’s only Week 2, Sunday’s contest between the Washington Commanders and Dallas Cowboys is virtually a must-win for both sides. Since the 2015 season, just 14.7% of teams that started 0-2 (14 of 95) ended up making the playoffs. After the poor display they put on the field in New York, the Cowboys have plenty to be concerned about in this matchup. With that thought in mind, here are three causes for concern in Week 2 against the Commanders. 1) Jayden Daniels’ rushing ability The Commanders are expecting a big-time bounce-back from 25-year-old quarterback Jayden Daniels this season. After putting together one of the best rookie years in NFL history, Daniels had an up-and-down sophomore season plagued by injuries. If Washington wants any chance at making the postseason, they need Daniels on the field and at his best. While Washington took a loss in their Week 1 matchup against Philadelphia, Daniels looked healthy and had a productive day against one of the NFL’s elite defenses. If the 25-year-old is healthy, he’s one of the most dangerous athletes at the quarterback position in all of football. Against Philadelphia, Daniels got back to using his legs as a weapon, rushing for 31 yards on five attempts. This week, the Cowboys will need to place plenty of emphasis on taking away Daniels’ ability to take off and run. In three career games against Dallas, Daniels has averaged a little over 42 rushing yards per game. The whole world saw Jaxson Dart burn the Cowboys on the ground multiple times last Sunday, and you can imagine Washington is going to incorporate plenty of quarterback runs into their offensive game plan this week. 2) Washington’s ability to stop the run One positive to come out of the Commanders’ Week 1 loss was how well they kept Philadelphia’s impressive run game in check. While the Eagles did record 136 total rushing yards on the day, 64 of those yards came on two runs by Saquon Barkley and Jalen Hurts. If you take away Barkley’s big run of 42 yards, Washington held the talented running back to just 41 yards on 14 carries, an average of 2.9 Y/A. On the day, the Commanders’ defense ranked 10th in the league in defensive Rush EPA (-01.67) and third in defensive Rush SR (26.3%). To avoid letting Dallas open things up in the play-action game, Washington will likely follow their Week 1 game plan against Philly and put heavy emphasis on slowing Dallas down on the ground. The Cowboys will need to execute better in the run game than they did in Week 1, when, as a team, they averaged just 3.8 Y/A. 3) 0-2 Potential playoff implications As we mentioned at the top, falling to 0-2 is basically the kiss of death to your playoff hopes. To make matters worse, whatever team loses this game will not just have a 0-2 record overall but in the division as well. This would make it very difficult for that team to win any potential divisional tiebreaks come season’s end. Since 2015, only one team (the 2025 Chicago Bears) has lost their first two games of the season to divisional opponents and still went on to win their division that year. It’s safe to say there will be plenty of urgency on both sides to win this game. With Dallas’ brutal upcoming five-game stretch, it is absolutely paramount they find a way to win on Sunday and avoid digging themselves into an early-season hole too deep to climb out of.
author: Matthew Holleran

title: Cowboys want a better defense, but the Commanders might have got one
summary: Time for a bounce-back game from the Dallas Cowboys. If that is to happen, it will come at the expense of the Washington Commanders. To see if that might happen, we checked in with Andrew Y. over at Hogs Haven for the lowdown on the Commanders heading into the second week of the season. Blogging […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - DECEMBER 25: Noah Igbinoghene #6 of the Washington Commanders tackles George Pickens #3 of the Dallas Cowboys in the first quarter of a game at Northwest Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images Time for a bounce-back game from the Dallas Cowboys. If that is to happen, it will come at the expense of the Washington Commanders. To see if that might happen, we checked in with Andrew Y. over at Hogs Haven for the lowdown on the Commanders heading into the second week of the season. Blogging The Boys: What were some of the best things that you saw from the Commanders in the first game versus Philadelphia that bode well for the season? Hogs Haven: I think the first thing almost any Commanders fan would say is the performance of the defense. Last year, the Commanders had one of the worst defenses in the NFL, so they completely overhauled it in the offseason, with a new DC in Daronte Jones (who brings an attacking Flores-like scheme) and replacing over half of the starters on defense. Early returns indicate the overhaul has paid off. The defense was living in the Eagles backfield last Sunday, generating a 48.48% pressure rate on Jalen Hurts and a 24% TFL rate, both notably higher than NFL average. On offense, things were a bit of a mixed bag, but there were a few positives. Other fans may disagree, but I saw a lot of positives in the way Jayden Daniels played. He played like more of a pocket QB, avoiding pressure by navigating the pocket and avoiding pressure like a ninja while keeping his eyes downfield. He didn’t make a lot of connections passing until the 4th quarter, but I blame that more on the playcalling and the quality of the Eagles defense. Playing from the pocket instead of breaking the pocket when nothing is immediately available should do a better job of keeping Jayden healthy. It was also notable that the OL played competently. A lot of people were worried that with the injury to Laremy Tunsil and former backup IOL Nick Allegretti starting at Center that the OL would be one of the worst in the league and would prevent the offense from functioning. I don’t think that was the case. The OL seemed competent, perhaps more at the league average level. That was a win compared to expectations. BTB: On the flip side, what were some of the most concerning things to occur? HH : Despite the defense playing aggressively and getting quite a few stops, they also gave up quite some big plays. In fact, they gave up 171 of the Eagles’ 318 total yards on just four plays . Mostly these seemed like they were caused by individual players making a mental mistake and I’m hoping it gets cleaned up with more time in the scheme. However, I think there is an element of truth to the idea that because the Flores-style defense is so aggressive, it can lend itself to allowing big plays by leaving the backend exposed when all the pressure it sends isn’t able to get home. On offense, the biggest concern was Jayden Daniels’ stats in the first half : 37.5 completion percentage, 43 passing yards, 0 touchdowns, 16 rushing yards, and a 45.8 passer rating. It improved in the second half and especially in the 4th quarter, but clearly the offense hasn’t found its groove. Again, I blame this mostly on the playcalling and quality of the Eagles defense, but it needs to improve and our rookie playcaller David Blough needs to learn quickly on the job. It’s also not great that Jayden Daniels had a 50% pressure rate in week 1. BTB: Give us a rundown on a few of the new players in Washington who could make a big impact this season. HH: On offense, I expect WRs Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams to have the biggest impact. Most readers will probably know about Stefon Diggs, who was the biggest FA signing for the Commanders on offense. Antonio Williams was a 3rd-round pick in this year’s NFL draft from Clemson. Williams has generated some buzz through training camp and caught 4-of-4 targets for 64 yards and a TD in week 1. On defense, as mentioned before, over half the defensive starters this year are new to the team. I won’t go through all of them, but the standouts are LB Sonny Styles, S Nick Cross, and EDGE Odafe Oweh.Styles was drafted 7th overall and has lived up to his billing. He was all over the field on Sunday making plays and even steamrolled Saquon Barkley to get a big hit on Jalen Hurts on a blitz. Nick Cross was a physical presence flying all over the field, showing well in coverage while also getting tackles and limiting yardage to the line of scrimmage. Odafe Oweh was the team’s biggest FA signing with a 4-year, $96 million contract. He didn’t have a huge impact in week 1 against the Eagles elite OTs, ending the game with 1 sack, 3 total tackles and a tackle for loss. I would also be remiss if I didn’t mention standout gunner Tyler Owens, who was a maven on special teams and had an angry run that went viral after the game. BTB : Is Dan Quinn’s job in jeopardy this year? What would the Commanders have to do this season to make sure he returns? HH: A lot of fans are ready to eject him right now, but I think the Front Office will be more patient. I think there’s an understanding that the roster was very weak when he took over and in particular had no depth, so it simply couldn’t withstand last year’s rate of injury. Although the injuries weren’t Quinn’s fault, there were also some problems with coaching (particularly on defense), which is what necessitated the change in coordinators, so Quinn deserves some of the blame. I think if the team has another 5 or 6 win season, DQ would definitely be on the chopping block, but if he does better than that, most of the losses are close losses, the team looks mostly well-coached, young players seem to be developing, and (maybe most importantly) Jayden Daniels is developing well and seems to be happy with the coaches, they will probably keep DQ for another year hoping that another offseason infusion of talent and the further development of our rookie coordinators will lead to better results next year. BTB: What is your prediction for the game? How does it play out and who wins? HH: The Cowboys are currently 4.5-point favorites and I rarely predict Vegas to be very wrong, so if I had to make a score prediction, it would be something like 27-24 in favor of the Cowboys. In terms of how the gameflow will work, I’m a bit worried about the Commanders giving up so many explosive plays and the Cowboys having a pair of WRs (and a QB) capable of making explosive plays in the passing game. At the same time, the Commanders run defense was pretty solid most of the time and Javonte Williams isn’t as much of a big-play threat as Saquon, so I think the Cowboys will have to mostly progress through their passing attack. On the Commanders side, I think they should run what worked against the Eagles. Since new DC Christian Parker is a Fangio disciple, maintaining the run-heavy, short passing game that seemed to work best in the 4th quarter of the Eagles game would be the best way to attack. On defense, Daronte Jones should stick with the stunt- and blitz-heavy script that worked against the Eagles, but make sure players execute their responsibilities better on the backend. Thanks for the knowledge, Hogs Haven. Ok BTB, what’s your takeaway from these answers?

title: Advanced stats show Cowboys strengths and weaknesses
summary: Fire the coaches! Cut the players! Churn the roster! Send a message! – It’s hard to avoid hyperbole in the days following a season-opening loss, but we take a dispassionate look at the Giants game anyway. By the numbers, of course. But the numbers come with their own baggage, because we have no way of […]

The Packers defeated the Cowboys 45-7. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-USA TODAY Sports | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Fire the coaches! Cut the players! Churn the roster! Send a message! – It’s hard to avoid hyperbole in the days following a season-opening loss, but we take a dispassionate look at the Giants game anyway. By the numbers, of course. But the numbers come with their own baggage, because we have no way of knowing which numbers are outliers and which numbers are indicative of the coming regular-season performance. In other words, if this had been a Week 8 game, we’d have the previous seven games worth of data to compare against to determine what is an outlier and what is a pattern and would likely be much calmer about a mid-season loss than staring into a dark abyss to start the season. -49.4 Passer Rating Differential (PRD): That’s the difference in passer rating between the Giants (134.2) and the Cowboys (84.8). We know that passer rating differential (PRD) is one of the stats most closely linked to winning in the NFL . And one of the interesting things about PRD is that it can be plugged into a very simple formula to predict win totals in the NFL. The PRD formula (Projected Wins = PRD * 0.16 + 8.5) has shown a fairly close correlation with the Cowboys’ actual wins over the last few years, as the table below illustrates. body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table { border: 1px solid #000 !important; border-collapse: collapse !important; } body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th { padding: 4px 6px !important; } Dallas Cowboys Passer Rating Differential, 2020-2025 Year 2020 2021 2022 2023 2024 2025 PRD -12.8 27.1 1.9 22.0 -17.2 -12.8 Projected Wins 6.5 12.8 8.8 12.0 5.7 6.5 Actual Wins 6 12 12 12 7 7 Projection error 0.5 0.8 3.2 0.0 1.3 0.5 The mean absolute projection error (the average of the absolute deviation between the projected and the actual win total) is quite low at 1.0 for the Cowboys over the last six years using our little formula, a strong indication that the formula is a good projection tool. So what does this mean for the 2026 Cowboys? Sadly, the -49.4 PRD produces a projected 0.6 wins for the 2026 Cowboys. If you’re wondering whether that means the Cowboys are on pace for a 1-16 season, congratulations 🥳🎊🎉 : you’ve just discovered the problem with extrapolating one game across an entire season. Of course, extrapolating one game of PRD across an entire season is statistically ridiculous — which is exactly the point. 73% Third-down efficiency : The Cowboys’ third-down efficiency on offense is one of the highlights of the game. The Cowboys were 8-of-11 on third down, which should bode well for the rest of the season. Too bad the defense was 9-of-11 (82%) on third down. +0.271 EPA/play : Per RBSDM.com , the Cowboys offense ranked fifth overall in EPA/play and eighth in success rate (percent of plays with positive EPA) with 48.3% Unfortunately, the defense ranked 32nd with an EPA/play of 0.363 and 31st in success rate with 59.1% The defensive problems weren’t limited to third downs. In fact, the second-down numbers may be even more revealing. John Owning summarizes : This is the Cowboys defense's performance by down in Week 1, per Sumer Sports. 1st down: 31 plays, 95 yards allowed (3.06 yds/play), and a -0.105 EPA/play for the opposing offense — this was actually a strong down for the defense, giving up only 4 first downs. 2nd down: 26… https://t.co/X3xwA4dEfO — John Owning (@JohnOwning) September 15, 2026 1st down : 31 plays, 95 yards allowed (3.06 yds/play), and a -0.105 EPA/play for the opposing offense — this was actually a strong down for the defense, giving up only 4 first downs. 2nd down : 26 plays, 210 yards allowed (8.08 yds/play), +0.476 EPA/play for the offense, and 13 first downs allowed — a big step down in performance. 3rd down : 11 plays, 89 yards allowed (8.09 yds/play), +0.886 EPA/play for the offense, and 9 first downs allowed out of just 11 plays — meaning they converted a first down on roughly 82% of their third-down snaps against Dallas. I think the issues on 2nd down were just as big, and maybe even bigger, than their issues on third downs 100% red zone percentage . The Cowboys were 3-of-3 on their red zone drives, up from their 56.9% average last year on a topic that had been declared a special area of attention this year. Bummer that the Giants were also 100% in the red zone, but on four drives, not three. 1.10 Yards Per Route Run (YPRR) for Cowboys receivers. YPRR is a football metric that measures a pass catcher’s efficiency by dividing their total receiving yards by the number of passing routes they ran, essentially giving us the average number of receiving yards a player makes every time he runs a route.
