title: Cowboys vs. Commanders: 2 offensive, 2 defensive players who will impact game
summary: It’s difficult to judge who were the impact players for the Dallas Cowboys last week in the season opener due to performing poorly in all three phases the game, but hopefully this week will be different. Hopefully multiple players will step up and make some key plays that helps sway the game in the Cowboys […]
full_text: It’s difficult to judge who were the impact players for the Dallas Cowboys last week in the season opener due to performing poorly in all three phases the game, but hopefully this week will be different. Hopefully multiple players will step up and make some key plays that helps sway the game in the Cowboys favor, securing their first win on the season. Last week we attempted to predict one impact player from both the offensive and defensive side of the ball, choosing WR Ryan Flournoy and DB Caleb Downs. Both made plays, but not quite the game-changing ones we were hoping for. This week we decided to double down by choosing two offensive and defensive players, because Dallas needs all the help they can get. OFFENSE WR CeeDee Lamb After failing to find a rhythm on offense last week against the Giants, the Cowboys need to get back to what they do best, feeding CeeDee Lamb with quick, high percentage passes to move the chains. Once that’s established, everything else should fall in place. From opening up better running lanes to airing it out down the field to George Pickens, No. 88 is still the engine that drives this offense. As such, he should be targeted early and often this week against the Commanders. TE Jake Ferguson After Dallas Goedert shredded the Commanders secondary last week for 77 receiving yards and two touchdowns, look for the Cowboys to exploit that weakness as well in this Week 2 matchup by getting Jake Ferguson much more involved. In the season opener he was only targeted twice and called both passes for a measly six yards. With the attention CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens should command, No. 87 should be able to find some favorable matchups working the middle of field and down the seam. DEFENSE DT Quinnen Williams Quinnen Williams earned the fifth highest PFF grade (77.6) for the Cowboys for his performance last week against the Giants, but didn’t really play up to the standard we expect from him. Maybe he just needed to knock off a little rust after watching from the sideline in preseason or was surprised by the physicality the Giants played with last week. Whatever the reason, we believe a fire will be lit under him and he will look much more the All-Pro DT we’ve seen in the past this week against the Commanders. OLB Donovan Ezeiruaku Donovan Ezeiruaku surprisingly earned the best PFF grade (86.8) from his performance against the Giants. He was Dallas’ leading tackler last week and was pretty impressive against one of the better young, talented LTs Andrew Thomas. We expect even more from him this week going up against an injury fill-in for Laremy Tunsil, Brandon Coleman. Coleman is a solid starting blindside protector, but not nearly as good as what No. 6 squared off against a week ago. Don’t be surprised if he exits Week 2 with multiple QB sacks.
author: Brian Martin

title: Digging into the numbers to predict Cowboys vs Commanders
summary: Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. We’ll look at historical data points as well as more recent numbers. At the end, we’ll add it all up to see what Dallas needs to do to secure a win and which team may have the edge. The history The Cowboys […]
full_text: Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. We’ll look at historical data points as well as more recent numbers. At the end, we’ll add it all up to see what Dallas needs to do to secure a win and which team may have the edge. The history The Cowboys lead the Commanders in head-to-head matchup all-time 81-49-2 . The Dak Prescott-led Cowboys are 13-2 against the Commanders. In five of those wins, Dak was pulled out early with the game locked up well before the end of the fourth quarter. In 15 games, Dak Prescott has thrown for 3,716 yards, 32 touchdowns, five interceptions, and has a passer rating of 107.4 . This is his best passer rating against any team in the NFC East. The most thrilling matchup between the two teams came in week 12 of 2024. This game featured seven scores in just the fourth quarter alone, including an electric kick return touchdown from KaVontae Turpin. Bounce back game? The Cowboys have not started 0-2 since 2010. Dak Prescott is 5-0 in the games immediately following a week one loss. Nearly 90% of teams that start 0-2 go on to miss the playoffs. In 2025, every team that started the season with two losses missed the playoffs. Cowboys key stats from last week Prescott threw for 175 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception. The longest play on offense for the Cowboys went for just 17 yards. The defense allowed a 134.2 passer rating from Jaxson Dart, gave up 165 yards on the ground, and allowed the Giants to chew up enormous amounts of clock on their way to the endzone throughout the game. Commanders key stats from last week Jayden Daniels threw for 164 yards against the Eagles and added another 31 yards on the ground. Philadelphia was able to pressure Daniels on 19 of 38 drop backs, resulting in the quarterback going 3-15 for 26 yards through the air. Against the blitz, Daniels went 5-7 for 47 yards and two touchdowns against Philadelphia’s blitz. The Commanders defense gave up explosive plays of 64 , 43 , 42 , 41 , 22 yards against the Eagles. They had a difficult time covering Dallas Goedert who had four receptions for 77 yards and two touchdowns. What do the numbers mean? The numbers lied to us last week. There were too many unknowns with the entirely new system and coaching staff in New York. This week tells us a clearer story. The Commanders’ defense forced five three-and-outs and seven Philadelphia punts. 138 of Jalen Hurts’ 203 passing yards came on just three plays. Of Saquon Barkley’s 83 rushing yards, 42 came on one rushing attempt. The Commanders are susceptible to big plays, but without those chunks, their defense was stout against the Eagles. It will be important for Dallas to utilize their weapons on the outside early and often to generate those big plays. After last week, the Cowboys should decide it’s time to start the game by airing the ball out. Before the season started, Sharp Football had the Commanders’ secondary ranked 31 st in the league, and last week’s tape confirmed it. Dallas should target Mike Sainristil as much as possible with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens as he was the weakest link in week one, giving up over 35 yards per reception. If Dallas takes the route of attacking the Commanders’ defensive backfield with chunk plays, it’ll be important for the offensive line to hold up against a solid pass rush consisting of Odafe Oweh, Dorance Armstrong, K’Lavon Chaisson and Daron Payne. Dallas will also need to look out for a blitzing Sonny Styles, who absolutely crushed Saquon Barkley on his way to a Jalen Hurts sack last week. On the other side of the ball, this defense will be looking to redeem themselves after a poor week one outing against the Giants. One key piece of information to keep in mind this week: blitzing Jayden Daniels may not be the best idea. Last week, Daniels struggled when the Eagles forced pressure without sending an extra man, completing just three out of fifteen attempts for 26 yards. However, when they attacked the pocket with the blitz, Daniels threw for two touchdowns and had a completion percentage of 71.4%. This week, getting home without sending extra blitzers will be one of the most important keys to the game. If this defense can do that in addition to fixing their mental mistakes from week one, they’ll find themselves back on track. Given the history of the Cowboys’ ability to avoid 0-2, and a massive strength on weakness matchup between Dallas’ receivers/Washington’s defensive backs, a bounce-back game is the reasonable expectation in week two. It would be surprising to see the Dallas offense struggle to launch again this week. 27 or more points feels like a lock against the Commanders. The real question will be how often the Cowboys defense can give the ball back to this offense. All things considered, the odds favor Dallas at home this week with a win against their division rival.
author: Dyllan Rivers

title: Broncos vs. Jaguars: 3 Players to Watch in Week 2
summary: The Denver Broncos looked absolutely dreadful in their Week 1 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. Whether it was on offense or defense, nothing seemed to click or go right for them. This weekend, they host the Jacksonville Jaguars who are 1-0 to start the season after beating the Cleveland Browns last Sunday. In order […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - SEPTEMBER 14: Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) hands off to Denver Broncos running back J.K. Dobbins (27) during the second half against the Kansas City Chiefs on September 14th, 2026 at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by William Purnell/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Denver Broncos looked absolutely dreadful in their Week 1 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. Whether it was on offense or defense, nothing seemed to click or go right for them. This weekend, they host the Jacksonville Jaguars who are 1-0 to start the season after beating the Cleveland Browns last Sunday. In order for the Broncos to have a shot at defeating the Jaguars, these three players have to perform at a high level. J.K. Dobbins — Running Back Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb opted with the bold strategy of barely running the ball on the road at Arrowhead on Monday Night Football . That put an immense amount of pressure on Bo Nix, who wound up struggling and having one of his worst games of his career. This Sunday, establishing the run has to be a focal point of their offensive plans. The Jaguars boast a strong defensive line that is extremely good stopping the run. However, the Broncos have to try and get their ground game going if they want any chance at winning on Sunday. J.K. Dobbins was out due to injury in last year’s loss against Jacksonville. Denver spent all offseason trying to revitalize and improve their rushing attack—let’s see them try and enforce that. If RJ Harvey is dinged up and not available to go due to a hamstring issue, rookie running back Jonah Coleman should see his first carries of the regular season. Courtland Sutton — Wide Receiver Last week against the Chiefs, I noted Jaylen Waddle as a player that needed to have a huge game. Unfortunately, Denver’s prized trade acquisition had one catch for two yards. That’s simply unacceptable. Courtland Sutton also failed to make an impact and had just two catches for 11 yards. This week, Sutton has to rise to the occasion and make an impact in the Broncos’ passing game. In last year’s matchup, Sutton led the Broncos with six receptions for 86 yards and a touchdown. He will have to be at his best to give Denver a chance to win. Whether it’s a touchdown catch or reverting back to form and being a chain-moving machine, the receiver corps elder statesman has to play at a high level. Of course, that also means Bo Nix has to do a better job at quarterback. The Broncos’ aerial attack can’t be flat for the second game in a row. Enough of the slow starts. Alex Singleton — Linebacker Truth be told, you could insert almost any player on defense as someone to watch and hope they improve drastically after what happened against the Chiefs. The defensive line was overmatched, the edge rushers failed to get adequate pressure, and several members of the Broncos’ secondary had a rough outing. For Sunday’s game against the Jaguars, I’m choosing inside linebacker Alex Singleton. His agent went to social media to blast fans and writers for criticizing the team. After the game, Singleton’s comments rubbed a lot of folks across Broncos Country the wrong way. I expect team captains to be more accountable than that. Liam Coen loves to diversify his personnel groupings, work in a lot of motion, and do whatever it’s necessary to try and confuse opposing defenses pre-snap. He also likes to utilize running backs in the passing game. I think that will pose a challenge for Singleton who has struggled with the latter on more than one occasion. Will he rise up to the challenge and play better on Sunday? You’ll just have to tune in and find out.

title: Future Broncos: 3 Prospects to Watch in Week 3 of NCAA Football Season
summary: Happy Saturday, Broncos Country. Welcome to another edition of Future Broncos. A lot of you had some great insight on prospects and questions for me after last week’s installment. Feel free to keep giving your opinions on the players I discuss, as well as any other prospects that have caught your eye early on in […]
full_text: PISCATAWAY, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 29: Kj Duff #8 of the Rutgers Scarlet Knights looks on against the Penn State Nittany Lions at SHI Stadium on November 29, 2025 in Piscataway, New Jersey. The Penn State Nittany Lions defeated the Rutgers Scarlet Knights 40-36. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Happy Saturday, Broncos Country. Welcome to another edition of Future Broncos . A lot of you had some great insight on prospects and questions for me after last week’s installment. Feel free to keep giving your opinions on the players I discuss, as well as any other prospects that have caught your eye early on in the collegiate football season. Here are three more prospects to watch this week—all at different positions than I’ve discussed prior. Clev Lubin — Edge Rusher — Louisville The Broncos are beginning their 2026 regular season without multi-year starter Jonathon Cooper in the fold. Who knows when he will be back this year, and it’s anyone’s guess how things will shake out with the ongoing legal process related to his off-the-field issues that transpired this summer. That is giving players like Jonah Elliss, Que Robinson, and Dondrea Tillman some extended reps to see how they perform. In turn, it will be helpful for the coaching staff to evaluate their future potential. Pending the outcome of Cooper’s situation and how the aforementioned trio perform, edge rusher could be in play early on for the Broncos in the 2027 NFL Draft. One player I’m keeping tabs on is Louisville edge rusher Clev Lubin . He initially started his collegiate football career at Army in 2022 but was redshirted the entire year. The next season, he transferred to Iowa Western where he posted 55 tackles, 23.5 tackles for loss, and 11.5 sacks. His top-notch play led him to the Sun Belt conference with Coastal Carolina for the 2024 season. He notched 44 tackles, 12 tackles for loss, and 9.5 sacks in 2024. Last season, Lubin earned third-team All-ACC honors after posting 61 tackles, 13.5 tackles for loss, and 8.5 sacks for the Cardinals defense. So far in 2026, Lubin has been quiet with respect to sacks . However, he has continued his penchant for forced fumbles with two on the season—bringing that total to 12 in just over four seasons of play. He has totaled over 110 pressures the past 25 games which ranks third in the NCAA in that timeframe. If Denver wants to bolster their pass rush, he is a player for them to consider. As of now, a lot of outlets have him ranked as a Top 75 player. You can catch him in action when the 23rd ranked Cardinals host the 16th ranked SMU Mustangs this afternoon on ESPN2. KJ Duff — Wide Receiver — Rutgers The Broncos revamped their wide receiver core this offseason making a big trade for Jaylen Waddle. However, he failed to make an impact in his first game with the Broncos, and no other receiver stood out in Denver’s woeful aerial attack on Monday Night Football versus the Kansas City Chiefs . Courtland Sutton has had an impressive career in Denver. However, with a huge cap hit the next several seasons and only continuing to get older, there is a shot the Broncos opt to move on from him at the end of the season. I’m not sure there is anyone in the fold on their current roster who can replace him. Sure, the Broncos are going to try and feature Pat Bryant a lot this season. Though I believe Denver can’t bank on him being the heir to Sutton. They certainly need to add to the room. That’s where Rutgers standout KJ Duff comes into play. At 6’5” and 225 pounds, Duff boasts the physical profile Head Coach Sean Payton covets at the position. As a freshman, Duff played in thirteen games for the Scarlett Knights and came down with 27 receptions for 42 yards and 1 touchdown. Last season, he really took off and reeled in 60 receptions for 1,084 yards and 7 touchdowns. Rutgers has struggled out the gate during their ’26 season, but Duff has been a bright spot . In their two losses, he already has 17 receptions for 333 yards and 5 touchdowns. He impresses with his contested catch ability and dominance in the red zone. He is only a junior, though the Scarlett Knights’ quarterback situation will almost have him declaring early to take his talents to the NFL. Does that seem like something the Broncos could use for their offense moving forward? Absolutely. If he continues to dominate, I have no doubt he will merit first round consideration next April. You can catch Duff in action this afternoon when Rutgers hosts 12th ranked USC. Greg Johnson — Offensive Lineman — Minnesota Virtually every outlet had the Broncos’ offensive line ranked as the top, or at least near it, entering the 2026 season. Though I felt their play against the Chiefs left a lot to be desired. That made me think about what the overall future might be for the unit. The Broncos drafted Boise State’s Kage Casey in the fourth round in the 2026 NFL Draft. Casey has the potential to be a future starter at left guard and also saw some reps during training camp at center. However, his addition to the line shouldn’t preclude Denver from making draft day investments on the offensive line in ‘27. One prospect down the highway from me is Minnesota senior offensive lineman Greg Johnson . Johnson appeared in just two games as a freshman. Since then, has been a key cog in P.J. Fleck’s offensive line for the Golden Gophers with over 1,900 starting reps under his belt. In 2024, Johnson was a thirteen-game starter at center. Last season, he started all thirteen games again with 11 at left guard, one at right tackle, and another at left tackle. This year, he will be manning down the left guard position for Minnesota and hopes his high level of play can make him an early round draft pick. At 6’6” and 325 pounds, Johnson is an imposing player in the offensive trenches. He is a big reason Minnesota’s ground game has been strong. Quite simply, he is an absolute bully with elite strength to level defenders while paving the way for Minnesota’s backs. He has performed well protecting Drake Lindsey the past two seasons. I wouldn’t be the least bit surprised if Johnson winds up being a Top 32 selection next Spring. He has positional flexibility and the talent to be a Day 1 starter on any offensive line in the NFL. You can watch him when the Golden Gophers host the Akron Zips this morning.

title: September is unkind to Sean Payton-led teams
summary: As bad as it was last Monday, the Denver Broncos season is far from over. And, frankly, it might just be a Sean Payton type September again in 2026. Since coming to Denver in 2023, he has led the Broncos to a 52-32 overall record in the regular season. In September, however, he is a […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY , MO - SEPTEMBER 14: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos scratches his head during the third quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri on Monday, September 14, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images As bad as it was last Monday, the Denver Broncos season is far from over. And, frankly, it might just be a Sean Payton type September again in 2026. Since coming to Denver in 2023, he has led the Broncos to a 52-32 overall record in the regular season. In September, however, he is a woeful 4-8 in that span — well below his .615 win percentage here in Denver. Even in his last four season with the New Orleans Saints it wasn’t pretty in September. Despite going 13-3, 13-3, 12-4, and 9-8 in those seasons, the team still lost five games in September. It gets even worse when the team is average or slightly above average. The previous four years before that good run the Saints had a run of mediocrity. The team went 7-9 for three straight seasons before an 11-5 playoff season. In that four year span, the Saints were 2-12 during the month of September. Woof. For whatever reason, Payton-led teams stumble out of the gates in most seasons. The best seasons he puts on record still has at least one early loss. Last season, Denver started 1-2. Maybe more of the same this season? Hopefully the win comes first, because an 0-2 start would not be ideal. I’m already looking forward to October, though, given the data I just reviewed here today. Horse Tracks

title: Broncos focused on slowing down Jaguars potent offense
summary: The Denver Broncos host the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday for their Week 2 matchup. Coming off a tough loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, the Broncos are trying to rectify what all went wrong and be at their best to go up against a well-coached Jacksonville team. Last season, the Broncos had one of the […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - DECEMBER 21: Dre Greenlaw #57 of the Denver Broncos gets set during the second quarter of an NFL football game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on December 21, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos host the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday for their Week 2 matchup. Coming off a tough loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, the Broncos are trying to rectify what all went wrong and be at their best to go up against a well-coached Jacksonville team. Last season, the Broncos had one of the best defenses in the National Football League. Few teams gave them major issues, but the Jaguars were one of them. Led by Trevor Lawrence, their offense scored 34 points against the Broncos—the most of any opponent. They had 346 yards of total offense and amassed a whopping 22 first downs. But where they really excelled was on third down, completing over 50-percent of their attempts. Today after practice, Head Coach Sean Payton had high praise for Lawrence and how formidable their offense has become under Liam Coen. “They’re doing a great job. He’s got a big arm. All of the things we saw when he came out as a high draft pick. These big quarterbacks who can move and he’s one of them, to the right, to the left. If you get caught in a man defense and you’re not rushing properly, he can pick up eight yards on a third-and-four easily. Then just the surrounding cast, you can tell they’ve been together. They’re confident in what they’re doing,” stated Payton. Under Coen’s leadership, Jacksonville jumped from 26th in points scored in 2024 to being sixth in the NFL in 2025. They went from a four-win team in ‘24 to one that won thirteen games just a season ago. Their transformation on offense played a big part in that. This season, they started off strong with an impressive victory over the Cleveland Browns where Lawrence was able to score four touchdowns. Denver has to find a way to limit Lawrence’s impact on the game. Though he isn’t the only player they have to take notice of. The Jaguars have a talented core of skill positions players that all offer unique skill sets. Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph offered his thoughts on their offense and who they will need to slow down in order to achieve a victory. “I thought Trevor from mid-season last year to now; he’s playing like a Top 5 guy. He has a bunch of weapons. The runner Bhayshul Tuten is very explosive. He’s a 4.3 guy, but he runs hard. He has this compact body, so again the tackle surface is very minimal. You need hats to the ball. Your eyes have to be right when you’re tackling backs like that,” stated Joseph. A fourth-round pick by the Jaguars in the 2025 NFL Draft, Tuten earned the starting role this offseason after Travis Etienne’s departure to the New Orleans Saints. Appearing in fifteen games as a rookie, Tuten notched 386 all-purpose yards and 7 touchdowns. In the season opener against Cleveland, he had 16 total touches for 88 yards and five first downs. He also forced seven missed tackles—something the Broncos can’t afford to let happen again this week. In addition to Tuten, Joseph mentioned several of their wide receivers who stood out to him last year and while watching film. “Parker Washington came on really late last year against us and kind of moved forward to be a real guy as a punt returner and as a receiver. He’s playing well. Jakobi Meyers is playing well as a blocker, a receiver, screen game, all those things he’s doing well. It’s going to be a challenge schematically, and to win some one-on-ones and to obviously tackle better.” Washington had six receptions for 145 yards and a touchdown against the Broncos last December . It was one of the best games of his career. In turn, it was one of the worst for nickelback Ja’Quan McMillian who struggled to combat Washington’s speed and ability at the line of scrimmage. Finding a way to limit Washington’s big play ability is essential for the Broncos on Sunday. Make no mistake, Broncos Country—the Jaguars are a very good team. Denver will have to be at their best to forego starting their ‘26 gridiron campaign 0-2.

title: Sean Payton says ‘you have to be honest’ about issues
summary: I would imagine the toughest part of a head coaches job is dealing with really bad performances. When your team doesn’t tackle, doesn’t put out maximum effort, doesn’t make good decisions from under center, etc etc. All things the Denver Broncos did on Monday in a blowout loss to their division rival. When asked if […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 14: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks on against the Kansas City Chiefs during the third quarter in the game at Arrowhead Stadium on September 14, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images I would imagine the toughest part of a head coaches job is dealing with really bad performances. When your team doesn’t tackle, doesn’t put out maximum effort, doesn’t make good decisions from under center, etc etc. All things the Denver Broncos did on Monday in a blowout loss to their division rival. When asked if players were more attentive this week, head coach Sean Payton noted the reality of the NFL being a league of grown men — not a league of parents coaching children. The mentality has to be different and he did a good job framing that reality. “I think you have to be honest about the corrections,” Payton said today. “I think you point out some of the things that were good when those things come up. We did a lot of things in the kicking game well. I think that these guys are grown men, and when they put the tape on, they see it. So I think we’re in one of those… We said after the game, I said, ‘This is going to be a tough day tomorrow, but we’ll get through it.’” At the end of the day, when the players lay an egg on gameday it is the coaches that also failed by proxy. They have to come together as adults and figure out how to get it fixed for the next game. Hopefully we see that happen this week with the Broncos when they host the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday. title: Broncos vs Jaguars 5 questions: How does Jacksonville replicate last season’s win?
summary: The Denver Broncos have a double dose of motivation this Sunday. They were embarrassed by the Jacksonville Jaguars the last time these two teams played. The Broncos are coming off a humiliating showing on Monday Night Football in the opener. Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars, meanwhile, just whipped Deshaun Watson and the Cleveland Browns. On […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - DECEMBER 21: s #10 of the Denver Broncos is tackled during the second half against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on December 21, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos have a double dose of motivation this Sunday. They were embarrassed by the Jacksonville Jaguars the last time these two teams played. The Broncos are coming off a humiliating showing on Monday Night Football in the opener. Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars, meanwhile, just whipped Deshaun Watson and the Cleveland Browns. On paper, it looks like Denver is in for another tough afternoon. How does Jacksonville replicate the 34-20 beatdown from last season? To get a feel for the Jaguars and what they can take from the playoff loss to the Buffalo Bills, we go “behind enemy lines” with Gus Logue from Big Cat Country . MHR: How tough was the playoff loss to the Bills? What can the Jags take from that loss into this season? Gus : The loss to Buffalo was brutal. Jacksonville entered last postseason on a league-best eight-game winning streak, highlighted by a convincing dub in Denver. Everyone in Duval County believed they were one of the best teams in the AFC. So the loss was tough because it felt like the Jaguars had a lot more football to play, although they used it as motivation in the offseason. After clobbering the Browns in Week 1, head coach Liam Coen said his team was hungry “to get a bad taste out of their mouth with the first time they played a game since, obviously, Buffalo.” Jacksonville wants to play sticker coverage this season to help its pass rush get home, partly because it couldn’t affect Josh Allen in their Wild Card Round exit. MHR: Aside from it being against Cleveland, why was Jacksonville so dominant in the opener? Gus : The top reason was probably the difference in quarterback play. Deshaun Watson’s traditional box score numbers don’t fully reflect how much he tanked Cleveland’s offense with lazy footwork and poor reads. Looking at Expected Points Added, Watson generated -2.8 EPA compared to 18.6 EPA for Trevor Lawrence, who lifted his own offense with aggressive decisions and jaw-dropping touchdowns. Those figures indicate that Jacksonville’s quarterback advantage gave them a 20-point advantage — but the Jags won by 24 — so I would also credit the coaching staff. Coen has proven himself as effective a culture builder as he is a play caller, and you could say the same for defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile, who will become a head coach himself in just a matter of time. The Jaguars have a balanced roster, a franchise quarterback, and a real-deal coaching staff. They were dominant in the season opener because they’re a really good team! It’s not like they won the turnover battle 5-0 or anything. MHR: How do the Jags replicate last season’s win against the Broncos this Sunday? Gus : By continuing to lean into a potent passing attack. Lawrence has been letting it rip ever since last season’s Week 10 collapse in Houston, and based on last week’s game, he’s not letting his foot off the pedal. The Jaguars will go under center and use heavy personnel more often this season, but the strength of the team is Lawrence throwing downfield to a receiver room that’s five deep. He’ll pick on cornerbacks not named Surtain in Week 2 the same way he did in last season’s meeting. On the other side of the ball, the Jaguars plan to repeat as the NFL’s No. 1 run defense, so they’ll key in on J.K. Dobbins and screen plays to make Bo Nix beat them with his arm. Campanile only blitzed Nix on 14.3% of dropbacks in their last meeting, which was the second-lowest rate for the Jaguars all season, but he may want to turn up the dial after seeing Nix take 4 sacks against the Chiefs in Week 1. MHR: What are your thoughts on the current spread? And what is your best bet for Sunday’s game? Gus : It’s tempting to take the points with the Jaguars. They beat the Broncos by two touchdowns last season, and since that game, I’ve grown more confident in Jacksonville and less confident in Denver. I still view the Broncos as Super Bowl contenders because their depth chart and coaching staff are too good to ignore — but IDK about Bo, y’all. As for my best bet for Sunday, I like Parker Washington to go over 51.5 receiving yards. He had a career-high 145 yards against the Broncos last year and a game-high 83 yards against the Browns last week. He’s the No. 1 pass-catcher on what projects to be a top-10, maybe even top-5 passing offense. His weekly receiving yard props should be in the 70s or 80s soon. MHR: What are your expectations and predictions for Sunday? Gus : I don’t want to fall victim to recency bias, but it was hard to watch Monday Night Football and not get excited about what Jacksonville’s under-center run game could do against Denver. Second-year running back Bhayshul Tuten looked impressive in the season opener. According to PFF, the only player with more broken tackles last week was … wait for it … Kenneth Walker III. I’ll predict a breakout game for Tuten and a second-half interception by Travis Hunter to seal another double-digit-point win at Mile High. Jaguars 23, Broncos 13.
author: Ian St. Clair

title: Scouting the Enemy: Jacksonville Jaguars
summary: The Denver Broncos host the Jacksonville Jaguars this Sunday for their first home game of the season. The Jaguars were able to dominate the Cleveland Browns in Week 1 and will be a tough challenge for the Broncos this weekend. Here is a deeper look at the Broncos’ Week 2 opponent. 2025 Jacksonville Jaguars Season […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 13: Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars celebrates a touchdown pass during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the Cleveland Browns at Everbank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos host the Jacksonville Jaguars this Sunday for their first home game of the season. The Jaguars were able to dominate the Cleveland Browns in Week 1 and will be a tough challenge for the Broncos this weekend. Here is a deeper look at the Broncos’ Week 2 opponent. 2025 Jacksonville Jaguars Season Review The Jaguars impressed last season in Liam Coen’s first season as leading the team. They were the AFC South champions and finished with ae 13-4 record. However, they would lose to the Buffalo Bills in in the Wildcard Round. 2026 Jacksonville Jaguars Offseason Additions and Departures The Jaguars approached the offseason a lot like the Broncos did. Instead of making a lot of big free agency splashes, they opted for continuity resigning players who helped them achieve their success last season. They also restructured a lot of in-house contracts, since they were quite low on cap space. One addition they made in free agency was inking running back Chris Rodriguez to a two-year deal. Prior to the roster finalization deadline, they traded for offensive lineman Daniel Faalele into the fold. However, a foot injury will keep him sidelined in the Week 2 matchup against Denver. The Jaguars also lost a handful of quality players this past offseason. Running back Travis Etienne signed a lucrative deal with the New Orleans Saints. Versatile linebacker Devin Loyd made his way to the Carolina Panthers earning a three-year deal worth $45 million. Those were key starters that played a big role in their turnaround last season. In the 2026 NFL Draft, the Jaguars didn’t have a first-round pick but still added 10 players on Day 2 and 3. Their first pick was a surprise, selecting Texas A&M tight end Nate Boerkircher in the second-round a lot higher than analysts projected him to go. They followed up that selection taking his teammate, defensive tackle Albert Regis in the third round and took Oregon guard Emmanuel Pregnon several selections later who will start at left guard on Sunday against Denver. Offensive X-Factor: Quarterback Trevor Lawrence It’s hard to believe it’s Trevor Lawrence’s sixth year in the National Football League. Some may say the former top pick hasn’t lived up to his hype coming out of college. However last year, he put together a rebound season. Lawrence had the best outing of his career throwing for 4,007 yards, 29 touchdowns and just 12 interceptions. Against the Browns in Week 1, Lawrence was absolutely dominant. He completed 18-of-23 passes for 245 yards and 4 touchdowns and was only sacked once. In the Week 16 matchup against the Broncos last season, Lawrence had himself a big game going 23-of-36 for 279 yards and 3 touchdowns. He also added a rushing touchdown. In order to defeat the Jaguars on Sunday, Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph is going to have to find a way to dial up the heat on Lawrence and force him into some mistakes. You can’t let him carve you up through the air and extend drives on third down. He’s one of the best in the game, so Joseph and the defense have their work cut out for them. Defensive X-Factor: Defensive end Josh Hines-Allen Last year, I had the aforementioned Devin Lloyd as their X-Factor on defense. For this matchup, I’ll be giving that nod to Josh Hines-Allen. A two-time Pro-Bowl player, Hines-Allen boasts over 60 sacks in his first seven seasons in the NFL. In 2025, he totaled 49 tackles, 12 tackles for loss, 28 quarterback hits, and 8 sacks and was the most productive pass rusher on their defense. Last week against the Browns, he was an impact player posting 5 tackles, two quarterback hits, and 1.5 sacks. The Jaguars tout a talented front four with Travon Walker playing opposite of him, along with imposing defensive tackles DaVon Hamilton and Arik Armstead. This is a game where Denver’s offensive line is going to have to step up and combat their pass rush. Quarterback Bo Nix is going to need time to operate in the pocket for their aerial attack to have success. The Broncos’ offensive line didn’t have their best performance against the Chiefs. They need to perform much better and do whatever it takes to slow down Hines-Allen. How the Broncos can secure a victory over the Jaguars The Jaguars will be a huge test in Week 2. After being blown out by Kansas City, Denver needs to find a way to win this game. Last year, Denver struggled to run the ball without J.K. Dobbins in the lineup. I’m hoping they can establish the run and control the pace of the game. You can’t be a competitive offense without being able to run the ball. If they don’t do that—they’re toast. The Broncos had two turnovers on downs, an interception, and fumble against Jacksonville last December. They have to be on the winning side of the turnover margin on Sunday to have a chance. Last but not least, they can’t beat themselves. Enough of the drops, enough of the penalties, enough of the missed tackles. Denver needs to get out of their own way and stop being their own worst enemy. Am I confident that will happen this weekend? No, but I’d love to be proven wrong. Hart’s Prediction: Jaguars 27, Broncos 20.
author: Christopher Hart

title: Discussion: What should the Detroit Lions do to fix their defense?
summary: The Detroit Lions defense is a major problem. I could use the next 500 words to lay out all the data to support that statement, but you all have eyeballs. You saw what happened in the second half against the New Orleans Saints. You witnessed Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills move through the Lions’ […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 17: Head coach Dan Campbell of the Detroit Lions reacts against the Buffalo Bills during the second quarter of the game at Highmark Stadium on September 17, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions defense is a major problem. I could use the next 500 words to lay out all the data to support that statement, but you all have eyeballs. You saw what happened in the second half against the New Orleans Saints. You witnessed Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills move through the Lions’ defense like a knife through butter…. melted butter. The good news is that it’s early in the season, and there is plenty of time to make adjustments, change personnel, or do whatever it takes to get this defense on track to… not be the worst defense in the NFL. So today’s Question of the Day is: What is the first thing you’d do to fix the Lions defense? My answer: I’m going to address the obvious up top, because I assume this is going to be a popular answer: the Lions won’t and shouldn’t fire defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard right now. Don’t get me wrong, I think Sheppard is largely to blame for the unit’s struggles right now and his seat should be, at least, heating up. I’ll go more into that in a second. But as coach Dan Campbell pointed out on Monday before the game, Detroit didn’t have any time to make any serious corrections from Week 1 on a short week. You have to at least give Sheppard the chance to go over the tape, come up with some solutions, and try to implement those over the next couple weeks. How Detroit started the season is absolutely unacceptable, and that’s why Sheppard’s seat should be warm, but not giving him the opportunity to adjust and adapt is silly. That’s what the first month of the season is all about. And that’s not even touching the topic of who else on staff is even capable of taking over. But let’s put that aside and go with my proposed solution: simplify everything. This offseason, Sheppard and company went out and made some significant changes to the scheme. While the overall principles are the same, Sheppard added a lot of window dressing. Defensive lineman are stunting and stemming a lot more. The back end is disguising their coverages with inverted looks and a much healthier mix of man and zone. Defensive linemen are regularly dropping into coverage, and defensive backs are blitzing the quarterback and extremely high rates. On the surface, those sort of changes were welcomed. The Lions defense was stale and passive last year. Changes needed to be made, and I was excited to see how it all played out. After all, it was a promising training camp for that unit. But through two weeks, it’s clear these players are not currently capable of running this much flash and flare. They are few reasons for that. Maybe they’re not understanding basic principles. Maybe it’s just too much on their plate. Or maybe it’s just not being taught well enough. It would be one thing if it was one player or one unit that was making the mental mistakes. But it’s everyone . Trusted veterans like Chuck Clark and Avonte Maddox are making poor reads. Jack Campbell—who is this defense—is off to a miserable start. Aidan Hutchinson is jumping into the wrong gaps. When literally everyone is making mental errors, you’ve overloaded them—forcing them to play slow and reactive rather than fast and proactive. Overthinking is a death sentence on defense, and so it’s on Sheppard to pare this thing down considerably. Give the secondary simpler rules and keys to deal with. Allow the defensive linemen to hone in on the things they do well, rather than focusing on trying to confuse quarterbacks with endless combinations. Maybe later in the season when some of the basics are set Detroit can expand upon what they do best, but it’s clear they’re too occupied mentally to perform well right now.
