title: With Rams linebackers hurting, should Shaun Dolac start?
summary: There was more to the story than just the score of the Los Angeles Rams pummeling at the hands of the arch-rival San Francisco 49ers last week. A physical toll was paid as well, particularly in the linebacker unit. Both starters Nate Landman (shoulder/thumb) and Omar Speights (hip) were nicked up.  Reports out of L.A. […]
full_text: There was more to the story than just the score of the Los Angeles Rams pummeling at the hands of the arch-rival San Francisco 49ers last week. A physical toll was paid as well, particularly in the linebacker unit. Both starters Nate Landman (shoulder/thumb) and Omar Speights (hip) were nicked up. Reports out of L.A. are that both will likely be available for the upcoming Monday Night Football tilt vs. the New York Giants. There is much pride in the NFL about biting the bullet and playing through pain, the difference between just hurting and being injured. The logic escapes though, when trotting out limited players, even if only slightly/moderately impaired, against a physical, run-based offense and an athletic quarterback. L.A.’s next opponent, the New York Giants employs both.. This leads to a question that needs to be asked and answered. Nate Landman is down with an arm injury #NFL #49ers #FTTB #Rams #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/qP4NUgkhC3 — Dom (@ZeroChillSports) September 11, 2026 Is Shaun Dolac the right move at linebacker? In relief against the ‘Niners, Dolac got in on 19 defensive snaps, by far his most work since he received 35 in relief of Speights back in Week 6 of 2025. He also put in 17 reps of special teams work. For the day, he logged six tackles. He primarily lined up to the wide side of the field, defending 13 run plays and six vs. the pass. While I didn’t keep track of the number, it appeared that the S.F. offense would attack outside when Landman was covering the wise side territory. Reviewing Dolac’s film, it wasn’t a breakout performance, but his downhill trigger and aggressive attacking of run gaps did stand out. Eight of the plays (five passes) went well away from his sphere of influence and he wasn’t involved. The one completed pass, a middle screen, went for five yards. Not much of a sample to grade his pass defense. I graded seven of Dolac’s 10 defended run plays as solid, two as negative and one a toss up. One of the two negatives was a missed tackle on a Christian McCaffrey spin move that went for a couple of extra yards and on the other, he was cleanly blocked on a sweep that went for 14. The toss up was another wide run (seven yard gain) where he came from the opposite side of the formation and made the tackle, but took an iffy pursuit angle that forced him to make the play from behind. Instincts and aggression drive Dolac’s work defending the run. He bangs heads into blockers with physicality fitting into run gaps and when tasked to read and pursue, uses nifty footwork and a nice swim move to maneuver around bigger blockers and navigate through the line of scrimmage traffic. In theory, since the Rams don’t do a lot of straight-up man coverage (more matching and pursuing to areas) with the line backers, Dolac’s change of direction and trigger abilities should offer zone coverage upside. The phrase “in theory” works because he just doesn’t have a much pro film defending the pass. Just look how fast Shaun Dolac is to the ball. The Rams UDFA LB reads Cooper Rush's eyes and is on Justice Hill as the ball arrives. pic.twitter.com/fOeDN49jm3 — Blaine Grisak (@BGMediaOnSI) October 13, 2025 Don’t judge a book by its cover Dolac came to L.A. via the undrafted ranks in 2025. Although he put up stellar numbers in college, at 6’1” 225 lbs with just over 30” arms, he was deemed as lacking the physical attributes of an NFL linebacker. Those are justified opinions, but Dolac is sneakily athletic and strong, according to nfldraftbuzz.com, his testing profile consistently rates in the 70th percentile. Earning his way up a depth chart is not new to Dolac, he began his college career at Buffalo as a walk-on and left after being named a consensus All-American and leading the NCAA with 168 tackles in his final season. Even though he twice topped 145+ tackles, with 40.5 of those for loss, there were no all-star game or a NFL Draft Combine invites extended. The snubs did not deter Dolac, he worked his way onto the Rams 2025 opening roster, and was not only activated, but played in all 17 games before a knee injury sidelined him for the playoffs. At the @UBFootball Pro Day, All-American Shaun Dolac ( @ShaunDolac ) ran an unofficial 4.55 in the 40-yard dash. That would be the 6th fastest linebacker at the combine. The nation’s leader in tackles racked up 25 bench reps which would be the 3rd highest. @SalSports @WGR550 pic.twitter.com/jTYzioLJ9s — Zach Monell (@Zach_Monell) March 13, 2025 Is a move imminent? Should fans expect it? Rams Head coach Sean McVay has a history of being hesitant to replace an imbedded starter, but with both Nate Landman and Omar Speights coming out of the opener nicked up, this appears to be an excellent time to give Dolac a long look. It would be interesting to see if his aggressive style can help light a fire under the Rams defense. Rams fans would likely welcome this move because it seems that the fielding of “serviceable” linebackers is simply baked into the Rams approach to the unit. There is certainly no guarantee that putting Dolac on the field in front of the others will turn the second line of the defense into an impenetrable force, but when forced into a large role in Week 6 of last season (a one-off outing, at that), he stepped right up to plate. As a pro, his play in training camp/practice has been lauded for on-field and chalkboard work. There is no need for the L.A. braintrust to play two injured players when they have a third option, a serviceable one at that.

Matthew Stafford throws 4 touchdowns After failing to throw a touchdown in the opener, Stafford will throw four in Week 2. One to Puka Nacua. One to Davante Adams. One to Colby Parkinson. title: Sean McVay hopeful Rams don’t play in Australia again
summary: If teleportation existed, and or had the Los Angeles Rams won in Australia, then perhaps Sean McVay would feel different, but as it stands McVay is happy the game in Australia is over. McVay is hopeful the Rams never have to play a game like that again. McVay, a true company man, says the atmosphere […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Head Coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams with Head Coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers on the field after the game at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. The 49ers defeated the Rams 27-7. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images If teleportation existed, and or had the Los Angeles Rams won in Australia, then perhaps Sean McVay would feel different, but as it stands McVay is happy the game in Australia is over. McVay is hopeful the Rams never have to play a game like that again. McVay, a true company man, says the atmosphere down under was “great”, however one can assume the travel, the idea of playing so far from home, the fact that L.A. got whooped up on, McVay appears content to leave that game and experience in the past. It’s interesting, and maybe one day we’ll hear McVay talk about what went right and what went wrong during the team’s preparation for their Australian game. As it stands, what we know is the Rams lost, and now they want to turn the page. Easier said than done. From the sound of it, Week 1 isn’t exactly all in the past, yet. In fact, Week 1 is still very much in the present, until the Rams can give fans a reason to believe otherwise. If winning is a cure-all, then losing is a deadly poison. The Rams are 0-2 in their last two games played. Facts. Can they find a cure Monday night? Tune in, find out. Sean McVay hopes Rams never play again in Australia; Aaron Donald’s status undecided (latimes.com) “McVay said the Rams have moved forward from the loss to the 49ers. “It’s almost like you try and do the ‘Men in Black’ thing,” McVay said, referencing the movie franchise, “where you say all right, ‘hey I don’t remember what happened.’ That was so long ago. We’re not playing in Australia ever again, I hope. Not because it wasn’t a great atmosphere. That will get taken out of context.” Sean McVay hopes the Rams never play in Australia again (nbcsports) “Bottom line is, I like the way that I feel of our preparation, eyes moving forward, chest out, chin up, eyes forward, and let’s go be about it,” McVay said. “Let’s go prepare the right way. Let’s have great focus and concentration. Let’s have a great energy and an edge in which we prepare and compete with and then let’s go be ready to go against a really damn good football team. What they looked like in Week 1, we got a great challenge ahead. That’s what every week is. We’re excited to compete. All we can do is really have a great day of preparation today.” Rams vs. Giants injury report: 3 LA starters limited, 1 DNP Thursday (ramswire) “Nate Landman, Omar Speights, Kam Curl and Kamren Kinchens were among the players who got banged up in the season opener, so their health will bear monitoring throughout the week leading up to Monday’s game. After practice on Thursday, the Rams released their first injury report of Week 2, listing several key players on it. Curl, Speights and Landman were all listed as limited participants on Thursday, while Kinchens missed practice altogether. Davante Adams got a veteran rest day, too.“ Rams, Packers, Chargers, Patriots: Which Week 1 losses should scare us most? (cbssports) “Super Bowl odds. That gave us 53 historical losses to compare with what happened over the rest of the season. The biggest takeaway might also be the most reassuring: If your team was supposed to be good before Week 1, getting blown out wasn’t much worse than a close loss. What mattered much more was how the team played. The good news: If a contender got blown out, the blowout itself isn’t the problem A Week 1 loss matters. Preseason contenders that won their opener from 2015-2025 made the playoffs 73% of the time, while those that lost fell to 42%. But once a contender lost, the margin barely mattered — one-score losers made the playoffs 41% of the time, and teams beaten by nine or more made it roughly 43% of the time.“ Former Rams Star WR Could Join AFC Contender (heavy.com) “Former Los Angeles Rams veteran wide receiver Brandin Cooks once played in back-to-back Super Bowls but lost both. title: Las Vegas Raiders-Los Angeles Chargers FEED topic: Which defensive tackle steps up?
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are riding the high of a Week 1 victory over the Miami Dolphins, but the Raiders were expected to win that contest. In a way, last week was the feel-good/tune-up game, and this Sunday is Las Vegas’ first real test with a matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers. While the Chargers […]
full_text: (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are riding the high of a Week 1 victory over the Miami Dolphins , but the Raiders were expected to win that contest. In a way, last week was the feel-good/tune-up game, and this Sunday is Las Vegas’ first real test with a matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers . While the Chargers are 0-1, they do have a talented roster and are expected to be contenders this season. So, a Raiders’ win would not only put some distance between them and a division rival, but it would also send a message to the rest of the league that the season opener wasn’t a fluke and Vegas will surprise some people this season, including me. One way for the Silver and Black to pull off the upset is to take advantage of arguably the weakest part of Los Angeles’ roster: the interior offensive line. However, a similar statement could be made about the Raiders’ defensive tackles. The Chargers have already had to pivot from their offseason plan with free-agent signing/center Tyler Biadasz suffering a season-ending injury during training camp, moving rookie second-round pick Jake Slaughter from guard to center. Granted, that’s Slaughter’s natural position, starting there at Florida from 2023 to 2025. But he’s young and struggled as a run blocker in Week 1, posting a 39.0 run-blocking grade from Pro Football Focus (PFF) and a 60.9 mark (on a 50-100 scale) from Pro Football Network (PFN). Additionally, Biadasz’s injury has led to Los Angeles playing musical chairs at left guard, with Kayode Awosika (35 total snaps) and Trey Pipkins III (20) rotating at the position against the Arizona Cardinals. All signs point toward Awosika holding down that spot moving forward, earning a 71.1 overall grade from PFF and 79.1 from PFN, compared to a 37.1 PFF grade for Pipkins. PFN doesn’t have publicly available data for Pipkins. At the other guard spot, Cole Strange was another offseason addition and had a rough Chargers debut in pass protection. PFF had him on the hook for five pressures on 35 opportunities for an ugly 10.6 grade, while PFN’s pass-pro formula ranked Strange 53rd out of 61 guards with a 68.1 mark in Week 1. But again, Las Vegas is still waiting for a defensive tackle to step up. Tonka Hemingway drew plenty of praise for his training camp performance, which is great to hear from the second-year pro. However, he blended in on limited snaps during the preseason and didn’t stand out against the Dolphins. That isn’t to say Hemingway played poorly by any means, but there is room for him to be more impactful moving forward. Perhaps the best or most impactful defensive tackle on the Raiders’ roster is the last one added to it: Foley Fatukasi. Despite playing just 18 snaps last week, Fatukasi had half a sack, a batted pass and two ‘ defensive stops ’ against the run, per PFF . Combine that with how he played in the last two preseason games, and more playing time should be in order for the nine-year veteran. Thomas Booker IV is in a similar boat, seeing just 19 snaps versus Miami but making the most out of the limited opportunities. Booker flashed a handful of times against the run and also recorded a pair of stops in the season opener. Meanwhile, it feels like Adam Butler and Jonah Laulu are sliding down the depth chart, or at least running that risk. So, for this week’s game day discussion on The FEED , we’ll be focusing on the interior of the Raiders’ defensive line. This is a good matchup for someone to step up and establish themselves as a starting defensive tackle for the rest of the campaign. The game kicks off at 1:05 p.m. PST and will air on CBS (check your local listings). I look forward to talkin’ some ball with y’all!
author: Matt Holder

title: Raiders Week 2: The must-account-for Chargers in an AFC West tilt
summary: One litmus test is in the books. And another one is on tap for Klint Kubiak and his Las Vegas Raiders football team. Against a division foe, no less. It was widely assumed Kubiak and his desert marauders would top the visiting Miami Dolphins in Week 1 and the Silver & Black obliged with a […]
full_text: (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images One litmus test is in the books. And another one is on tap for Klint Kubiak and his Las Vegas Raiders football team. Against a division foe, no less. It was widely assumed Kubiak and his desert marauders would top the visiting Miami Dolphins in Week 1 and the Silver & Black obliged with a 27-13 victory. In Week 2, a higher quality opponent awaits the Raiders in Inglewood: The 0-1 Los Angeles Chargers. Unlike Las Vegas — which waxed an underdog opponent — the Bolts were thunderstruck by the Arizona Cardinals 26-14 this past Sunday. Like Miami and even Las Vegas, Arizona is very much in a new-era phase with neophyte head coaches in rookie Mike LaFleur (Jeff Hafley for Dolphins and Kubiak, obviously, for Raiders). The loss was a sobering reality check for the Chargers — a hackneyed media darling pick as a team that can make noise in the playoffs. So much so, head coach Jim Harbaugh had this to say after the defeat: “We made some preseason type of mistakes. Now I wish we played our starters more in the preseason to give them some game reps.” Kubiak and Harbaugh are knee-deep in prepping for the Week 2 clash in SoFi Stadium and it’s an opportunity for both the Raiders and Chargers to prove Week 1 was not or was a fluke. After the season opening slate, Las Vegas and the Kansas City Chiefs finds itself atop the AFC West at 1-0 while the Chargers and Broncos (who played the Chiefs this past Monday night) are winless. Standings are likely to fluctuate as the season goes forward, but the initial matchup between the Raiders and Chargers presents a pivot point for the two rivals. So let’s take a look at Chargers that can give the Raiders headaches in this Sunday afternoon tilt. Edge rusher combo Tuli Tuipulotu and Khalil Mack present a formidable duo for Kubiak’s offense to combat. And defensively, quarterback Justin Herbert can make all the throws to stress Rob Leonard’s defense. No. 86 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @chargers LB Tuli Tuipulotu! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/gj4en5FqHw — NFL (@NFL) July 1, 2026 Edge-ucational Opportunity The duo of Tuipulotu and Mack was rendered ineffective by the Cardinals in Week 1 — there’s no sugar coating it. While the former had five total tackles and two quarterback hits and the latter had two total tackles, that’s well below the contributions the Bolts’ pass rush combo have produced before. And the combo provides both veteran savvy (Mack is 35 years old) and youthful exuberance (Tuipulotu is 24). Expect the Chargers defense to be champing at the bit to prove the season-opening loss was a fluke. Los Angeles is going to force one-on-one matchups between their two premiere pass rushers and Las Vegas offensive tackles Kolton Miller (stalwart on the left) and DJ Glaze (heavy presence on the right) when Tuipulotu and Mack deployed as two-sided rushers opposite each other. The Chargers are keen on sending the duo after the quarterback from the same side, too. This can create lethal stunt and twists where Tuipulotu uses his well-built 6-foot-3 and 266-pound frame to power through gaps and draw multiple blockers while Mack uses his effective speed-to-power transition for closing speed on a direct path to the quarterback. Not only will that stress Raiders’ lineman, but tight ends and running backs, alike. Mack also tends to save his best for matchups against the Silver & Black — he was drafted by the team fifth overall in the 2014 NFL Draft — as he’s faced off against the Raiders in 10 games and racked up 13 sacks, 12 tackles for loss, four forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries, and 42 total tackles. Offensive line boss Rick Dennison did some heavy lifting this offseason to get the Raiders trenches up to snuff and we’ll get to see how far (or how far they still have to go) Las Vegas O-line has come since a disastrous 2025 campaign. And that’s just the aerial attack. Tuipulotu and Mack aren’t just selling out for sacks, they’re disciplined, patient, and savvy run defenders, too. They both can set the edge and diagnose and destroy blocking designs to blow up plays in the backfield — what Raiders’ elite edge rusher Maxx Crosby excels at, too. The Bolts’ edge duo are tone setters and if they’re firing on all cylinders, Kubiak’s offense can be grinded to a halt if the Raiders’ can’t replicate what the Cardinals did. Justin Herbert in his first game with OC Mike McDaniel: 17-of-27 209 passing yards 1 TD, 1 INT pic.twitter.com/R6PbaD3qxc https://t.co/cVwBGsFgPa — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) September 13, 2026 Herb-al Remedy The sixth overall pick of the 2020 draft, Herbert remains a thorn in not only the Raiders’ side, but the rest of the division. The 28-year-old stands 6-foot-6 and 236 pounds and started off the game against the Cardinals well enough. But as the game progressed, Herbert was rattled (as were the rest of the Chargers) finishing 17 of 27 for 209 yards with a touchdown pass and interception while getting sacked three times by Arizona. Harbaugh has said numerous times Herbert is the engine that drives the Chargers and a rebound game is a must. Herbert has done fairly well against the Silver & Black all-time in the 11 times he’s faced the team going 8-3 overall while connecting on 255 of 390 passes for 2,909 yards and 22 touchdowns to just three interceptions. He’s been sacked 22 times by the Raiders, however. Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard is all too familiar with Herbert and will have to orchestrate the defense to stymie a quarterback that can make all the throws but is susceptible to getting hit and/or taken down for sacks. Another strong outing by Crosby and fellow edge rusher Kwity Paye is in order alongside disciplined performances from linebackers Quay Walker and Nakobe Dean along with the secondary holding up in coverage. The interesting thing here: The ways Los Angeles can deploy their dynamic duo of Tuipulotu and Mack is eerily similar to how Las Vegas can attack with Crosby and Paye. We saw in Week 1, that Paye can line up as an interior rusher and take advantage of stunts and twists, too. Head-to-Head Sunday’s matchup between the Raiders and Chargers will be meeting No. 133 between the two AFC West squads. The Silver & Black lead the all-time series 69-62-2 (68-62-2 in regular season, 1-0 in playoff action). The Bolts, however, are riding a four-game win streak dating back to September 2024. The last Raiders win was on Thursday night back in 2023 (63-21 shellacking). The Chargers own the longest win streak in the series with 13-straight from 2003 to 2009. Kicker here: The Raiders haven’t won in SoFi Stadium with fans present. The team is 1-7 in that particular venue with the win coming in an empty stadium in 2020. Quote of Note “Execution fuels emotion, so if you execute at a high level everybody’s getting excited. When everybody’s getting excited, good things happen. And it’s not just one person. Malcolm (Koonce) is right in that category too. He’s an energy giver. He makes a play and starts headbutting people. Kwity did that. As a coach, you want to feel that from everybody.” —Las Vegas Raiders defensive coordinator Rob Leonard on how much Maxx Crosby and Kwity Paye feed off each other as edge rushers

title: Raiders’ tight end Brock Bowers is doubtful to play Sunday
summary: Las Vegas Raiders superstar tight end Brock Bowers may be making a key step back toward the playing field. According to multiple media reports, Bowers was seen on the practice field as the team started its final work day before playing at the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday. It is the first time Bowers has […]
full_text: (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders superstar tight end Brock Bowers may be making a key step back toward the playing field. According to multiple media reports, Bowers was seen on the practice field as the team started its final work day before playing at the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday. It is the first time Bowers has hit the practice field since having knee surgery 10 days ago. He missed the first two days of this practice week. Still, he is likely not going to play against the Chargers. Las Vegas head coach Klint Kubiak said Friday that Bowers is doubtful to play Sunday. He will work out prior to the game, but would need to make a lot of progress to be cleared. Kubiak said he is optimistic Bowers will play at the New Orleans Saints on September 27. Michael Mayer will start for Bowers at the Chargers if he can’t play. Mayer had six catches for 32 yards in Week 1. Meanwhile, starting cornerback Darien Porter remained out of practice Friday and was ruled out of the Chargers’ game. He missed the entire week of practice. Kubiak said Wednesday Porter was day-to-day like Bowers. Porter left the Miami game, a 27-13 Las Vegas win, late in the fourth quarter with a foot injury. Rookie Zeke Masses played the final 10 plays of the game for Porter. Masses will likely start Sunday. Perhaps rookie Jermod McCoy will debut Sunday. He was active last week, but didn’t play. Also, No. 3 quarterback Aidan O’Connell was not seen on the practice field Friday. He has missed the past two days for personal reasons and his return is to be determined. He is not expected to be at Sunday’s game. Meanwhile, Chargers’ receiver Ladd McConkey practiced Friday for the first time this week because of a ribs injury.

title: Klint Kubiak displays his creativity in his 21 personnel groupings.
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders had one of their better offensive performances on Sunday, putting up 27 points. It was their highest home-opener total since 2021, when they beat the Baltimore Ravens. What shined on offense was creativity with 21 personnel from Klint Kubiak. According to Next Gen Stats, the Raiders ran 21 personnel on 36% […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders had one of their better offensive performances on Sunday, putting up 27 points. It was their highest home-opener total since 2021, when they beat the Baltimore Ravens. What shined on offense was creativity with 21 personnel from Klint Kubiak. According to Next Gen Stats, the Raiders ran 21 personnel on 36% of their offensive snaps. He found creative ways to have multiple backs on the field and keep defenses off guard. At times, Jeanty and Washington were on the field at the same time. Other times it was Laube and Jeanty. A great example was the second-quarter touchdown to Ashton Jeanty. Laube and the former first-round pick were both in the backfield after the motion. It led to a touchdown, with Kubiak creating a one-on-one with Jeanty and Chris Johnson. Jeanty was even lined up at fullback at one point. On this play, Michael Mayer made a 14-yard catch after running an angle route out of the backfield from fullback. The Raiders got a first down on this play. All of this showed the creativity Kubiak brings by moving players around and creating matchups. It will be fun to watch how he keeps finding different ways to keep football teams off guard as the season continues.

title: Raiders Week 1 wide receiver snap and production review
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders opened the 2026 season with a 27-13 victory at home over the Miami Dolphins.While it was an overall strong opening effort, perhaps the team’s most questioned unit, the wide receiver group, didn’t have a great day as the top four receiver combined for nine catches for 83 yards and a touchdown. […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders opened the 2026 season with a 27-13 victory at home over the Miami Dolphins. While it was an overall strong opening effort, perhaps the team’s most questioned unit, the wide receiver group, didn’t have a great day as the top four receiver combined for nine catches for 83 yards and a touchdown. Let’s look at them all: Tre Tucker The fourth-year player led all Las Vegas receivers with 48 snaps (70 percent of the offensive plays). He had two catches on four targets for 27 yards. He didn’t play less than 88 percent of the snaps in any game last season and he averaged playing 94.9 of the snaps last season. Tucker’s biggest issue in his career has been producing consistently. Jalen Nailor The free-agent addition played 41 snaps (60 percent). He had three catches for 27 yards on five targets. Nailor averaged 65 percent of the snaps in Minnesota last season when he had 29 receptions. Jack Bech The 2025 second-round pick played 27 snaps (39.9 percent) Sunday. He had three catches for 23 yards on four targets and he had a touchdown, the first of his career. He played a higher snap count average in eight of the 16 games he played as a rookie than Sunday’s total. Malik Benson The rookie sixth-round pick played just seven offensive snaps (10 percent). He had one catch for six yards on two targets. It will be interesting to see if his role grows in upcoming weeks. Conclusion: The four receivers didn’t produced much and they were targets a total of 15 times, which isn’t a ton. There are lot of factors that go in a game plan and the Raiders’ running game was clocking. Yet, with star tight end Brock Bowers out in Week 1, more was expected from the Raiders’ receivers. Regardless, NFL teams need more production from their receivers, so this will be something to watch Sunday at the Chargers and beyond.
author: Bill Williamson

title: Las Vegas Raiders offensive line turning heads for right reasons
summary: The 2026 Las Vegas Raiders starting offensive line played so well that we have to ask what went wrong in 2025. It would be too easy to trash and bash the previous offensive line coach while he’s not here to defend himself. However, the truth of the matter is that Brennan Carroll, was simply horrendous […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 Las Vegas Raiders starting offensive line played so well that we have to ask what went wrong in 2025. It would be too easy to trash and bash the previous offensive line coach while he’s not here to defend himself. However, the truth of the matter is that Brennan Carroll, was simply horrendous at his job. How lost 3/5 of these offensive linemen played last season was malpractice. The fact that a rookie running back had to go to his general manager to watch film and try to better understand what he needed to do was appalling. Big time pass protectors On Sunday, under the leadership of offensive line coach Rick Dennison, Kolton Miller, Spencer Burford, Tyler Linderbaum, Jackson Powers-Johnson and Delmar Glaze absolutely tore the Miami Dolphins defensive line a new one. We must give praise where praise is due. Miller and Glaze were the first and third-highest-graded tackles in pass-block win rate according to ESPN Analytics and NFL Next Gen Stats. Top 5 (left) and bottom 5 (right) tackles in pass block win rate in Week 1. (ESPN Analytics / NFL Next Gen Stats) pic.twitter.com/7TGiaAGBH3 — Seth Walder (@SethWalder) September 14, 2026 Linderbaum, since signing with the Silver and Black in free agency, has come in and made a huge difference at the point of attack. Proving against the Dolphins to be not only the toughest guy on the line, but also one of the smartest. As the captain of the offensive line, his communication was a key part in ensuring quarterback Kirk Cousins was never sacked and only touched a handful of times. C Tyler Linderbaum picking up looping DE on 3 man stunt on touchdown to Jack Bech. #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/kKqXnUimbe — Ryan Holmes (@Rholm22) September 15, 2026 Not only didn’t the Raiders offensive line surrender a sack but the 29% pressure allowed rate was third least in week 1 across the league. Cousins, enjoyed an average of 2.9 seconds to throw which was 14th in week 1. Miami’s defense may not be world beaters, but to go from being dead last to middle of the pack in your first game is massive immediate improvement. The maulers and mashers For years and throughout many different coaching regimes, the words zone blocking scheme were prophecies of dysfunction and doom. Yet somehow Dennison got the best showings we’ve seen out of his two guards, Burford and Powers-Johnson. The holes and lanes they opened up were large and made life easy for the ball carriers. Not to mention the cutback and bouncing lanes were there when the defense managed to clog the intended gap. Ashton Jeanty ran the ball 23 times for 102 yards, averaging 4.4 yards per carry. His backup, Mike Washington Jr, ran the ball seven times for 41 yards and an average of 5.9 yards per carry. Very admirable numbers for the two workhorses. If this is indeed a sign of things to come, then the Raiders offensive line provided they stay healthy is going to have a huge bounce back year in 2026.

title: Raiders-Chargers Week 2: 5 things to watch
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders, 1-0, visit the Los Angeles Chargers, 0-1, Sunday. Here are five keys to victory: Offensive line dominance: A major reason why the Raiders are 1-0 after a 27-13 home win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday was because of the offensive line. Last season, of course, the offensive line was a […]
full_text: (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders, 1-0, visit the Los Angeles Chargers, 0-1, Sunday. Here are five keys to victory: Offensive line dominance: A major reason why the Raiders are 1-0 after a 27-13 home win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday was because of the offensive line. Last season, of course, the offensive line was a big reason why the Raiders were woeful on offense. That wasn’t the case last week. The unit opened big holes in the running game on a regular basis and didn’t allow a sack. The Chargers have a strong defense. This will be a big test. But if Las Vegas’ offensive line holds up again, a victory is very possible. Ashton Jeanty: The second-year running back has a huge Week 1. He had 29 touches (23 carries and six catches) on the Raiders’ 68 offensive plays. He accounted for 147 of the Raiders’ 290 scrimmage yards. He wore down Miami late in the game. That sounds like a formula coach Klint Kubiak would like to repeat this week. Stop the run: The Raiders did a nice job of holding Miami running back De”Von Achane to just 36 yards rushing. They must do that against the Chargers’ Omarion Hampton. He is a load and he can make big plays. Las Vegas has to keep that to a minimum. Pressure Herbert: The Raiders had five sacks and constantly pressured Malik Willis last week. Maxx Crosby and Kwity Paye were relentless. The opportunity for another big pressure day is available this week. The Chargers had trouble protecting Justin Herbert last week. If the Raiders can force Herbert into making mistakes that will go a long way toward an upset win. Better receiver production: Las Vegas receivers Jalen Nailor, Tre Tucker, Jack Bech and Malik Benson combined for nine catches for 83 yards and a touchdown. That, of course, isn’t good enough. That production must improve this week.

title: Raiders News: Mike McDaniel calls Maxx Crosby ‘professional game wrecker’
summary: Ahead of the Week 2 matchup between the Las Vegas Raiders and Los Angeles Chargers, Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel was asked about game planning for Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby and praised the five-time Pro Bowler Last week, Crosby had a big game against McDaniel’s former team, the Miami Dolphins, coming alive in the […]
full_text: (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Ahead of the Week 2 matchup between the Las Vegas Raiders and Los Angeles Chargers, Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel was asked about game planning for Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby and praised the five-time Pro Bowler “You talk about one of the guys in my career, one of the guys I respect the absolute most,” McDaniel said of Crosby during his Sept. 17 press conference. “He is upper echelon just because of the relentless drive and competitiveness: Play in, play out. It’s almost unmatched. So you play really good players every single week, and every single week they have pass rushers. NFL teams have pass rushers, and they’re generally pretty talented, but every so often there’s a guy that is a professional game wrecker. “So you have to present to the players, and we obviously all of our guys know who Maxx Crosby is and have gone against him numerous times. But when you present it like, ‘Hey, this is how this defense plays when he’s able to be left to his own devices,’ you show the entire offense because it takes a group of people to stop a player of his caliber.” Raider Nation, take the conversation everywhere! title: Dolphins’ Chop Robinson out for Sunday vs. 49ers
summary: After being downgraded on Thursday’s injury report following a concussion, Dolphins’ edge rusher Chop Robinson has officially been ruled out ahead of Sunday afternoon’s game against the San Francisco 49ers. Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Robinson suffered the concussion during Wednesday’s practice. It is Robinson’s third concussion within the last year. Also ruled out of the game […]
full_text: After being downgraded on Thursday’s injury report following a concussion, Dolphins’ edge rusher Chop Robinson has officially been ruled ou t ahead of Sunday afternoon’s game against the San Francisco 49ers. Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Robinson suffered the concussion during Wednesday’s practice. It is Robinson’s third concussion within the last year. Also ruled out of the game was linebacker Ronnie Harrison, Jr. Primarily a special teams player in Week 1, Harrison has been dealing with a hamstring injury that kept him from practicing all week. With Robinson sidelined, Josh Uche, Malik Herring, Robert Beal Jr., and potentially Clelin Ferrell, who is currently on the practice squad, are all candidates to see increased workloads. Hafley could also continue deploying defensive tackle Zeek Biggers on the edge, as he did during last Sunday’s loss to the Raiders. Miami’s injury report also listed long snapper Tucker Addington as questionable for the game. Addington injured his shoulder in Week 1 but played through the rest of the game. The 49ers’ side of the injury report included officially ruling out wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling who did not practice throughout the week with an ankle injury. as well as designating running back Kaelon Black and kicker Eddy Pineiro as questionable. Black was limited in practice on Thursday and Friday after sustaining a groin injury. Pineiro did not practice all week due to an illness. The Dolphins and 49ers kickoff on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. Eastern.

title: Miami Dolphins reasons for hope, concern heading into Week 2
summary: Howdy y’all.  I’m a little behind this week, so I didn’t get to watch and write all the stuff I wanted to for here or AOR.  I’m trying to develop a few regular posts for this site each week to keep all y’all as engaged as possible.  You know, given what this season is and […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Caleb Douglas #7 of the Miami Dolphins runs against the Las Vegas Raiders in the second quarter of their game at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Raiders defeated the Dolphins 27-13. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Howdy y’all. I’m a little behind this week, so I didn’t get to watch and write all the stuff I wanted to for here or AOR. I’m trying to develop a few regular posts for this site each week to keep all y’all as engaged as possible. You know, given what this season is and all. Y’all saw the Tuesday Thoughts post, and I’m gonna make that one a regular. If y’all have any ideas for additional posts, let me know. Anyway… I figured I would start a post with 3 things to watch for in each game that promote optimism and 3 things that should make us worried. Aside from the usual stuff. So welcome to The Earl’s Three For Three! Three Reasons for Hope 1. Experience Has Been Gained Last week, the Dolphins’ rookies played 27.2% of the possible snaps . That was league-leading and nearly 10% more than the next closest team (Browns at 16.7%). Over a quarter of the snaps were played by someone who had never taken an NFL snap. Chris Johnson, Jacob Rodriguez, and Kadyn Proctor played every snap. Caleb Douglas, Michael Taaffe, and Chris Bell played 91%, 75%, and 52%, respectively. Not all of this was pretty. Johnson was picked on early and often, and Taaffe missed a few assignments. But this week, they know what it’s like. They know the feeling of stepping onto an NFL field for the first time . Once upon a time, I had the opportunity to interview Cameron Wake over the phone for The Phinsider. I asked him about his first experience in the NFL, and he talked about that feeling when you first step out there and think, “I made it.” I imagine it was overwhelming for these young players, even ones like Proctor who played for one of the biggest college programs out there. But not only is the first-time feeling gone, but they also have a good idea of what the play is like at the NFL level. I recall a comment from Hall of Fame LB Patrick Willis about getting hit by Edgerrin James in his first game and realizing what “grown man” strength was and how the NFL is on a different level. That’s gone now. These rookies have seen the real game now. They have felt the real game now. They still don’t know enough yet, but they won’t be as surprised now. That’ll lead to smarter and quicker decisions, better communication, and higher confidence. 2. There Is Hope Up Front The Rams are a true Super Bowl contender, and the 49ers shut them down. That should be scary, right? Not necessarily. Despite the outcome, the Rams still put up 290 yards of offense, with 122coming on the ground. The 49ers allowed the Rams a 4.2 YPC average. There was also not a single sack in this game. The 49ers generated 8 pressures on 29 dropbacks, but recorded no sacks. Miami’s offensive line isn’t as accomplished as LA’s, but they should have extra motivation this week after how they performed against Vegas. The 49ers can’t just pin their ears back and rush the passer either. Matthew Stafford is great at maneuvering the pocket, but he does not have the ability to threaten defenses on the ground like Malik Willis. They may play more “contain” rather than straight rush. All it takes is for him or Achane to hit a big play to force the defense to play honest. This is a chance for the offensive line to make a statement against a front that is not quite as formidable. 3. Caleb Douglas Is A Weapon The most important thing Douglas has brought to the Dolphins is his ability to get open . Much has been made about his size and speed since the draft. His stat line stood out and set franchise records. But what really stood out in week one was his ability to create separation. Douglas generated 5.3 yards of separation at the catch , despite having less cushion than other receivers. The Raiders tried to press him, and he still won. Of course, the Raiders secondary isn’t exactly loaded with premier talent. But for a rookie in his first game, and on the road, he stood out in a big way. He’ll have a much tougher test this week. The 49ers’ defensive back group, led by emerging star Renardo Green, is more talented than Las Vegas’s. Now that word is out on Douglas, he will get far more attention. But nothing suggests Douglas will fail to succeed this week. He is quickly becoming a go-to weapon and potentially a star. Three Areas of Concern 1. The 49ers Are Also Strong Up Front The Rams gained 122 yards on the ground, which is nice. But the 49ers gained 174 yards on the ground. And did so with only 1 more attempt than the Rams. They leaned heavily on both CMC and rookie Kaelon Black, with CMC going 10-68 and Black going 14-65. Deebo Samuel got in on the act with a 12-yard carry. The Niners did not record a single negative run play . This is a frightening idea, as the Dolphins were just pantsed by Ashton Jeanty and the Raiders, who, while talented, only had a 3.7 YPC average last season and an offensive line as maligned as the Dolphins’. The Dolphins will need to tighten up SIGNIFICANTLY if they want to have any hope of containing the 49ers rushing attack. The Niners’ passing game wasn’t necessarily special. Purdy went 25-for-34 for 205 yards. That’s a YPA of 6.1, which is meh. But he also threw 3 TDs. He was also not under any pressure whatsoever, despite the Rams having added the reigning defensive player of the year in Myles Garrett. Garrett is now on IR, but he played 40 snaps and generated 1 pressure. As a team, the Rams generated three total pressures. Miami generated 4 pressures last week. Granted, the Dolphins didn’t earn the right to rush the passer, and Cousins got the ball out quickly. Purdy also had time to throw quickly. Regardless, the Dolphins failed the test against a Raider front and now face a much better offensive line. 2. Kyle Shanahan Is A Madman If you read my most recent article at Aqua And Orange Review , I highlighted some offensive personnel and defensive package tendencies from the first week of action. The Niners defense was mostly base 4-3 until they got a big enough lead to force LA to throw more. Miami was heavily 11-personnel, which may have been due to their situation. The flip side to this is that Kyle Shanahan does not stick to any one personnel grouping exclusively. I’ll let you read the AOR article for that, but his ability to use a variety of groupings for any play call will keep Miami’s young and inexperienced defense on their heels. Jeff Hafley has his tendencies too, but whether he can go toe-to-toe with Shanahan is a big question, especially with this group. They have worked together, so they know each other well. It may come down to the talent more than the Xs & Os. I think Hafley will have some answers, but this defense hasn’t seen the funkShanahan is about to throw at them. 3. Miami’s Linebackers Are Good; San Francisco’s Linebackers Are Better I thought about discussing the plethora of playmakers at the 49ers’ disposal and how it will be a “pick your poison” situation for the defense. I thought about discussing some of Brock Purdy’s playmaking skills. But those are obvious choices that everyone discusses. I want to look at another position group: the linebackers. Jordyn Brooks is an All-Pro, and Jacob Rodriguez looked good in his first action for the Dolphins. But the 49ers have the best LB in the game with Fred Warner and a solid running mate in Dre Greenlaw. They will close the middle of the field for the Dolphins. They will allow the 49ers to call coverages that some teams could not call due to LB limitations. This will force the Dolphins to call plays that avoid where Warner and Greenlaw are camping out. Even if they are out of position or away from the play, they have the range to get in on the action. This also affects the run game and the intermediate passing game. Slowik will have to get…

full_text: LAS VEGAS, NV - SEPTEMBER 13: Miami Dolphins linebacker Chop Robinson (44) walks off of the field after a NFL regular season game between the Las Vegas Raiders and Miami Dolphins at Allegiant Stadium, Sunday September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, NV. (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins’ Week 2 injury report is a little more impactful than the report they had heading into last week’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders when everyone finished the practice week available for the game. This week, as the Dolphins prepare to face the San Francisco 49ers, Miami may find themselves without key players. Linebacker Ronnie Harrison, who played nearly half of Miami’s special teams snaps against the Raiders, remained sidelined at Thursday’s practice after missing Wednesday’s workout as well. He is dealing with a hamstring injury. Edge rusher Chop Robinson was also out of Thursday practice as he deals with a concussion. He was a limited participant on Wednesday, marking a downgrade in his status and bringing his availability for Sunday into question. Long snapper Tucker Addington, who sustained a shoulder injury against the Raiders, and rookie tight end Seydou Traore, dealing with thumb and Achilles injuries, were both limited in Thursday’s practice. That matched their participation status from Wednesday. Safety Dante Trader, Jr., and quarterback Malik Willis were both listed on the injury report but participated fully in practice on Wednesday and Thursday. Trader is dealing with a hamstring issue, while Willis has a toe problem. The 49ers’ side of the injury report included kicker Eddy Pineiro and wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling missing practice Thursday. They both also did not workout on Wednesday. Pineiro has an illness while Stribling has an ankle injury. Running back Kaelon Black, defensive end Nick Bosa, fullback Kyle Juszczyk, tight end George Kittle, and defensive end Keion White were all limited on Thursday. Black was added to the injury report with a groin issue. Bosa returned to practice after a rest day on Wednesday, but is also dealing with a knee injury. Juszczyk has a finger issue, while Kittle has an Achilles injury and White has a back issue; all three were also limited on Wednesday. San Francisco listed linebacker Dre Greenlaw, defensive end Khalid Kareem, running back Christian McCaffrey, cornerback Upton Stout, and tackle Trent Williams as full participants at Thursday’s practice. Greenlaw, McCaffrey, and Williams all returned from a rest day on Wednesday; Greenlaw is also dealing with an Achilles issue. Kareem is an upgrade from being limited on Wednesday as he works through a shoulder injury while Stout remained a full participant despite an Achilles issue. Both teams will update their injury reports on Friday, providing a game status designation. The biggest question for Miami will be the availability of Robinson, who is the top edge rusher on the Dolphins’ depth chart.

Hafley, who is in his first season as Miami’s coach, reiterated he’s committed to fixing that on Wednesday. “We’ve played one game. I want to run the football,” Hafley said moments before holding a west coast-based practice in Napa Valley. “We have to run the football! That’s all there is to it.” But is it really that easy? Based on the four seasons Hafley spent coaching Boston College, there’s little reason to doubt his commitment. You can listen to the show in the embedded player below, or you can check out the Bears Talk Underground page on the Bleav Network. Larry and I talked about how each of our teams fared in Week 1, including how much fun it is listening to Green Bay fans melt down about officiating, and we look at some of the keys to victory for both of our teams for this Sunday’s contest in Chicago. I’m pretty sure I’ve been talking to Larry more regularly than I’ve been talking to any other podcast out there. . .over a decade, if memory serves me correctly. It’s always a good time talking to him when our teams get together, particularly when they get together in Chicago, where weird things seem to have a tendency to happen. We won’t get a chance to talk again until Week 18, since the NFL has decided to rekindle what had been a tradition for a number of years by bringing the Bears to the Twin Cities to finish out the regular season. Minnesota Vikings Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Jordan Mason RB Thumb DNP DNP DNP IR-OUT Blake Cashman* LB Wrist LP FP FP — Jauan Jennings WR NIR DNP DNP DNP NIR-OUT Kyler Murray* QB Concussion LP LP LP Concussion- OUT Andrew Van Ginkel* OLB Chest LP LP FP — Brian O’Neill* RT Knee LP DNP LP QUESTIONABLE Harrison Smith* S NIR-REST — — LP — Christian Darrisaw * LT NIR-REST — — LP — Chicago Bears Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Coby Bryant* S Knee DNP DNP DNP IR-OUT Neville Gallimore DT Illness DNP FP FP — Grady Jarrett* DT NIR-Rest DNP FP FP — Darnell Wright* RT Knee DNP LP FP — Kyle Monangai RB Hamstring LP LP FP — Malik Mohammad* DB Ankle LP LP FP — Dayo Odeyingbo* DE Shoulder LP LP FP — D’Andre Swift* RB Ankle/Knee LP LP FP — Ozzy Trapilo* LT Knee LP LP FP — Xavier Woods DB Groin LP LP FP — Joe Thuney* LG NIR-Rest — DNP FP — Injury Report Terms and Glossary FP = Full participant in practice. LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. NIR = Not injury related. PUP = Physically unable to participate list. IR = Injured reserve. Note: only starters on IR are listed. Player Name* = Starter. Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. Notes on Injured Players For the Bears, despite a longer list of players that were limited this week in practice, everyone was a full participant in practice on Friday and they have no players with injury designations for the game on Sunday. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray apparently did not clear the concussion protocol in time to start on Sunday, or maybe he might have but the Vikings are holding him out in abundance of caution, with Kevin O’Connell saying he expects Murray to clear the protocol early next week, suggesting he’ll be the starter week three at Tampa Bay. Carson Wentz will start against the Bears and J.J. McCarthy will be the backup with Murray out on Sunday. Jauan Jennings has missed practice all week due to a family matter and will miss the game on Sunday as well because of it. Brian O’Neill was back in practice on Friday, but limited, and is the only Viking besides Murray and Jennings to have an injury designation for the game as questionable. My guess is he’ll start.
